proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, privacy-preserving agent workflows, sensitive data controls, and runtime security guardrails across agent architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with developing pre-competitive security standards, threat models, and privacy-preserving execution patterns for autonomous agent ecosystems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Operating as an intersecting architectural layer across the foundation, the working group collaborates across technical committees and groups to ensure consistent guardrails, secrets isolation, and blast radius reduction in agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Scope and Boundary Governance
The working group formalizes its technical scope through defined domain boundaries and cross-working-group handoffs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]:

- **Core Security Controls**: Technical priorities include prompt injection mitigation, capability-based agent authorization, hooks and checkpointing specifications, auditability and forensic traceability, memory layer protection, and blast radius limitation for rogue agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Privacy and Sensitive Data**: Scope encompasses PII obfuscation, secrets management across operational credentials and proprietary model data, and privacy-preserving workflows utilizing trusted execution environments (TEEs), encrypted vector databases, and zero-knowledge verification[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Commerce Security Guardrails**: Agentic commerce topics are restricted specifically to security controls—preventing fund draining, account token leakage, and unauthorized transaction delegation—while protocol-level commerce patterns are coordinated with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Boundary Delegations**: Value judgments, algorithmic bias, and ethical frameworks are deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]. Benchmarking for general [hallucination](../taxonomy/hallucination.md) is aligned with the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), with this group focusing on non-malicious derailment and operational sabotage[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]. Identity and delegation primitives are cross-coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].

# Leadership and Operations
- **Chair**: Alex Frazer was elected working group chair during the initial charter formation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Cadence**: Bi-weekly technical meetings with collaboration managed via Discord, GitHub, and shared document repositories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Deliverables**: Near-term milestones include the working group charter submission to the governing board, an internal security taxonomy to seed foundation-wide definitions, and reference security guidance for agent runtime environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing compliance frameworks, gap analyses, and governance guidance across global AI regulations and risk controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative tasked with evaluating regulatory landscapes, cataloging risk management frameworks, and developing standardized guidance for compliant agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. Operating under Linux Foundation antitrust and pre-competitive collaboration principles, the group conducts biweekly meetings to map regional and international requirements to technical agent controls [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

The group operates under the technical oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and interfaces with peer groups including the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) and [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Three-Step Working Model
The group executes its technical agenda through a phased deliverable cycle [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. **Landscape Analysis**: Reviewing and inventorying existing regulatory frameworks, industry standards, and enterprise use cases [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. Focus benchmarks include the EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, GDPR/PII constraints, and national regulatory co-creation models (such as Singapore regulatory initiatives) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis**: Identifying areas where current regulatory and risk frameworks fail to address emerging autonomous capabilities, non-deterministic execution paths, and cross-boundary agent interactions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Producing practical, pre-competitive recommendations, risk assessment protocols, and governance guardrails for production agentic deployments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

## Operational Recordkeeping
The working group standardizes operational reporting across all sessions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732]:
- **Meeting Notes Structure**: Meeting summaries, decisions, deliverables, and assigned action item tables are formatted using standard machine- and agent-readable templates [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].
- **Artifact Archiving**: Every biweekly record cross-references verified meeting transcripts, AI summaries, and video recordings in a reverse-chronological repository index [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-19**: Inaugural working group kickoff covering antitrust governance, chair nomination procedures, charter roadmap, and initial EU AI Act / eIDAS 2 regulatory scoping [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **2026-03-05**: Formally adopted the three-step deliverable model (landscape analysis, gap analysis, distilled guidance) and initiated the shared regulatory submissions backlog [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for evaluating project proposals, managing working groups, and enforcing the Project Lifecycle Policy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), operating under the AAIF Governing Board (GB) within The Linux Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Formally adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC Charter establishes the committee's authority to review technical project proposals, recommend project admissions to the Governing Board, and implement and maintain the foundation's Project Lifecycle Policy[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification
## Composition and Leadership
Each Platinum Member of the AAIF may appoint one representative to the Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. The TC elects an annual Chair and optional Co-Chair to preside over meetings until resignation or replacement[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Operational Responsibilities
Under Section 2 of its Charter, the TC is tasked with:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving Working Groups such as [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Coordinating collaboration between Technical Projects, defining community technical priorities, and advancing shared technical vision[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Evaluating incoming proposals and recommending project acceptance to the Governing Board in accordance with the [project proposal process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Applying and maintaining the [project lifecycle policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), including voting on stage transitions across Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus tiers[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending resource priorities to the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Voting Rules and Lazy Consensus
Decisions aim for consensus, but formal decisions operate on a one-vote-per-voting-member model[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- **Quorum**: Requires at least 50% of voting members present to execute binding votes during meetings[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Lazy Consensus**: Approvals may proceed under a 72-hour silence-as-agreement mechanism. Any formal objection forces an electronic vote requiring a majority vote of all voting TC members[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Deadlock Escalation**: Unresolved votes can be escalated to the Governing Board for resolution assistance[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Charter Amendments**: Requires approval by a two-thirds majority of the TC and subsequent GB approval[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History
The formal charter of the Technical Committee was adopted on March 3, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security taxonomy, and architectural design patterns for trustworthy agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical initiative focused on establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. Formally adopting its mission in March 2026, the group produces open threat models, taxonomy definitions, and architectural design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to implement shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Architecture / Specification
## Mission and Purpose
The group adopted its mission statement on March 31, 2026: *"The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem. Producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI."*[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

## Core Deliverables
The working group's initial deliverable roadmap focuses on five core assets[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]:
1. **Security and Privacy Taxonomy**: Standardized terms and definitions for agentic threats, boundaries, and safety mechanisms, maintained as a living document[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
2. **Agentic AI Threat Model Framework**: Threat modeling guidance and attack surface analysis covering prompt injection resistance, social engineering, and agent execution boundaries without overly prescriptive or brittle controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Reusable architectural patterns addressing skills isolation, audit logging, MCP tool execution guardrails, and boundary controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
4. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical baseline controls for builders across data minimization, secure memory, and runtime monitoring[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
5. **Cross-Workgroup Security & Privacy Review Checklist**: Verification checklists allowing peer working groups to assess security and privacy requirements in their deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].

## Inter-Group Coordination Boundaries
The SP-WG maintains coordination boundaries to prevent duplicative specification work[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]:
- **Identity and Trust**: Defers identity issuance and delegation mechanisms to [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), while SP-WG provides security requirements for logging, bounding, and auditing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Observability and Traceability**: Coordinates with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on behavioral anomalies, audit logging, and runtime monitoring[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **Agentic Commerce**: Coordinates with [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) on payment security and transaction guardrails[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Governance and Regulatory**: Focuses on technical privacy engineering controls (data minimization, isolation, secure memory) rather than legal interpretation, aligning regulatory posture with [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-17**: Junjie Bu (Google) introduced as co-chair alongside Alex Frazer; deliverable structure and cross-WG review concepts introduced[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **2026-03-31**: Formal mission statement adopted; "skills" incorporated into security architecture scope[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group aligning ecosystem telemetry, addressing agent-level tracing gaps, and standardizing multi-turn execution observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body led by primary contact Pavan Sudheendra[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. The group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding of agent observability, giving practitioners visibility into what AI agents do, how they execute, and their operational impact across debugging, evaluation, safety, and accountability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Architecture / Specification
## Non-Standards-Body Coordination Mandate
The OT-WG explicitly does not position itself as an isolated standards body competing with established specifications such as the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, or W3C Trace Context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Instead, it operates as a coordination forum intended to resolve ecosystem fragmentation, prevent vendor lock-in across proprietary trace formats, and contribute upstream to existing standards organizations whenever possible[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

## Guiding Principles
The OT-WG operates under six core principles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
- **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary**: New specifications are developed solely when an identified gap is not addressed by external bodies, with an emphasis on upstreaming solutions.
- **Interoperability over innovation**: Prioritize extending existing schemas and conventions over novel isolated specifications.
- **Observable by default**: Require agentic architectures to expose telemetry natively.
- **Move at the speed of the ecosystem**: Target iterative, incremental deliverables rather than delayed comprehensive specifications.
- **Adoption is key**: Value practical, implementable standards over theoretical abstractions.
- **Vendor and framework neutrality**: Avoid giving commercial advantages to any single platform or runtime.

## Core Focus Areas
The working group addresses structural gaps in existing telemetry models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
- **Session and Workflow Observability**: Moving beyond individual LLM request tracing (as covered by OpenInference or OTel GenAI conventions) to model multi-turn sessions, subagent spawning, and tool invocations across runtime boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: The founding focus area establishing standardized behavioral tracing across turn boundaries, causal links, and execution context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Multi-Modal Lineage**: Tracing content lineage, fidelity, and grounding across multi-modal transformation boundaries in complex workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-13**: Working group charter draft updated establishing foundational scope, coordination-first mandate, and founding focus areas under chair Pavan Sudheendra[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security taxonomy, architectural design patterns, and cross-group review checklists for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to standardize threat models, operational guardrails, and architectural patterns for autonomous and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group provides guidance across agent containment, identity, delegation, secrets management, and privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's scope covers five core functional areas and five approved initial deliverables for its initial 3–6 month horizon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

- **Taxonomy**: A living reference document defining shared security and privacy terms that feed into the broader AAIF taxonomy.
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: A research initiative assessing whether existing industry threat frameworks adequately cover agentic systems or if a novel framework is required, evaluating multi-agent trust boundaries, memory store isolation, and emergent attack vectors in self-modifying networks.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A builder-focused catalog of technical patterns detailing human-in-the-loop gates, execution hooks and extensibility, logical and semantic constraints, and privacy-preserving sandboxing.
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical operational guidance covering topics such as credentials elimination, secrets management, and secure tool invocation, complementing [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An assessment checklist and formal review model inspired by IETF standards practices, helping other AAIF working groups identify security and privacy implications early in their specification lifecycle.

Additionally, the working group monitors external technical developments, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors proposal for standardized security hooks, MCP Apps identity verification, and Linux Foundation Project Glasswing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-04-14, the working group unanimously approved its charter, operational scope, and the five initial deliverables via formal vote [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. The approved charter and deliverable portfolio were scheduled for presentation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) during the week of 2026-04-20 prior to formal team assignments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive visual catalog and ecosystem map tracking open-source software and open standards projects across the agentic AI domain.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive visualization and structured catalog of open-source software, foundation models, developer tooling, and open standards spanning the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1] Operated under the auspices of the Agentic AI Foundation and aligned with the domain taxonomies curated by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape highlights prominent open technologies and community projects powering autonomous agent workflows.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

# Architecture / Specification

The catalog is generated via the open-source `cncf/landscape2` compiler engine, which ingests declarative configuration definitions to build static web interfaces and interactive radar visualizations.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

Key architectural components in the landscape source repository include:
- `landscape.yml`: The central registry file organizing projects in alphabetical order under defined category hierarchies and holding optional extended schema metadata fields.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- `hosted_logos/`: Local vector asset repository storing SVG-format project and corporate logos, required to use non-reversed backgrounds and stacked vertical variants.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- Daily Build Pipeline: Automated continuous integration pipelines regenerate the deployed landscape view on a 24-hour cycle following merged pull requests.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

# Submission and Evaluation Criteria

To ensure quality and vendor neutrality, entries submitted to the landscape must satisfy explicit inclusion standards:[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Open Source Popularity Threshold**: Projects must be open source with at least 1,000 GitHub stars and fit cleanly into an established category.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Single-Category Representation**: Organizations and projects are restricted to a single primary category box representing their primary offering, with rare exceptions reserved for large multi-domain enterprises.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Exclusion of Proprietary Software**: Closed-source products, commercial distributions of open-source software, proprietary standards, and proprietary wrappers around open tools are disqualified from inclusion.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Entity Attribution**: Organizational ownership must map to the legal entity or trademark owner managing the software codebase.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill packaging AAIF visual, typographic, copy tone, and governance standards for automated asset and document generation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-brand-guidelines` skill is a modular instruction package that applies Agentic AI Foundation visual, copy, and governance standards to automated agent workflows.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b] Packaged according to the open [agent skills standard](../standards/agent-skills.md), the skill instructs agents on formatting presentations, documentation, web designs, social graphics, and marketing materials without diluting foundation neutrality.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]

Hosted within the AAIF [public agent skills catalog](../resources/public-agent-skills.md), the skill is structured for runtime discovery and dynamic loading by general-purpose agent runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

# Architecture / Specification

### Packaging and Metadata

The skill resides in `skills/aaif-brand-guidelines/SKILL.md` within the `aaif/public-agents` repository and is authored by Angie Jones.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b] Frontmatter metadata identifies the package:

- `name`: `aaif-brand-guidelines`
- `organization`: `AAIF`
- `version`: `1.0`

### Core Brand Tenets

The skill enforces three foundational pillars aligning with the core [brand guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md):[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]

1. **Neutrality**: Ensures generated designs and copy avoid implying ownership or governance by any single vendor or platform. It instructs agents to prefer balanced layouts, open standards framing, and transparent language over promotional hype.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]
2. **Collaboration**: Directs content generation toward shared ecosystem initiatives, open standards, and cross-industry cooperation, deprecating hero-centric or siloed positioning.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]
3. **Trustworthiness**: Leverages Linux Foundation governance credibility through clean, high-contrast visual compositions, grounded claims, and strict typography rules.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]

### Style Rules and Execution Gates

- **Color Constraints**: Mandates a primary palette anchored by White (`#ffffff`) and Black (`#000000`) for high-contrast accessibility.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]
- **Copy Tone**: Requires direct, factual, and ecosystem-oriented phrasing, rejecting speculative claims or aggressive marketing tactics.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]
- **Distribution**: Distributable globally or on a per-project basis via the `skills` CLI using `npx skills add aaif/public-agents --skill aaif-brand-guidelines`.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

# References

- Skill Implementation: `skills/aaif-brand-guidelines/SKILL.md` in `aaif/public-agents` [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]
- Packaging Manifest: `skills/README.md` in `aaif/public-agents` [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]
- Ingestion Pull Request: PR#1 in `aaif/public-agents` [^evt-public-agents-pr-1]

# Overview

The AAIF Public Agent Skills repository (`aaif/public-agents`) hosts standardized, reusable agent capabilities packaged under the [Agent Skills standard](../standards/agent-skills.md).[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808] Each skill bundles procedural instructions, metadata, reference materials, and optional automation scripts into modular directories, enabling AI agents to dynamically retrieve specialized domain context on demand.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

The repository acts as an upstream reference catalog for vendor-neutral agent tooling, compatible with multi-turn agents including [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

# Architecture / Specification

### Directory Layout

Every published skill resides within its own subdirectory under `skills/` with a mandatory manifest:[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

```text
skills/
├── <skill-name>/
│   ├── SKILL.md
│   ├── assets/
│   ├── references/
│   └── scripts/
└── README.md
```

- `SKILL.md`: Root configuration comprising YAML frontmatter (name, description, author, organization, version) and markdown instructions.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808][^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]
- `assets/`: Static resources such as templates, logos, and diagrams.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]
- `references/`: Extended technical specifications and reference documentation.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]
- `scripts/`: Deterministic execution scripts and helper executables.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

### Package Management and CLI Distribution

Skills are distributed and managed locally using the `skills` CLI wrapper:[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

- **Discovery**: Listing available repository skills via `npx skills add aaif/public-agents --list`.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]
- **Installation**: Installing a single skill globally using `npx skills add aaif/public-agents --skill <skill-name> --global` or installing all repository skills via `--all`.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]
- **Lifecycle**: Updating installed local skills via `npx skills update <skill-name>`.[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]

### Catalog Modules

- [`skills/aaif-brand-guidelines`](../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md): Provides visual composition rules, copy tone standards, and Linux Foundation neutrality governance.[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b][^evt-public-agents-pr-1]

# References

- Repository Structure: `skills/README.md` in `aaif/public-agents` [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]
- Initial Skill Addition: Pull Request #1 in `aaif/public-agents` [^evt-public-agents-pr-1]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group advancing vendor-neutral specifications, reference architectures, and trust models for AI agent identity, authentication, delegation, and cross-boundary governance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical initiative focused on vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Led by Primary Contact Grant Miller, the group establishes models allowing autonomous agents to verify identity, establish provenance, prove authority delegation, and assert human consent constraints across organizational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

The working group coordinates with complementary technical efforts, including [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) for threat modeling and secure execution environments, and [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) for telemetry representation[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Core Domains
The Identity & Trust Working Group defines technical frameworks across five primary focus areas[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Mechanisms establishing how agents identify themselves, authenticate against external services, and convey lineage, operator identity, and host system context.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Models representing agent delegation from humans, teams, roles, or services, determining how far delegated authority extends and enforcing delegation depth.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained access policies, policy constraints, and formal representation of human approval gates.
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Verification protocols for evaluating whether an external agent is trusted to execute requested tasks across organizational boundaries.
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata**: Descriptors, catalog registrations, and discovery metadata carrying trust verification assertions.

## Boundary Definitions and Non-Goals
The group explicitly bounds its scope to avoid duplicating responsibilities of other initiatives[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Not a Standards Development Organization (SDO)**: Does not ratify formal standards independently, but submits recommendations to upstream SDOs.
- **Comprehensive Execution Security**: Assumes baseline host runtime security and leaves secure runtime containment to [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md).
- **Normative Responsible AI**: Avoids general ethical and regulatory policy frameworks, deferring broad compliance to [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).
- **Production Infrastructure**: Does not operate production identity infrastructure or run certification programs.

# Lifecycle History
- **Charter Drafted**: The working group charter was established outlining primary leadership under Grant Miller and formalizing in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation initiative establishing vendor-neutral security guidelines, threat modeling frameworks, and privacy architectures for agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Chaired by Alex Frazer, the group collaborates across AAIF technical initiatives to harden agent-to-agent interfaces, tool execution boundaries, and human approval controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

The working group interfaces closely with [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) on delegation boundaries, [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) on audit logs, and [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on shared foundational nomenclature[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-Working-Group Taxonomy Initiative
During all-hands chair alignment, the AAIF working groups designated taxonomy development as the first cross-WG shared deliverable to prevent divergence across working group silos[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The Security and Privacy WG draft taxonomy was selected as the foundational baseline for cross-initiative contributions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## External Protocol Security Tracking
The working group actively monitors emerging protocol extensions impacting trust boundaries:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors**: Protocol hooks enabling in-flight inspection, policy enforcement, and payload redaction across MCP client-server boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **MCP Apps**: User interface integration into the MCP ecosystem, breaking strict browser separation boundaries and requiring novel sandbox containment models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-28 All-Hands**: Alex Frazer reported the charter was presented to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), receiving four formal approvals and multiple verbal endorsements during a GitHub outage; the WG agreed to proceed operational work in parallel[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Leadership Transition**: Manik succeeded Matt as AAIF Chief Technology Officer, prompting meeting cadence adjustments to accommodate Sydney-based coordination[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Operating Model Evolution**: WG transitioned bi-weekly plenary meetings into brief checkpoint syncs, shifting substantive deliverable drafting into self-organized async workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Official intake workflows, qualification criteria, and Technical Committee review procedures for proposing and establishing new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal requirements and operating procedures for proposing a new working group within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. All working group proposals are managed through structured GitHub issue intake and submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for governance review and formal charter ratification[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

The intake workflow ensures that proposed groups have designated member sponsorship, unambiguous charter boundaries, and minimal overlap with active initiatives[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake Requirements and Qualification
Proposals are submitted via structured YAML issue templates in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. Incoming submissions are assigned to foundation management (such as Christina Harter) and require specific submitter credentials[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]:
- **Member Organization Affiliation**: The primary submitter must represent an active AAIF Member Organization[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Membership Tier Disclosure**: Submitters must disclose whether their sponsoring organization holds Platinum or Gold membership status within the foundation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Required Metadata**: Submissions must document full submitter contact information, professional title, proposed working group title, scope justification, and prior art references[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c][^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].

## Proposal Lifecycle and Review Window
Proposals move through clear lifecycle checkpoints before formal charter drafting:
1. **Intake and Triage**: New issues receive the `New` label upon creation and undergo schema validation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
2. **Review Window**: While the TC accepts proposal submissions continuously, formal reviews for prospective groups are scheduled to commence on June 1, 2026[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
3. **TC Evaluation**: The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) evaluates alignment against foundation goals, dependency overlaps, and member participation commitments.

# Lifecycle History
- **Template Standardization**: Issue template cleanup resolved duplicate metadata blocks and corrected field labeling between prior art resources and supporting attachment inputs[^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1][^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].
- **Intake Opening**: Issue intake activated with notification that formal TC evaluation sessions commence June 1, 2026[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Public Agent Resources and Skills
proposed_concept.description: Public repository packaging portable agent skills, repeatable recipes, prompt templates, and CI canary workflows for foundation automation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Public Agents repository (`aaif/public-agents`) provides reusable, modular assets designed for autonomous and semi-autonomous agent execution across foundation workflows[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]. The repository organizes functional extensions into distinct operational tiers, including installable agent skills, repeatable task recipes, reusable prompt templates, and validation documentation[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

The repository adheres to [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) conventions and provides foundational automation for administrative triage and community management[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Repository Structure
The repository is partitioned into modular resource collections[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]:
- `skills/`: Agent skills encapsulating domain expertise, formatting rules, brand guidelines, and tool execution instructions.
- `recipes/`: Structured, multi-step agent workflows and repeatable task definitions.
- `prompts/`: Reusable prompt templates and instruction sets for specific LLM roles.
- `docs/`: Architectural specifications and contributor guidance.

## Inference Validation and Canary Actions
The repository maintains manually triggered GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/` to validate model connectivity and test LLM inference pipelines without third-party orchestrators[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]:
- **GitHub Models (`copilot-test-action`)**: Connects to GitHub Models (`https://models.github.ai`) using the standard built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` across organization-scoped chat completion endpoints (`/orgs/{org}/inference/chat/completions`), requiring no external secrets[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- **Google Gemini (`gemini-test-action`)**: Dispatches prompt workloads to Google Gemini endpoints (such as `gemini-2.5-flash` or `gemini-2.5-pro`) using secret headers (`x-goog-api-key`) scoped either to repository secrets or restricted deployment environments[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Lifecycle History
- **Repository Initialization**: Structured baseline directories for skills, recipes, and prompts, alongside GitHub Models and Gemini inference verification workflows[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Guidelines Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill assisting contributors in drafting, validating, and packaging vendor-neutral blog content for aaif.io intake.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill packages editorial rules, contributor eligibility criteria, neutrality constraints, and intake submission requirements for publishing articles on the Agentic AI Foundation blog [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]. It enables agents to evaluate draft proposals, enforce Linux Foundation neutrality standards, structure author metadata, and assemble compliant intake packages [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].

# Architecture / Specification

The skill structures the blog lifecycle into a multi-step agent workflow and verification pipeline [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]:

1. **Story and Timeliness Verification**: Confirms alignment with AAIF priorities—including updates on hosted projects (such as `../resources/goose.md`, MCP, or AGENTS.md), technical tutorials, case studies, or working group developments—ensuring announcements fall within a recent window (typically within two months) [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
2. **Contributor Eligibility Check**: Validates the submitting entity (member company, project maintainer, working group member, Technical Committee, or community contributor, the latter capped at two submissions monthly) [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].
3. **Neutrality and Policy Enforcement**: Strips marketing rhetoric, commercial exclusivity claims, or ungrounded superiority statements; checks that member organization submissions confine corporate references to at most two closing sentences and a single link [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. It also prevents criticism or discouragement of any open-source technology [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].
4. **Package Assembly**: Validates author biographies, headshots/logos, suggested titles, social amplification copy, and target dates against the official intake form before handoff to the Linux Foundation editorial team [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Lifecycle History

The skill was established in `aaif/public-agents` by author Angie Jones as version 1.0, codifying the narrative guidelines published in `aaif/foundation` [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# References

- Skill specification: [aaif/public-agents](https://github.com/aaif/public-agents/blob/fcc3ebc4db293e01305373fc9c2f2c46845ee015/skills/aaif-blog-guidelines/SKILL.md) [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
- Editorial guidelines: `../guidelines/blog-guidelines.md` [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]

proposed_concept.title: Blog Guidelines and Intake Process
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, contributor eligibility rules, and intake submission workflows for the Agentic AI Foundation blog on aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) blog guidelines define the editorial standards, eligibility criteria, and submission workflow for content published on aaif.io [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Managed by the Linux Foundation team, the blog acts as an educational and technical publication platform highlighting open-source agent projects, technical tutorials, and production deployments [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

### Contributor Eligibility and Quotas
- **Member Companies**: Permitted to publish vendor-neutral insights; permitted up to two closing sentences and one external link (e.g., career opportunities or project repositories) [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Project Maintainers & Contributors**: Focus on hosted projects such as MCP, `../resources/goose.md`, and AGENTS.md, detailing releases and architecture [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Working Groups & Technical Committee**: Technical reports and milestones authored on behalf of Foundation bodies like `../governance/technical-committee.md` [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Community Contributors**: May submit up to two technical posts per calendar month [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

### Editorial Constraints
- **Vendor Neutrality**: Content must avoid sales jargon, sponsored placement framing, or disparaging competing open-source projects [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Timeliness and Readiness**: Submissions must represent original, finalized material reflecting developments from the preceding two months and require internal stakeholder approval before intake [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **SLA**: Authors must provide at least a two-week lead time prior to desired publishing dates to accommodate Linux Foundation review and scheduling [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

### Automated Assistance
Contributors can automate formatting and guideline compliance checks via the `../skills/aaif-blog-guidelines.md` agent skill distributed via `../resources/public-agent-skills.md` [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# References

- Policy source: [aaif/foundation/policies-guidelines/blog-guidelines.md](https://github.com/aaif/foundation/blob/8df4e5b4087f2dcd5fbc77b702f68b1fc7418693/policies-guidelines/blog-guidelines.md) [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group aligning ecosystem telemetry, addressing agent-level tracing gaps, and standardizing multi-modal agent behavior trace models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to build a shared understanding of agent observability across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Ratified in April 2026 and approved in May 2026 under the leadership of primary contact Pavan Sudheendra, the group addresses the fragmented agent observability space and bridges the gap between individual LLM call instrumentation and multi-turn, multi-modal workflow execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification

### Guiding Principles and Mandate
- **Coordination Forum over New Standards Body**: The group is explicitly structured as an alignment and coordination vehicle rather than a competing specification developer [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. It prioritizes contributing upstream to existing efforts, including the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG (`../resources/opentelemetry.md`), OWASP AOS, and the W3C Trace Context working group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Coordinate First, Specify Only When Necessary**: New specifications or schema profiles are generated only when rigorous gap analyses identify unaddressed operational requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Observable by Default**: Systems should natively expose state transitions, tool invocations, and semantic boundaries out of the box [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

### Focus Areas and Scope
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Founding focus area advancing session- and workflow-level instrumentation standards beyond single LLM spans (`../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Multi-Modal Lineage & Grounding**: Developing telemetry representations that capture content fidelity and provenance across cross-modal agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry**: Harmonizing trace context handoffs across tool boundaries (`../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md` and `../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-15**: Charter ratified by the working group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **2026-05-13**: Charter formally approved by foundation governance [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# References

- Working Group Charter: [aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/charter/CHARTER.md](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/blob/ecdd24bcbb59140ce89b608a8ddf815a38140a2b/charter/CHARTER.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Proposal Process governs the formal intake, technical evaluation, and stage admission for open-source projects joining the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Operating under the oversight of the `../governance/technical-committee.md`, the process provides a transparent, structured pathway for candidate projects to submit metadata, demonstrate compliance with foundation criteria, and enter lifecycle stages defined by the `../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md` [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification

### Submission Form and Requirements
Project submissions are managed via structured issue templates in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Intake requirements distinguish between mandatory structural inputs and optional maturity indicators:

- **Mandatory Disclosures**: Core project identity, licenses, maintainer governance models, and architectural fit within the agentic ecosystem [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].
- **Optional Fields**: In alignment with the underlying project lifecycle policy, items such as a published public roadmap and an OpenSSF Best Practices badge are explicitly optional at initial intake [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Projects entering Sandbox are not blocked by the absence of these badges or forward roadmaps during intake triage [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Lifecycle History

- Form specifications in PR #23 adjusted field validation to prevent premature rejection of Sandbox candidates missing optional maturity criteria [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# References

- Issue Template Refactoring: [aaif/project-proposals/pull/23](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/pull/23) [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]
- Foundation Project Lifecycle: `../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md` [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, agent containment architectures, cross-WG review checklists, and privacy controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA, also referenced as S&P) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to build security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. The group produces open threat models, agent containment architectures, cross-working group review checklists, and reusable design patterns that AI developers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to mitigate multi-agent vulnerabilities, prompt injection, tool invocation risks, and unauthorized boundary traversals[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Boundary Controls
The working group operates under explicit scope boundaries defined in its charter[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]:

- **In Scope**:
  - Threat modeling and attack analysis (including prompt injection, confused deputy, agent memory corruption, and cascading failures)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
  - Security architecture and reusable design patterns covering agent containment, execution sandboxing, and policy enforcement[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
  - Tool and hook security, including standardizing execution hooks across agent runtimes and protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
  - Data protection, least privilege, and privacy controls across multi-agent delegation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
  - Cross-working group security and privacy review checklists[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

- **Out of Scope**:
  - Value judgments, bias assessments, and philosophical AI ethics (deferred to [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
  - Prescribing or interpreting statutory regulatory compliance regimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
  - Commercial certification or compliance audits of third-party agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group organizes execution across sequenced deliverables managed in dedicated workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]:

1. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: The primary near-term technical baseline evaluating agent attack surfaces and vulnerability taxonomies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
2. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An early-stage review rubric designed to assist peer AAIF working group chairs in evaluating security and privacy implications during deliverable drafting[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Implementation guidance and anti-patterns specifying architectural patterns such as execution hooks, approval gates, and containment boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
4. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Advisory documentation detailing baseline operational hygiene and implementation principles (aligned with [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
5. **Taxonomy Alignment**: While initially planned within the working group, security taxonomy efforts have been transitioned into an AAIF-wide horizontal initiative under [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), with working group members contributing domain-specific definitions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

## Governance and Operations
The working group is led by Chair Alex Frazer and Co-Chair Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. Governance follows consensus decision-making with simple-majority voting fallbacks (51% quorum) and escalates unresolved disputes to the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The group conducts bi-weekly plenary meetings alongside async coordination through dedicated Discord channels and collaborates externally with adjacent efforts including the MCP Access Control Services (ACS) hooks initiative and the AARM standard[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-29**: Initial draft charter established under PR #1 defining the mission, scope boundaries, and core deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **2026-05-12**: Working group transitioned charter formalization to the LFX platform, organized workstream leadership, and coordinated taxonomy integration with the AAIF cross-WG taxonomy initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **2026-05-13**: Charter formal approval recorded in charter documentation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and ecosystem architecture map visualizing agent runtimes, protocols, guardrails, and project tiers using CNCF Landscape2.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape (AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map) is an interactive visualization and classification directory tracking open-source agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability frameworks, and commerce rails across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007] Developed in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the map categorizes community and industry initiatives into structured functional domains.

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape platform is constructed on the CNCF Landscape2 engine and deployed as a Next.js static export.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]

## Configuration and Presentation

Landscape appearance, metadata, and asset sources are configured via `settings.yml`:
- **Base Path**: Configured for static export sub-routes (`/ws-taxonomy-landscape/landscape`) on GitHub Pages.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]
- **UI Theme**: Applies an AAIF-branded color palette featuring Slate 900 (`#0f172a`), Slate 800 (`#1e293b`), and Blue 500 (`#3b82f6`).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]
- **Display Modes**: Default card grid layout displaying logos and brief capability descriptions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]

## Project Tiers

The architecture map categorizes technologies into four standardized project tiers to communicate governance maturity and affiliation:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]
- **Graduated**: Stable open-source technologies meeting rigorous adoption, production governance, and contributor diversity standards.
- **Incubating**: Active projects maturing under foundation governance while completing technical and security criteria.
- **Member**: Projects and commercial technologies maintained or sponsored by AAIF member organizations.
- **External**: Relevant third-party frameworks, specifications, and ecosystem tools operating in the broader agentic landscape.

## Automated Pull Request Preview CI

Pull requests modifying `landscape.yml`, `settings.yml`, or hosted asset directories trigger a GitHub Actions preview workflow.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00] The workflow calculates overlay URL query parameters against the `aaif.landscape2.io` preview service and comments on the pull request with a live interactive preview link, enabling automated visual and structural review before changes are merged.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining technical project admission requirements, lifecycle stages, and the annual review process.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy establishes the governance rules and criteria for technical projects joining the foundation and progressing across operational stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. It governs both existing open-source projects transitioning into the foundation and new technical initiatives incubated directly within the AAIF [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Requirements
Projects apply for foundation admission via the public project proposals repository [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Every formal submission must document:
- Project identity, mission alignment, adoption evidence, and relationship to existing AAIF efforts [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- An identified [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) sponsor, if available to mentor the project [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- OSI-approved permissive licensing and cataloged external dependency licenses [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Public repositories, release engineering mechanics, automated validation pipelines, and accessible issue tracking [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Documented governance practices, maintainer rosters, decision-making workflows, and official communication channels [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

## Project Stages
The policy defines three formal stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- **Growth Stage**: Active projects demonstrating foundational utility, community adoption, and technical momentum [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Impact Stage**: Mature, production-grade projects demonstrating substantial industry adoption, sustainable contributor diversity, and cross-ecosystem alignment [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Emeritus Stage**: Projects that are no longer actively maintained or have completed their operational mission, retaining archival status within the foundation [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171], [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Annual Review
All active projects participate in an annual evaluation by the foundation to evaluate progress, verify health metrics, and execute stage transitions [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
Adopted with an effective date of March 18, 2026, establishing formal stage progressions and proposal evaluation mechanics [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Subsequent maintenance resolved typographical errors across the policy and proposal issue templates [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.description: Intake criteria and submission requirements for Foundation members proposing new Agentic AI Foundation working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines govern how Agentic AI Foundation members submit formal proposals to launch new working groups [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working Groups operate as structured, time-bound collaborations of subject matter experts convened to address specific challenges, develop specifications, produce actionable guidance, and advance foundation priorities [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Submitter Eligibility
Working Group proposal submissions are restricted exclusively to accredited Foundation Members in good standing across any membership tier [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Submissions submitted by non-member entities are not reviewed [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Submission Requirements
Proposals submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) must supply structured documentation across eight core areas [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Name, organizational affiliation, role, contact email, leadership availability, and membership tier [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
2. **Working Group Identity**: Clear title and an accessible, jargon-free single-sentence summary of the group's focus [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Articulation of the specific agentic AI challenge, gap, or opportunity and strategic alignment with foundation objectives [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
4. **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Concrete technical outputs such as whitepapers, specifications, benchmarks, reference architectures, or regulatory guidance [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
5. **Timeline & Structure**: Operational cadence and charter duration, which typically spans a 12 to 24 month cycle [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
6. **Membership & Expertise**: Cross-industry skill profiles and confirmed commitments from interested organizations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
7. **Impact & Urgency**: Value proposition and urgency justifying formal foundation engagement [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
8. **Resource Considerations**: Necessary tooling, infrastructure, or community resources required to sustain group activities [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Lifecycle History
Formulated and released in March 2026 to standardize member-driven working group creation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and architectural ecosystem map cataloging open-source software, foundation member initiatives, and production tools across the agentic AI space [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]. It structures the agent runtime ecosystem, communication protocols, safety guardrails, and orchestration layers into standardized visual categories [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Organization and Watchlist
The landscape architecture establishes clear separation across member institutions and technical projects [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]:
- **Agentic AI Project Watchlist**: Tracks top open-source agentic projects and synchronizes with the Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard on [LFX Insights](https://insights.linuxfoundation.org/report/agentic-ai-momentum) [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Member and Project Decoupling**: Uses independent groupings to prevent member organization data from coupling with project entries, while highlighting member-sponsored open-source projects [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

## Automated Validation Pipeline
All landscape configuration changes are validated via GitHub Actions pull request workflows utilizing the `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` action [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]:
- **Data Validation**: Enforces schema correctness on `./landscape.yml` to verify project metadata, repository URLs, and subcategory classifications [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].
- **Settings Validation**: Validates `./settings.yml` to ensure layout configurations and visual presentation rules comply with CNCF Landscape2 specifications [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].

# Lifecycle History
Expanded in March 2026 to incorporate the OSS project watchlist, group decoupling for member projects, and CNCF landscape2 automated validation [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14], [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, interoperability patterns, and interfaces across agent-driven commerce lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group chartered to catalog, align, and harmonize open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Formally approved on 2026-05-15 under the leadership of co-chairs Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the working group serves as a neutral forum mapping emerging protocols across merchants, digital wallets, payment networks, and identity systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

The group maintains strict protocol neutrality and does not author competing commerce protocols; rather, it identifies common patterns across existing solutions and issues architectural recommendations to the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its technical activities around interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns connecting agentic platforms with the broader commerce ecosystem[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:

- **Discovery and Negotiation**: Agent-to-merchant interfaces standardizing structured offers, inventory availability, contractual terms, and fulfillment specifications.
- **Cart and Checkout**: Cart composition mechanisms, state validation, and checkout handoffs between agent runtimes and merchant platforms.
- **Identity and Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity verification, agent delegation scopes, and explicit consent signaling, developed in coordination with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Interoperability abstractions connecting agents, digital wallets, and payment networks across card rails, real-time banking, and on-chain rails, capturing intent, authorization, and settlement signals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Fraud Signaling**: Exchange of risk-posture and trust signals between agents, merchant endpoints, and risk-scoring systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Human-in-the-Loop and Autonomy Boundaries**: Standardized models for confirmation checkpoints, escalation workflows, and autonomy-level constraints aligned with [patterns/human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Post-Purchase Interfaces**: Telemetry and data payloads for claims, dispute initiation, chargeback handling, and tracking order lifecycle status.

### Explicit Non-Goals and Boundary Exclusions

To avoid duplicating domain-specific infrastructure or conflicting with Foundation-wide initiatives, the charter excludes[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
1. **Underlying System Internals**: Operational mechanics, routing engines, or clearing rules of payment rails, fraud engines, and identity providers.
2. **Authoring Competing Protocols**: The group catalogs and converges external protocols rather than designing replacement specifications.
3. **UI and Hardware**: Point-of-sale terminals, consumer UI hardware, and front-end marketplace visual presentation.
4. **General Policy**: Foundation-level responsible AI and societal-impact policies.

# Lifecycle History

Approved by the AAIF Technical Committee on 2026-05-15, the charter established an operating cadence focused on reference architectures, cross-ecosystem mappings, and interoperability guidance[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security best practice guides, design pattern catalogs, and cross-working group security review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish open threat models, agent containment architectures, security best practice guides, and security-review criteria across foundation initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Following formal approval of its working group charter in May 2026, the group organized active workstreams focused on practical security controls, runtime isolation patterns, and cross-working group governance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group coordinates four primary technical deliverables through self-selected contributor channels[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: A structured analysis adapting existing threat modeling frameworks to agentic behaviors, prompt injection vectors, tool authorization boundaries, and autonomous loop execution. This workstream operates in close alignment with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive guidance detailing operational controls across secrets elimination, in-loop policy enforcement, and credential isolation, expanding on [guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable architectural patterns codifying safe agent operations, sandboxing, and runtime governance.
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: An evaluation checklist ensuring horizontal security and data-privacy reviews across technical proposals and reference architectures.

# Lifecycle History

In its meeting on 2026-05-26, the working group announced formal charter ratification by AAIF leadership[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Due to earlier charter review timelines, active deliverable deadlines were shifted back by approximately one month. Operational governance adopted a self-selection model within workstream channels for leads and co-leads, alongside lightweight async contributions coordinated with foundation-wide tools[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
