proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Horizontal AAIF technical initiative governing cross-domain taxonomy curation, ecosystem landscape mapping, and category alignment across Foundation working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a horizontal Agentic AI Foundation technical initiative responsible for defining cross-domain taxonomies, terminology standards, and the authoritative AAIF landscape directory[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. The group provides a unified vocabulary and categorization schema connecting autonomous agent frameworks, protocols, security barriers, observability stacks, and governance policies across all AAIF working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

In May 2026, Junjie Bu was appointed co-chair of the cross-WG Taxonomy workstream and chair of the Landscape workstream, directing weekly synchronization and asynchronous pull-request-driven maintenance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group maintains the official ecosystem landscape schema, organizing tools and frameworks into seven core domain categories directly mapped to Foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:

1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Autonomous agent frameworks (e.g., Microsoft AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, Google ADK) and orchestration runtimes (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, Dapr, LangGraph), aligned with the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md).
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Inter-agent communication protocols and tool discovery systems, aligned with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Policy engines, proxy gateways, and containment frameworks, aligned with the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Tracing platforms, semantic conventions, and behavioral telemetry, aligned with the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Buyer delegation protocols, transaction orchestrators, and digital wallets, aligned with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Compliance tools, assurance trackers, and accountability frameworks, aligned with the [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Automated graders, canary pipelines, and benchmark test suites, aligned with the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md).

# Lifecycle History

Originally established to curb fragmented nomenclature across emergent agent frameworks, the working group transitioned in mid-2026 into a formal cross-working-group workstream model[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Operating primarily through GitHub pull requests and lightweight weekly 30-minute meetings, the initiative provides shared data schemas consumed by threat modeling, protocol standardization, and interoperability efforts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.description: Schema-validated catalog and interactive landscape mapping open-source and member agentic AI frameworks, protocols, and developer tooling across seven Foundation domains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and schema-validated catalog maintained by the Agentic AI Foundation to track open-source and member-driven projects across the agentic software ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. Governed under the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape models projects across autonomous runtimes, protocols, security boundaries, observability, and commerce[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification

The catalog is defined declaratively within `landscape.yml`, categorizing projects into seven major domains aligned directly with Foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:

- **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**:
  - *Autonomous Agent Frameworks*: Microsoft AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, Google Agent Development Kit (ADK).
  - *Orchestration Runtimes*: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Diagrid Dapr Runtimes, LangGraph.
- **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Standardized messaging schemas, agent-to-agent communication formats, and discovery gateways.
- **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Policy engines, proxy firewalls, and sandboxing environments enforcing runtime boundaries.
- **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Telemetry capture engines, semantic conventions, and tracing collectors across agent-tool interactions.
- **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Agent-mediated checkout, digital wallets, and payment delegation infrastructure aligned with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).
- **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Auditability frameworks, AI bill of materials tracking, and regulatory governance platforms.
- **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Repeatable evaluation harnesses, synthetic benchmarks, and performance testing frameworks.

Each entry records repository URLs, project membership status (`member` vs. `external`), primary website links, and SVG logo assets. Contributions follow standardized validation checks ensuring YAML diagnostic compliance and repository guideline verification[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Intake workflow, evaluation criteria, status labels, and Technical Committee approval rules for open-source projects applying to join the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The project proposal process outlines the official intake mechanism, review workflow, and governance criteria for external open-source projects applying to become foundation-hosted projects under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Projects apply through the public `aaif/project-proposals` repository to seek classification as either a Growth or Impact project under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

AAIF membership is decoupled from project contribution: submitting organizations do not need to be foundation members, and project acceptance conveys neither commercial membership tier nor a seat on the Governing Board[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Application and Triage Workflow
Prospective projects apply by submitting an issue template on `aaif/project-proposals`[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. The submission moves through the following stages:
1. **Application Intake**: The proposal issue is submitted, cataloged on the Foundation Project Proposals Board, and assigned the `New` label in the triage backlog[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
2. **Review Presentation**: Project maintainers prepare a technical presentation with AAIF staff assistance and are scheduled for a formal review session at an upcoming Technical Committee meeting[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
3. **Technical Committee Evaluation**: The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) reviews the project against admission requirements and determines suitability for Growth or Impact status[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Status Labels
Proposal tracking uses standardized issue labels throughout evaluation[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: The application has been logged and queued in the triage backlog.
- `Approved`: The application has satisfied TC review and been recommended for foundation hosting.
- `Declined`: The application has been rejected with explanatory TC feedback provided in the comments.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Supplemental technical, licensing, or governance information is requested from maintainers.
- `Too Early`: The project requires additional maturity, adoption, or community breadth before re-evaluation.

## Voting and Governance Rules
- **Approval Threshold**: Acceptance requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) across all voting members of the Technical Committee[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Governing Board Referral**: Following a positive TC vote, the proposal is referred to the AAIF Governing Board for final administrative and legal approval[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Reapplication Window**: Projects receiving a declined vote are permitted to reapply as soon as three months later, provided tangible technical progress has addressed prior reviewer feedback[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Overview

The working group collaborates cross-functionally across AAIF initiatives, providing specialized security review checklists and assigning delegates to horizontal workstreams including the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Leadership
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into specialized workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, formulating unified baseline audit criteria for AAIF projects and specifications.
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, maintaining actionable deployment and development guidance aligned with [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, standardizing threat vectors specific to agent autonomous tool use and delegation.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, documenting architectural mitigations including isolation and control gates.

## Cross-Working Group Integration
To ensure cross-cutting consistency across Foundation definitions, Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the working group's designated delegates to the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Technical updates are reported asynchronously to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on a monthly cadence through GitHub to avoid blocking workstream progress with bureaucratic approval gates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

Rather than functioning in isolation, the workstream operates as a horizontal effort requiring delegate representation from each domain-specific working group, including the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

- **Cross-Group Representation**: Each AAIF working group designates dedicated delegates who actively review proposals, reconcile domain-specific taxonomy conflicts, and align classification standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Open Contribution via Decoupled Data**: Contributions and modifications are open to the entire foundation community, maintained in decoupled structured repositories where changes are proposed and tracked asynchronously via GitHub pull requests[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

The working group delegates technical investigations into specialized focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:

Technical specifications and charters are authored through GitHub PR workflows, transitioning away from centralized documents to provide verifiable audit histories and concrete issue tracking for contributor onboarding[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing threat models, runtime defensive controls, security review checklists, and privacy guidelines across agentic AI systems. Repository governance and deliverable publication follow structured automation rules across charter, deliverables, and meeting documentation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its repository operations across three primary directories governed by localized agent instructions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]:
- `charter/`: Contains the foundational charter (`charter/DRAFT.md`), which remains in draft status until formally approved by a recorded working group decision[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- `deliverables/`: Houses formal output documents according to a strict three-state lifecycle[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:
  - `Draft`: Work in progress prefixed with `DRAFT-` (e.g., `DRAFT-threat-model-framework.md`)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
  - `Final`: Formally approved deliverable with the `DRAFT-` prefix removed. A deliverable cannot transition to Final without a corresponding meeting note in `meeting-notes/YYYY-MM-DD.md` explicitly recording the approval decision[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
  - `Moved`: Retained redirect files maintaining inbound links when deliverables transfer to external workstreams or repositories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- `meeting-notes/`: Chronological records named `YYYY-MM-DD.md` capturing links, discussion topics, explicit decisions, deliverables, and assigned action item owners[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31].

# Lifecycle History
The repository enforces CommonMark ATX headers, ISO-8601 dates, and deliverable status tracking in directory indices[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]. Proposed contributions from independent community participants include cross-referencing OWASP Agentic Systems Incidents (ASI) vectors, establishing pre-execution static analysis disciplines, and consumer messaging human-in-the-loop patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6].

# References
- [Repository Agent Guidelines](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/3a3d0ef5367e0beb6aafa56908ae277a73f133e0/AGENTS.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, reusable design patterns, security best practices, and cross-working-group review processes for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing threat models, curating reusable security design patterns, authoring operational best practices, and conducting horizontal security reviews across all AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. The working group operates as an intersecting security layer across the foundation to ensure agent autonomy, tool invocation, and multi-agent interactions adhere to rigorous security and privacy boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical program into four core workstreams alongside cross-working-group delegates:

## Threat Modeling
The Threat Modeling workstream conducts gap analyses against established frameworks such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF to determine where agentic-specific threat vectors—including multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation risks, delegated authorization boundaries, and prompt/model supply-chain integrity—require novel guidance or framework enhancements[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. The workstream is co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

## Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
The Design Patterns workstream curates reusable architectural patterns and anti-patterns for agent builders using a problem/context/solution/trade-offs format[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Key pattern areas encompass hooks and checkpointing (see [patterns/approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)), human-in-the-loop controls (see [patterns/human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)), privacy-preserving execution via trusted execution environments and zero-knowledge proofs (see [patterns/attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)), blast radius containment, secure memory lifecycle management, agent containment and runtime intervention (see [patterns/kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)), and agent authorization models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. It is co-led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

## Best Practices Guide
The Best Practices workstream synthesizes practical guidance and operational standards for practitioners, answering implementation questions across secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrail configuration, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. It is co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

## Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist
Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), this workstream operationalizes the SP WG's intersecting oversight function by defining a lightweight review checklist for deliverables emerging across other foundation groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Initial priorities include:
- Identity & Trust: Agent identity verification and delegated authorization boundaries (see [working-groups/identity-and-trust](identity-and-trust.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- Observability & Tracing: Behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging guarantees (see [working-groups/observability-and-traceability](observability-and-traceability.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- Agentic Commerce: Payment security guardrails, fund draining prevention, account leaks, and payment-agent scope limits (see [working-groups/agentic-commerce](agentic-commerce.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Lifecycle History
Originally, the working group maintained an independent Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions workstream. On 2026-06-22, this deliverable was merged into the cross-WG [working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream to maintain unified foundation-wide terminology[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Security and privacy terminology representation is maintained through designated delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

mutations.rationale: Record the consolidation of WG-specific taxonomy initiatives into the centralized cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream chaired by Junjie Bu.

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body chartered to identify vulnerability vectors, formalize threat models, catalog defensive design patterns, and provide actionable security and privacy baselines for agentic architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The working group operates openly in GitHub, maintaining dedicated workstream subdirectories with scoped ownership, contributor tables, and regular progress reports delivered to the AAIF Technical Committee [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification

### Workstreams and Governance

The working group divides its mandate into specialized workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

1. **Threat Modeling (`threat-modeling/`)**: Conducts gap analyses across existing standards—including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—to evaluate agent-specific threats such as memory poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, rogue execution, tool invocation risks, excessive agency, blast-radius containment, and commerce payment vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
2. **Design Patterns Catalog (`design-patterns/`)**: Formulates reusable secure and privacy-preserving design patterns using a problem/context/solution/trade-offs schema, sequenced behind threat model deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
3. **Best Practices Guide (`best-practices/`)**: Develops prescriptive builder and implementer guidance paired with curated external references [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
4. **Cross-WG Review Checklist (`review-checklist/`)**: Defines a lightweight review rubric to evaluate deliverables across other foundation working groups through security and privacy criteria [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
5. **Taxonomy (`taxonomy/`)**: Originating within the SP WG, the general terminology effort has transitioned into the centralized AAIF-wide [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as designated SP WG review delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

### Operational Policies

- **System of Record**: GitHub repositories are public and serve as the single system of record for maturing and canonical documents to enforce change tracking and contributor attribution, while Google Docs is restricted to early-stage brainstorming [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Technical Committee Interface**: Chairs submit monthly updates by the final week of the month, followed by a 7-day TC review window [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Workstream leads coordinate directly with [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) members through Manik [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Initial taxonomy draft elevated to a cross-WG initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed to lead the unified foundation taxonomy effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman designated as taxonomy delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Migration of taxonomy deliverables to `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` finalized [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-23**: Repositories made public; monthly TC reporting template ratified; workstream leads confirmed [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

mutations.rationale: Update central taxonomy coordination details, delegate structures across working groups, and repository pointers established in PR#4, deliverables/taxonomy.md, and meeting notes.

# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group (WS Taxonomy/Landscape) is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to build common conceptual terminology, resolve conflicting taxonomy definitions across working groups, and maintain unified landscape catalogs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Led by Junjie Bu, the group synchronizes asynchronously and via weekly sync meetings in the central `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification

### Cross-Working Group Coordination Model

The central taxonomy initiative incorporates delegate reviews and domain-specific topic slices from Foundation technical working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4]:

- **Security and Privacy**: Represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman, consolidating 10-20 core terms and evaluating agent archetypes classified by capability attributes such as tool access and network permissions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Provides structured JSON taxonomy slices keyed by priority (`p0`, `p1`, `p2`) covering system boundaries, evaluation subjects, quality metrics, grounding evidence, and failure symptoms [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].
- **Observability and Traceability**: Aligns cross-plane tracing concepts (orchestration, execution, protocol, reasoning/context) with OpenTelemetry guardrails and the Agent Behavior Trace Model [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

### Ingestion Workflow

Working groups contribute domain vocabulary slices using schema-validated JSON formats, which are merged centrally to eliminate duplicates and harmonize conflicting operational terms before elevation to foundation standards [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Initial taxonomy effort elevated from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to a cross-foundation initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed as cross-WG initiative lead [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Initial working group review delegates formally appointed [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Central repository established at `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open telemetry protocols, agent trace models, and multi-agent execution observability standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is chartered to establish open telemetry standards, trace models, and cross-boundary correlation formats across autonomous and human-in-the-loop agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]. The group focuses on protocol boundaries, execution observability, and standardized telemetry pipelines while aligning closely with upstream telemetry ecosystems such as OpenTelemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification

### Observability Planes and Trace Model Crosswalk

The working group formalizes a four-plane taxonomy model mapped against dimensions of the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:

- **Orchestration Plane**: Tracks coordination, delegation, and workflow routing.
- **Execution Plane**: Observes tool invocations, process runtimes, and low-level action steps.
- **Protocol Plane**: Measures inter-agent communication, serialization, and network boundaries.
- **Reasoning and Context Plane**: Captures context window utilization, prompt evolution, and intermediate planning turns.

### OpenTelemetry Alignment Guardrails

Observability standards developed by the WG prioritize compatibility with OpenTelemetry (OTel) semantic conventions. AAIF-specific extensions are explicitly categorized to prevent conflicting redefinitions of core OTel semantic attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

### Specification Recommendation Decision Path

Under Issue #12, the working group executes a 12-month decision roadmap regarding the Agent Behavior Trace Model: conducting gap analyses across existing external specifications to determine whether to adopt an existing standard, contribute upstream extensions, or publish a new normative AAIF specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate the three trace model dimensions, the four-plane crosswalk, and the evaluation roadmap from issues #10 and #12.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and behavioral trace specification defining agent turn boundaries, causal execution links, and multi-plane reasoning traces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification and crosswalk defining observable behavioral dimensions for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]. Maintained under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model formalizes how causal execution graphs, reasoning chains, and external outcomes are instrumented without breaking compatibility with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) baselines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Dimensions

The trace model organizes observability telemetry across three primary dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:

1. **Execution Structure**: Causal relationships between parent tasks, sub-tasks, spans, and child processes.
2. **Reasoning and Planning**: Multi-turn prompts, reasoning traces, intermediate decisions, and plan revisions.
3. **Outcomes and Effects**: Environmental mutations, tool execution results, and verifiable acceptance states.

### Plane Crosswalk

These dimensions intersect with four operational planes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:

- **Orchestration Plane**: Task dispatch, scheduling, and delegation tracking.
- **Execution Plane**: In-sandbox runtime invocations and tool operations.
- **Protocol Plane**: Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent message interchanges.
- **Reasoning/Context Plane**: Context window state, embeddings, and cognitive memory retrieval.

# Lifecycle History

- **Open Review**: Tracked under WG Issue #10 to release taxonomy v0.2 and publish an explicit plane-to-dimension crosswalk [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
- **Standardization Roadmap**: Under WG Issue #12, candidate trace standards are evaluated through a comparative gap analysis to determine whether the foundation should adopt an upstream standard, extend existing formats, or introduce a distinct AAIF trace specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate focus group structures, taxonomy efforts, and operational deliverables established in the June 25, 2026 working group meeting.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open telemetry protocols, agent trace models, context propagation, and runtime inspection standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, trace data models, and runtime inspection standards for agentic systems across the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. It coordinates specialized technical focus groups analyzing model-level primitives, execution state persistence, and multi-agent coordination patterns.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group partitions technical exploration across four specialized focus streams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:
- **LLM Primitives**: Executes landscape surveys and gap analyses targeting low-level model invocation, token lifecycle metrics, and protocol observability.
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates runtime state representation, memory structures, context window mechanics, and persistence models across existing platforms.
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Analyzes multi-agent task delegation, boundary-crossing telemetry, and cross-runtime execution traces.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Explores cognitive step decomposition, audit format standardization, and white-box tracing mechanisms.

In addition to focus groups, the working group maintains core terminology definitions in coordination with the foundation-wide taxonomy initiative and evaluates integration points with emerging resource discovery specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-25**: Transitioned workstream tracking to public GitHub issue trackers, formalized bi-weekly community presentation sessions, and confirmed Discord as the working group's primary collaboration channel [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining evaluation frameworks, failure mode taxonomies, and recovery patterns for accurate, enterprise-grade AI agent operation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish the standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably in enterprise environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. The working group addresses non-deterministic failures across autonomous workloads by classifying failure modes, defining structural resilience mechanisms, and recommending both proactive and reactive controls[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Technical Boundaries
The group's work centers on three technical areas[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Accuracy and Reliability Frameworks**: Defining evaluation metrics, quality thresholds, failure classifications, and detection techniques to measure drift and performance degradation in deployed agents.
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Specifying proactive architectural constraints, such as verification loops and grounding against authoritative trust anchors, to ensure agent trajectory alignment.
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Formulating standard specifications for safe-state restoration, rollback patterns, compensatory actions, and triggers requiring deterministic human escalation.

Explicitly out of scope are underlying model internals (training, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering), the development of commercial guardrail software or production runtimes, legal compliance advice, and trace/log wire protocols[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Telemetry emission mechanics are formally delegated to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), with ARWG defining the observable signals and evaluation criteria that the telemetry layer must capture[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

## Architectural Assumptions
The working group's deliverables assume a standard enterprise operating environment[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Operational Predictability**: Agent execution harnesses provide standardized lifecycle hooks for state recovery and trajectory steering.
- **Immutable Agent Identity**: Agent instances possess globally unique identities to enable evaluation and auditability across different software versions and runtime platforms.
- **Versioning for Reproducibility**: Metrics are only valid when bound to frozen configurations of models, system prompts, and toolsets.
- **Trust Anchors**: High-stakes workflows expose authoritative systems of record against which agent intermediate outputs can be systematically grounded.

## Deliverables and Cross-Group Coordination
ARWG maintains a canonical deliverable structure spanning D1 through D6 and internal item I1[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]:
- **D1 (Architectural Framing and Vocabulary)**: Structural taxonomy covering evaluation subjects, output quality, reliability dimensions, observability attribution, grounding, failure symptoms, root causes, and correction mechanisms[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. Contributes terminology directly to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis)**: Applied operational report synthesizing requirements across enterprise personas (product managers, operations/deployment engineers, evaluators, data scientists) to establish field-grounded benchmarks[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol)**: Standardized testing protocol whose scope is derived directly from D2 gap synthesis and tooling interoperability requirements[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Lifecycle History
The ARWG charter was approved on 2026-05-15 and updated on 2026-06-30[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Working group leadership includes Chair Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. The group operates on a biweekly main plenary schedule alternating with deliverable-focused working sessions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. Deliverable ID consistency across D1–D6 was harmonized in the working group charter prior to Technical Committee review[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate charter ratification, cross-working-group delegate governance, ISO/NIST alignment criteria, and asynchronous review workflows from merged meeting records.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting foundation initiative standardizing terminology, agentic AI classifications, and open-source landscape mappings across AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative established to standardize agentic AI terminology, define architectural boundaries, and maintain a unified ecosystem landscape map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. The workstream eliminates terminology fragmentation and redundant research across Foundation working groups through an asynchronous, pull-request-driven governance model led by nominated domain delegates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream coordinates terminology intake, boundary definitions, and landscape mapping through a federated structure:
- **Delegated Working Group Representation**: Each technical working group—including [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)—nominates active delegates and domain editors to review cross-cutting terms and resolve boundary conflicts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Dual-Tier Definition Structure**: Taxonomy terms require both an accessible summary for general clarity and detailed scope notes to provide technical precision for implementers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Standards Alignment**: Terminology is aligned where possible with established international frameworks such as ISO and NIST, explicitly documenting intentional deviations when addressing novel agentic capabilities[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Asynchronous Intake and Review**: Proposals follow a git-based PR workflow with unified review tracking matrices to process overlapping terms and boundary definitions offline before formal merging[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Human Oversight Policy**: Term definitions require human editorial review and adherence to established style guidelines, ensuring AI-assisted drafts undergo mandatory expert verification[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Metadata Schemas**: The workstream maintains SKOS Lite and CNCF-style metadata schemas to model agentic concepts, relationships, and source citations alongside [agentic-ai-landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-21**: Initial charter review and adoption of SKOS Lite metadata schema alongside the CNCF landscape format[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].
- **2026-06-01**: Ratification of the PR-driven asynchronous contribution workflow and integration strategy with existing landscape tooling[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **2026-06-08**: Transition of legacy definitions into PR-based intake and agreement to treat boundary definitions as continuous deliverables[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **2026-06-15**: Adoption of the ISO/NIST standards alignment principle and initiation of the AI usage policy requiring human oversight[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **2026-06-22**: Workstream charter merged across participating working groups, establishing delegate alignments and unified cross-group terminology review[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

mutations.rationale: Update the agentic AI landscape resource with ratified decisions adopting CNCF landscape tooling, decoupled repository structure, and member-versus-external entity classification.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Schema-validated catalog and interactive landscape mapping open-source and member agentic AI frameworks using CNCF-style metadata.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and schema-validated catalog mapping agentic frameworks, developer tooling, infrastructure, and member projects across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Governed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape adopts industry-standard CNCF landscape tooling to provide clear categorization between member-driven initiatives and external open-source or commercial technologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape platform is decoupled into an underlying data specification and a web presentation layer:
- **Data Model & Schema**: Leverages CNCF landscape tool metadata conventions to define categories, subcategories, project maturity, and licensing details[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Entity Classification**: Explicitly distinguishes Foundation member-driven projects from external community and commercial solutions to ensure transparency in ecosystem representation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Contribution Pipeline**: Changes are submitted via GitHub pull requests against the decoupled data repository, allowing automated linting and delegate review before publishing updates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-21**: Decoupled web portal and data repository architecture proposed using CNCF-style metadata structures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].
- **2026-06-01**: Formally adopted the CNCF landscape tool format and aligned on merging landscape directory efforts into `landscape.aif.io`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **2026-06-08**: Reconfirmed CNCF format adoption and established core delegate review criteria for new landscape entries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate June 2026 reporting and July 2026 meeting minutes establishing co-chairs, SKOS-Lite schema, CNCF-style landscape format, and the unified term review workflow.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative standardizing terminology using SKOS-Lite schemas, ecosystem mapping via CNCF-style configurations, and cross-working group term harmonisation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation charged with harmonizing terminology, establishing universal taxonomy definitions, and curating an interactive agentic AI landscape catalog [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates appointed delegates across Foundation working groups to resolve domain overlaps and maintain unified concept models [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains two core technical data schemas and an asynchronous contribution pipeline:
- **Taxonomy Data Schema**: Uses a SKOS-Lite (Simple Knowledge Organization System) data model to structure agentic terms, distinguishing domain-specific concepts from universal cross-cutting terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Landscape Schema**: Implements a CNCF-style configuration format to categorize open-source projects, member frameworks, and foundational technologies in the agentic ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Term Intake and Review Pipeline**: Member working groups contribute 10–20 core terms that are aggregated into a centralized tracking matrix [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Working group delegates apply consensus tags, flag candidate terms for culling, and identify universal primitives across domains such as identity and accuracy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Operational Cadence and Governance
Working group progress reports are submitted monthly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on the final business day of each reporting period, followed by a seven-calendar-day async review window prior to merging [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Related Concepts
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, and protocol-level observability across single- and multi-agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation body focused on establishing standardized telemetry conventions, verifiable execution trace formats, and boundary observability models for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Led by chairs Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group investigates failure visibility, context propagation, and runtime verification across LLM invocations and agent communication protocols [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes technical deliverables through specialized focus groups and cross-cutting specifications:
- **Focus Groups**: Initially chartered across five functional domains: LLM Primitives Observability, Protocol Observability, Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination), Agentic State and Context, and Agentic Reasoning [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. To address operational overlaps and simplify meeting cadences, the LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability focus groups were unified into a single combined track [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Provable Traceability Architectures**: Technical efforts focus on producing hardened, provable trace architectures and evaluating agentic execution records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Specification Alignment**: The group evaluates discovery and trace proposals, including the [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) specification and causal behavioral trace representations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Resource Discovery Specification
proposed_concept.description: Specification for discovering and verifying AI resources using static indexing catalogs and dynamic registries backed by SPIFFE and ANS trust mechanisms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification defines a decentralized architecture for AI agents to locate, inspect, and verify distributed AI tools, endpoints, and resources [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]. Presented by Junjie Bu and backed by a consortium of ten industry participants, the specification provides discovery interfaces and trust manifests to ensure agent interactions target verified infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Architecture / Specification
ARD decouples static metadata publication from live service querying through two core building blocks:
- **Catalogs**: Provide static indexing facilities and natural language search capabilities, enabling agents to parse resource capabilities and functional metadata [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Dynamic Registries**: Expose REST APIs for runtime discovery, registration, and health verification of dynamic resources [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Trust and Identity Integration**: Embeds cryptographic verification mechanisms through trust manifests, supporting decentralized identity standards including SPIFFE (Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone) and Agent Network Standard (ANS) specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Related Concepts

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining agent threat models, design patterns, security best practices, and cross-group review checklists for the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) develops threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and operational best practices for agentic AI systems within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group coordinates technical deliverables across five active workstreams, liaises with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), and collaborates with external standards bodies such as OWASP, AARM, MCP ACS, and ETSI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group operates through five specialized workstreams and defined reporting mechanisms[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, this workstream evaluates threat vectors across eight key areas, synthesizing foundations from MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security controls and operational baselines (see [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, cataloging structural runtime security patterns such as [attested isolated runtimes](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and tool attestation mechanisms[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing intake security audit checklists and evaluating potential overlaps with external initiatives such as the FINOS AI governance framework[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Coordinated through delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman into the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

## Reporting Governance

The working group reports monthly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) following standardized guidelines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]:
- **Cadence**: Reports are submitted via pull request by the last business day of each reporting month[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee reviews reports asynchronously within a 7 calendar-day window, mediated by an assigned TC liaison representative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Charter KPIs**: Progress is tracked against four key charter metrics: Adoption, Quality, Community, and Timelines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Lifecycle History

In June 2026, the working group moved from formation into execution, formally establishing public repositories and chartering its five workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]. The Taxonomy of Terms was transferred to the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape initiative during this period, and initial drafts for threat modeling gap analysis and security best practices were submitted for member review in July 2026[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative standardizing terminology using unified working sheets, consensus columns, and PR-driven workflows across foundation working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group (WS Taxonomy and Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative led by Junjie Bu responsible for establishing standard terminology, conceptual boundaries, and ecosystem mapping across all working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. Formed through delegates appointed by each foundation technical working group, the initiative consolidates terms into a unified review pipeline before formalizing them as pull requests and standardized schemas[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates through a staged asynchronous and synchronous workflow designed to achieve cross-working-group consensus[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]:

## Delegate Model

Each AAIF working group designates core representatives to coordinate terminology integration and avoid siloed definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. For example, the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman to review and align security concepts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

## Curation Workflow

- **Unified Working Sheet**: Term proposals from across the foundation are collected in a central working sheet, allowing contributors to submit entries, attribution names, and commentary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Consensus Tracking**: The sheet tracks acceptance via a dedicated consensus column to identify finalized definitions and flag contested entries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **Discord Triage**: Contentious terms are surfaced in foundation discussion channels for community input prior to culling or refinement[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **PR Conversion**: Validated terms transition from the spreadsheet to repository pull requests incorporating CNCF-style metadata schemas and definitions style guides[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Lifecycle History

The workstream kicked off on 2026-05-21 with initial charter planning and weekly Monday syncs[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. In June 2026, individual working groups (including Security & Privacy) merged their independent terminology initiatives into the unified workstream[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. In July 2026, the group entered its execution phase, extending meeting syncs to one hour and initiating structured review of the consolidated working sheet[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the central technical leadership and governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). It oversees technical vision, admits and guides open source projects, coordinates cross-working-group alignment, and reviews monthly operational progress reports submitted by working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

# Architecture / Specification

The Technical Committee provides operational oversight across working groups through designated liaisons and structured review schedules[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]:

## Working Group Oversight and Reporting

- **Monthly Reporting Cadence**: Working groups submit standardized progress reports via pull requests by the last business day of each reporting month[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Liaison Representation**: The TC assigns a liaison representative to each working group (such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) who relays updates, clarifies cross-foundation alignment, and facilitates informational oversight[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Async Review Window**: Monthly reports undergo an asynchronous 7 calendar-day review window; if no blockers are identified by the close of the window or upon explicit sign-off, the report is merged[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Escalations and External Alignments**: The TC advises working groups on external cross-foundation relationships (e.g., OWASP, AARM, MCP ACS) and inter-foundation overlap (e.g., FINOS AI governance)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Lifecycle History

In mid-2026, standardized monthly reporting templates and asynchronous liaison review workflows were operationalized across AAIF working groups, establishing structured monitoring of deliverable milestones and charter KPIs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating shared agentic AI terminology using SKOS-Lite schemas and maintaining the global ecosystem landscape portal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative that curates a shared glossary of agentic AI terminology and maintains an authoritative ecosystem map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Formally ratified on June 21, 2026, the workstream serves as a common terminology gatekeeper and landscape repository so that vertical working groups—such as [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Governance, Risk and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), and [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)—operate from harmonized vocabularies rather than isolated definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operating Model
The workstream operates under a federated curation model led by Junjie Bu (Google) as Chair and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) as Co-Chair[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Rather than inventing vertical domain definitions independently, the workstream relies on designated Domain Editors nominated across working groups (two delegates per group) to ingest, de-duplicate, and reconcile glossaries supplied across the foundation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

Scope boundaries enforce separation between shared and specialized assets[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]:
- **Horizontal Curation (In Scope):** Cross-cutting terminology consolidation, SKOS-Lite metadata mapping, consensus arbitration on overlapping definitions, and deployment of public web dashboards.
- **Vertical Ownership (Out of Scope):** Specialized domain whitepapers, legal compliance analyses, and execution protocol designs (such as MCP or A2A specifications), which remain strictly owned by their respective vertical technical working groups.

## Data Schemas and Portal Delivery
Glossary terms are organized using a flexible SKOS-Lite metadata structure comprising `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Ecosystem projects and platforms are tracked via a centralized `landscape.yml` configuration[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

The foundation publishes its deliverables via an automated GitHub Actions deployment workflow (`deploy-pages.yml`) triggered on pushes to the default branch[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]. The workflow assembles the static landscape assets, the raw `landscape.yml` catalog, the interactive Taxonomy Explorer (`dist/taxonomy`), and the portal landing page stamped with an automated build timestamp in Pacific Time, publishing the assembled bundle directly to GitHub Pages[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

## Cadence and Communication
- **Meetings:** Weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT / 11:30 AM ET / 4:30 PM BST (30-minute sync)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Mailing List:** `ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Discord:** `#ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Repository:** `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-21:** Formal workstream charter ratified by foundation leadership[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing standards, benchmarks, failure mode classifications, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate reliably under enterprise conditions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]. proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry formats, causal trace propagation protocols, and cross-boundary execution models for multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]. The group collaborates with standards bodies including OpenTelemetry and the IETF while aligning domain terminology with the foundation-wide [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Focus Group Organization
The working group organizes technical work streams across specialized focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]:
- **Protocols and Primitives:** Consolidated focus group (merging the protocols and primitives work streams) establishing unified terminology, exchange formats, and telemetry representations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Multi-Agent Observability:** Work stream developing trace context propagation and multi-agent delegation semantics across distributed networks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Agentic Resource Discovery and Skills:** Reviewing pipelines and proposals for discovering agent capabilities and skills telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

## External Interoperability and Upstream Contributions
- **OpenTelemetry Alignment:** Upstream contributions of reference implementations and standardized SDKs based on the working group's gap analysis[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **IETF Collaborations:** Tracking emerging agent network observability work across IETF efforts (including Agent Proto, DMSC, and Dawn)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Peer-to-Peer and Transport Tracing:** Assessing P2P protocols (such as libp2p and Lumina), OpenID specifications, and Server-Sent Events (SSE) for cross-hyperscaler agent interaction and identity-aware telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Identity & Trust Coordination:** Coordinating with the Identity & Trust Working Group on cryptographic verification of agent payloads and proof-of-control architectures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

## Contribution Governance
In accordance with foundation guidance from the AAIF CTO and Governing Council, repositories maintain managed intake controls while taxonomy terms are harmonized through dedicated working syncs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
