proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. The working group operates under protocol-neutrality principles, purposefully avoiding authoring competing commercial protocols in favor of identifying common ground across existing or emerging efforts and advising the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Scope and Domains
The group standardizes interoperability reference models and patterns across multiple phases of the commerce lifecycle [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]:
- **Discovery and Negotiation:** Standardizing catalog search, capability negotiation, and offer evaluation between buyer and merchant agents.
- **Checkout and Orchestration:** Harmonizing cart generation, multi-party commitments, and payment service provider routing.
- **Post-Purchase Lifecycle:** Defining stateful schemas for receipt exchange, shipment tracking, returns, and dispute mitigation.

### Governance and Leadership
- **Co-Chairs:** Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the term March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Meeting Cadence:** Biweekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Neutrality and Antitrust:** Members act as individuals rather than corporate proxies under the standard Linux Foundation Antitrust Policy [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

mutations.rationale: Add formal charter scope, leadership contacts, approval dates, and core focus areas covering workflow primitives, state persistence, and tool invocation boundaries.

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining reference architectures, execution profiles, and workflow orchestration primitives for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) establishes shared workflow models, execution semantics, and foundational terminology enabling agentic AI systems to reliably operate across frameworks, tools, and execution environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Approved on May 13, 2026, the working group translates non-deterministic agent decision-making into resilient, auditable multi-step execution flows across organizational boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Architecture / Specification

### Scope and Responsibilities
The working group divides its technical deliverables into three core pillars [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:
1. **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics:** Standardizing primitives for tasks, tool invocations, branching, subagent handoffs, step ordering, and parallel execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
2. **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution:** Defining persistence schemas, pause-and-resume mechanisms, retry idempotency, and workflow-level audit logs for multi-hour or multi-day runs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
3. **Tool Invocation and External Coordination:** Harmonizing external service interactions across API, CLI, and messaging boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

### Coordination and Boundaries
- **Runtime Signals Separation:** Workflow-level systems of record and step outcomes are managed by W&PI, while runtime telemetry metrics and traces are coordinated with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Leadership:** Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) with Adam Seligman (Workato) serving as Co-Chair [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

mutations.rationale: Update with active workstream deliverables, external collaboration posture, and cross-working-group review efforts documented in the July 2026 meeting minutes.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining agent threat models, design patterns, security best practices, and cross-workgroup review criteria.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops threat models, design patterns, and defensive implementation guidance across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]. The working group establishes reference controls for prompt injection, session replay, and tool poisoning, while coordinating cross-cutting architectural reviews with sibling workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification

### Active Deliverables and Workstreams
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, scoping attack vectors on decomposed agent components such as tool-orchestration layers and context histories [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing baseline recommendations across secret elimination and runtime policy controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, categorizing enforceable structural mitigations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing formal review rubrics and interface checks against the scopes of [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13].

### Taxonomy and Collaboration Stance
- **Taxonomy Alignment:** The working group curates security-specific definitions (e.g. constraints, guardrails, session boundaries, and replay attack prevention) for inclusion in the shared taxonomy maintained by [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **External Liaisons:** Unofficial collaboration with organizations including OWASP continues while formal partnership frameworks are processed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

mutations.rationale: Update with leadership, July 2026 milestone progress on deliverables D1 and D2, and cross-working-group taxonomy contribution streams.

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing benchmarks, evaluation standards, and engineering practices for reliable autonomous agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) establishes benchmark methodologies, evaluation frameworks, and operational engineering standards to measure and improve the fidelity of autonomous agent execution [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group addresses non-deterministic drift, validation consistency, and execution resilience across real-world systems [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Architecture / Specification

### Workstreams and Deliverables
- **D1 (Terminology & Methodology Support):** Grounded in academic and empirical literature, D1 provides core definitions and evaluation methodology, operating through staged milestones covering outcome correctness, perturbation robustness, and system reliability [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis):** Reframed from a pure benchmark catalog into an enterprise-oriented requirements and pain-point analysis, surveying practitioner personas to resolve gaps preventing open benchmark reuse [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **I1 (Liaisons):** Coordinating cross-group dependencies, including active liaison channels with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

### Cross-WG Alignment
ARWG feeds validated accuracy terminology into the central workstream managed by [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), filtering prioritized terminology batches to focus on WG-specific execution semantics [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate progress from the April and May 2026 reports covering the approved charter, the Agentic Commerce Capability Map deliverable, and payment protocol evaluations (ACP, UCP, MPP).

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing commercial protocols, payment flows, and transactional interaction models for autonomous agent transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group defines open, protocol-neutral specifications and architectural standards for commercial agent transactions, bridging discovery, checkout negotiation, payment execution, and post-purchase lifecycle workflows [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. The group focuses on commerce-facing interfaces and verifiable boundary signals rather than internal proprietary merchant engines [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group coordinates cross-cutting dependencies with identity, authorization, and security frameworks to ensure fraud and trust signals survive multi-party transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its domain across key commercial phases and abstractions:
- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map:** A protocol-neutral deliverable standardizing touchpoints across discovery, delegated authority, checkout, payment, fraud signaling, and post-purchase [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Discovery & Negotiation:** Distinguishes asynchronous product feeds from live catalog retrieval and treats checkout negotiation as stateful, merchant-authoritative transactions across protocols such as ACP and UCP [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Payment Abstractions:** Models payment handling around three core abstractions: handlers, instruments, and credentials [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]. It evaluates composition patterns including the challenge-credential-receipt flow from the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Trust and Fraud Signals:** Defines verifiable boundaries separating shopper identity and risk from agent identity and risk, including delegation binding and risk-triggered context requests [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Lifecycle History
In April 2026, the working group initiated drafting of its charter and began discovery/checkout protocol evaluations [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. In May 2026, the charter was formally approved, establishing the Capability Map as the initial core deliverable and kicking off technical analyses of ACP, UCP, and MPP [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

mutations.rationale: Update working group status with reporting from July 2026 covering sub-WG progress, NVIDIA SAW evaluation, and OAuth 2.0 baseline proposal.

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining agent identity, credential delegation, decentralized trust mechanisms, and verifiable action records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes foundational identity standards, cryptographic trust delegation models, and verifiable execution receipts for autonomous agents across multi-party and cross-platform interactions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. The group is chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

The working group operates across three primary sub-working groups: Taxonomy, Reference Architecture, and Critical Use Cases [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's architectural activities center around several core tracks:
- **Authorization Baseline:** Profiling OAuth 2.0 as the normative presentation baseline for cross-platform agent authorization, covering token formats, delegation chains, and scope expressions, while keeping backend policy evaluation out of scope [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Reference Architecture:** Standardizing components across Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. It enforces the foundational assumption that sub-agents cannot hold more permissions than delegating agents or the initiating user [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **External Standards Evaluation:** Ingesting external architectures including NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) four-layer identity model, the Open Delegation and Identity Standard (ODIS), and OpenID Foundation specifications [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Critical Use Cases:** Developing operational requirements across Internal, B2B, and B2C interaction models spanning naming, deployment, dynamic per-request authorization, and retirement [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group submitted formal progress highlighting the taxonomy demarcation between observability and action records, advanced the reference architecture component table, and requested Technical Committee consensus on the OAuth 2.0 authorization baseline profile [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

mutations.rationale: Create taxonomy concept for Action Record as formulated by WG Identity & Trust to delineate verifiable consequential actions from runtime observability traces.

proposed_concept.title: Action Record
proposed_concept.description: Tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record of a single consequential action taken by an autonomous agent.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An Action Record is a tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable artifact documenting a single consequential action executed by an autonomous agent [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. Distinct from operational telemetry, an Action Record is designed to provide third parties, auditors, counterparties, or courts with conclusive proof of what an agent verifiably executed [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Architecture / Specification
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes a strict architectural boundary between Action Records and observability:
- **Observability vs. Verification:** Observability and runtime tracing answer operator-facing questions ("what is my agent doing?"), whereas the Action Record answers evidential questions for counterparties and auditors ("what did this agent verifiably do?") [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Selective Disclosure and Privacy:** Action Records must support content-private properties, allowing selective disclosure of operational payload data without breaking cryptographic verification [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Relationship to Identity Artifacts:** An Action Record binds to identity and delegation chains while functioning as an independent, non-repudiable proof of action rather than an access grant or session token [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

Related standards include [standards/evidence-record-spec](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) and [standards/trace](../standards/trace.md).

mutations.rationale: Incorporate monthly reports detailing WG leadership, the four-stage commerce lifecycle, wallet integrations, and fraud signal coordination.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing capability maps, gap analyses, and reference architectures across discovery, checkout, payment mandates, and post-purchase workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI) that investigates protocols, payment mechanisms, and transactional interactions across autonomous and assisted commercial systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. The group focuses on evaluating the commerce lifecycle, resolving integration friction across fragmented protocols, and mapping how autonomous agents observe, execute, and negotiate transactions on behalf of consumers[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its domain around a four-stage commerce lifecycle model intersected by cross-cutting governance concerns[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

1. **Product Discovery**: Analyzing feed-based versus live-query discovery mechanisms, catalog normalization, data freshness, and vendor trustworthiness[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Evaluating protocol bindings across frameworks such as the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) (ACP), structured messaging formats, and human approval handshakes[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
3. **Payment and Wallets**: Exploring agent wallet architectures, payment credential exchanges, micropayment standards (such as x402), and verifiable authorization mandates (such as AP2) that constrain agent financial liability[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
4. **Post-Purchase and Remedies**: Addressing order state tracking, cancellations, returns, refunds, adjustments, and dispute handling, emphasizing the boundary between read-only order observation and state-changing mutations[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

Cross-cutting focus areas include fraud and trust signal interoperability. The group analyzes how risk signals traverse agent, platform, merchant, and payment processor boundaries, differentiating agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk, in collaboration with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History
The working group launched in February 2026 to survey the agentic commerce landscape and alleviate protocol fragmentation and merchant integration burdens[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. In March 2026, the group adopted a problem-first lifecycle methodology and initiated its capability map and gap analysis[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]. Work in mid-2026 expanded to fraud and trust signal propagation in June[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe], followed by post-purchase workflows and wallet integration models in July[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

mutations.rationale: Update workstream leadership, term arbitration methodology, and progress across the 128-term vocabulary backlog based on the July 2026 report.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream arbitrating shared agentic AI terminology, managing the 128-term unified vocabulary backlog, and publishing the ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation working group co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) dedicated to standardizing agentic AI terminology and mapping open-source and member technologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. The workstream arbitrates contested domain terms across foundational concepts, maintains machine-readable taxonomy definitions, and curates the public foundation landscape portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream manages a unified 128-term vocabulary backlog spanning multiple Foundation domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:
- **Arbitration Process**: Utilizes sequential group review syncs to evaluate terms before formal definition drafting. Candidate terms are either admitted, culled, or held for debate when working groups hold diverging technical positions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Scope Alignment**: Terminology review clusters cover Universal Terms, [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Publication Pipeline**: Approved terms are codified in Git pull requests, moving debate history out of working spreadsheets and directly into version-controlled repositories powering the public taxonomy portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the workstream shifted from collecting candidate terms to formal arbitration, reviewing 46 terms across extended weekly syncs and admitting its first 13 approved terms into the public taxonomy repository via PR #33[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. By early August 2026, cumulative progress reached 67 reviewed terms out of the 128-term backlog, with 21 admitted entries live in the taxonomy, 15 culled, and 25 contested terms (including the definition of `Agent`) held for deeper consensus building[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Reference Architecture Generator Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill producing structured AAIF reference architectures and technology evaluation assessments for AI agent frameworks and specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Reference Architecture skill (`aaif-ref-arch`) is a modular agent skill designed to analyze open-source AI agent tools, frameworks, and specifications to generate structured reference architectures and evaluation assessments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]. It automates repository inspection, architecture decomposition across primitive, orchestration, and system layers, and telemetry tracing analysis.

# Architecture / Specification

The skill provides a deterministic 4-stage process [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]:
1. **Source Gathering**: Inspects repository READMEs, architectural blueprints, schemas, and reference implementations.
2. **Reference Architecture Generation**: Formats output documentation covering Zoom Level scope, prerequisites, ASCII architecture diagrams, instrumentation walkthroughs, sample trace outputs, cost profiles, validation criteria, and operational boundaries.
3. **Evaluation Assessment**: Produces structured maturity assessments against AAIF guidelines.
4. **Commit & Packaging**: Validates git cleanliness and aligns documentation with foundation standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

# Lifecycle History

Authored by Matthew Khouzam under MIT license in the Tracing Landscape repository under `tracing_landscape/.agents/skills/aaif-ref-arch/SKILL.md` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural guideline organizing workflow reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs and reusable patterns rather than raw agent counts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model organizes reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than structural system properties like agent counts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. In this framework, reference architectures represent complete compositions of patterns, capabilities, and operational guarantees tailored to specific operational needs, while individual patterns capture reusable solutions to isolated sub-problems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].

# Architecture / Specification

The architectural model defines clear boundaries between artifacts:
- **Reference Architecture**: A complete end-to-end composition of reusable patterns, required capability roles, boundary controls, and exit states answering a distinct practitioner job (e.g., [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Pattern**: An independently adoptable solution to a recurring sub-problem that specifies invariants, failure modes, and implementation axes without being tied to a single product or runtime [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Topology as Attribute**: Structural topology (such as single-agent versus multi-agent) serves as an internal characteristic rather than a top-level classification taxon [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Scenarios as Validation**: Real-world use cases validate architectural fit, exposing gaps in variants or indicating the need for distinct job architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Lifecycle History

Proposed on 2026-07-20 in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group as decision record `job-oriented-architecture-model.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

mutations.rationale: Enrich the human approval gate pattern with authoritative invariants, problem definition, and failure modes from the merged pattern specification.

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern requiring an authorized, uniquely identified human to explicitly approve an immutable proposal before a workflow executes a protected effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Human Approval Gate pattern halts execution before a protected effect until a uniquely identified, authorized human principal makes an explicit decision on an immutable proposal [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. It ensures that human judgment is captured within a durable, tamper-evident record linking who reviewed, what version was reviewed, and the exact decision rendered before downstream execution proceeds [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern mediates between proposal generation and executor action:
```text
immutable proposal ──► present to authorized human ──► explicit decision
                              │                           │
                              └── durable wait ─────────┘
                                          │
                          decision record: who · what · when
```

### Invariants
- **Unique Human Principal**: The approver must be an individually authenticated human holding authorization for the specific decision class; shared role accounts are disallowed [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Proposal Immutability**: The interaction surface must display the exact proposal payload that binds to execution. Any mutation or superseding proposal invalidates pending reviews and requires a fresh decision [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Explicit Affirmation**: Approval and rejection must be explicit; timeouts, queue silence, delivery failures, or system crashes must never default to approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Deterministic Decision Binding**: The resulting decision record couples run identifier, proposal version, approver identity, decision status, and timestamps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Idempotency & Race Safety**: Out-of-order, late, or duplicated decisions cannot trigger duplicate resumes or executions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

### Related Patterns
- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

mutations.rationale: Update leadership, track consolidation into three active focus groups, and active collaboration with P2P networking and verifiable telemetry initiatives.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, and protocol-level monitoring across agent execution boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry formats, execution tracing models, and cross-boundary monitoring protocols for autonomous and multi-agent systems within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group bridges application-layer telemetry, runtime kernel and network tracing, and distributed agent interaction models.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

# Working Group Structure and Focus Tracks
In July 2026, the working group restructured its operational tracks from five focus groups into three consolidated tracks to streamline participation and reduce scope overlap:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

1. **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability** (Lead: Zayne Turner): Focuses on Agentic Resource Discovery ([ARD](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)) observability covering skill discovery, provenance, and pre-execution trust decisions, alongside establishing skills as first-class citizens in execution tracing and drafting the cross-boundary observability gap model.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
2. **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination** (Lead: Ty Smith): Develops multi-agent tracing methodologies, modular Observability Maps, and Context Intelligence Graph runtime prototypes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
3. **Agentic State & Context** (Lead: Govindaraj): Focuses on unified reasoning and state observability, landscape analysis, and integration with verifiable capsules such as Agent Action Capsules.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Key Initiatives and Collaborations
The group advances several core specifications and cross-ecosystem collaborations:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Spearheaded by Matthew Lee to build interoperability across application-layer libraries and contribute recommendations to the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) core specification.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Peer-to-Peer and Verifiable Telemetry**: Exploring integrations with LibP2P networking stacks, GossipSub telemetry, and Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) using CBOR42 serialization to separate telemetry semantics from cryptographic proofs in decentralized agent architectures.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Collaborates with the [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream to reconcile universal terminology for observability primitives.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by defining a shared workflow model and standardized terminology for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87] It produces interoperability guidelines, specification extensions, and reference architectures enabling AI agent workflows to function consistently across diverse runtime frameworks, external tools, and enterprise execution environments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

The working group is led by appointed chairs serving terms from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Chair**: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)

- **Reference Architectures**: Codifies repeatable architectural patterns and orchestration models, including human-in-the-loop gates and autonomous execution loops.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]

# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification standardizing the representation of agent execution turns, causal interaction links, reasoning states, and cross-boundary tool calls.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7] Incubated within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the initiative provides a shared telemetry model that captures multi-agent coordination while remaining interoperable with mainstream distributed tracing systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Architecture and Standardization Strategy
The specification effort is led by Matthew Lee (Datadog) and targets two complementary outcomes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
1. **Application-Layer Interoperability**: Creating reference libraries and data models that provide consistent trace semantics across diverse agent frameworks and execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
2. **Upstream Alignment with OpenTelemetry**: Identifying limitations in existing generative AI semantic conventions to submit formal recommendations to the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) core specification.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

The trace model coordinates with focus group initiatives addressing [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) provenance and first-class skill execution tracking.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practitioner guide detailing failure patterns, defensive controls, and decision frameworks across five core security domains for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practitioner-focused reference document produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. It establishes implementation guidance across five key security domains, structured around recurring failure patterns, actionable technical controls, and operational decision frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

The guide explicitly excludes identity and delegated authorization architecture—such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693 token exchange—which falls under the remit of the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide addresses five distinct operational domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
1. **Secrets Management**: Eliminating long-lived credentials and securing ephemeral access across dynamic agent tool invocations.
2. **Secure Tool Invocation**: Securing Model Context Protocol (MCP) server connections, boundary enforcement, and tool supply-chain validation.
3. **Guardrails**: Implementing runtime policy evaluation, prompt injection mitigation, and in-loop boundary checks.
4. **Evaluation Frameworks**: Automated security testing, robustness grading, and red-teaming harnesses for agentic workflows.
5. **Post-Incident Forensics**: Auditing agent action trails, capturing state artifacts, and conducting root-cause attribution.

Each domain section follows a standardized tripartite structure [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
- **Failure Patterns**: Empirical failure modes and exploitation vectors observed in production and test environments.
- **Defensive Controls**: Concrete architectural, protocol-level, and operational controls mitigating each failure pattern.
- **Decision Frameworks**: Evaluation rubrics guiding builders on tooling, configuration, and architectural tradeoffs.

The guide concludes with a curated reference matrix of security tooling evaluated by maturity, licensing, and implementation costs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History
The guide represents Deliverable 4 of 5 under the Security and Privacy Working Group work plan [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. An initial draft v0.1 was submitted via PR #9 following the kickoff of the dedicated Best Practices workstream in July 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body focused on hardening agent architectures against systemic vulnerabilities, prompt injection, unauthorized tool execution, and data exfiltration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3]. The group develops threat modeling frameworks, architectural design patterns, and engineering implementation standards for production agentic deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output across five workstreams stood up in mid-2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3]:
- **Threat Modeling**: Developing threat modeling gap analyses for autonomous agent execution environments.
- **Best Practices**: Authoring the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) spanning secrets, tool invocation, guardrails, evaluations, and forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Structuring architectural patterns for safe execution boundaries and runtime isolation.
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Reviewing security and privacy terminology in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **Privacy and Data Protection**: Formulating data minimization and boundary architectures for agent workloads.

Identity federation and delegated authorization specifications are out of scope for the group and coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned from formation to active execution in June 2026 with confirmed workstream leads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3]. In July 2026, the group moved its drafts into public repository PRs, publishing initial iterations of the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and the Best Practices Guide [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry formats, execution tracing models, and cross-boundary audit logging for autonomous and multi-agent systems within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. The group develops specifications across model inferences, tool executions, and platform orchestration boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group establishes telemetry standards including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), [Agent Trace](../standards/agent-trace.md), and [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic convention integrations.

Technical operations maintain GitHub as the primary source of truth, managing tasks and cross-WG coordination via structured work items [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. Active issues must declare one of six standardized lifecycle statuses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]:
- `needs owner`: Validated work awaiting a designated driver.
- `scoping`: Working group participants defining deliverables, boundaries, and outcomes.
- `in progress`: Active research, drafting, or implementation.
- `ready for review`: Material prepared for group review and decision windows.
- `blocked`: Progress gated on external input, decision, or dependency.
- `done`: Outcome landed or formally closed.

# Lifecycle History
The working group codified repository-first operational guidelines in its working methods specification to standardize meeting rhythms, review windows, and status updates delivered to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The working group develops open threat models, security design patterns, and defensive guidelines that model providers, runtime authors, and peer working groups can adopt to secure autonomous agents and establish clear accountability boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operations
- **Leadership**: Chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the term March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Meeting Cadence**: Meets biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT, operating under open governance where past and future meetings, recordings, and repositories default to public access[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Review and Acceptance Process**: The working group conducts internal review and can directly merge pull requests within its approved charter scope without waiting for upfront [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) approval, providing transparency via monthly reports[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Active Deliverables and Workstreams
1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis & Framework**: Comparative gap analysis assessing agentic threat surfaces against MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, incorporating STRIDE, PASTA, and human-user agent (HUA) interaction models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8].
2. **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Practitioner guidance identifying architectural failure modes and baseline controls, sharing identity and credential delegation scope with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Structured repository and contribution templates for reusable architectural security patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
4. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Coordination mechanism to evaluate security and privacy intersections across all Foundation workstreams and prevent charter overlap[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
5. **Taxonomy Alignment**: Working group delegates align security and privacy definitions with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# References

# Overview
Higress is an open-source, cloud-native AI gateway built on Envoy and Istio that provides a unified control plane for LLM API management, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server hosting, and AI agent traffic governance[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18]. Originally developed by Alibaba and hosted as a Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox project, Higress is positioned in the [Agentic AI Landscape](agentic-ai-landscape.md) within the Orchestration & Multi-Agent subcategory alongside gateway systems like Solo.io's `agentgateway`[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].

# Architecture / Specification
Higress bridges infrastructure traffic routing with agent protocol boundaries:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Hosting & Registry**: Exposes built-in hosting, registry, and routing mechanisms for MCP tool servers across heterogeneous backends[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].
- **Unified AI Traffic Management**: Intercepts and routes model inference requests, agent-to-agent communication streams, and external tool calls through an Envoy proxy data plane[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].
- **Policy and Observability Boundary**: Implements rate limiting, token-aware routing, authentication, and traffic security policies at the protocol boundary before requests reach foundational models or downstream agent tools[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].

# References
- Upstream Repository: https://github.com/alibaba/higress [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18]
- Boundary Interoperability: [Agent-MCP Server Boundary](agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)
- Related Gateways: [Context Forge](context-forge.md)

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill providing structured GitHub issue triage, prompt injection isolation, codebase grounding, and historical review matching.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `issue-analysis` skill is a modular agent skill designed for repository maintainers to produce structured, first-pass technical assessments of filed GitHub issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Maintained under the Apache-2.0 license within the [submission-analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) repository, the skill establishes an objective evaluation pipeline that classifies incoming issues, assesses severity, develops falsifiable root-cause hypotheses, and outlines concrete next steps without executing irreversible code modifications or unverified patches [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

Operating in accordance with the [agent-skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) packaging model, the skill enforces an adversarial input boundary, treats issue descriptions strictly as untrusted data, and grounds triage reasoning against local repository files and a historical corpus of past human reviews [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification

The issue analysis workflow proceeds across four sequential stages:

1. **Evidence Ingestion and Prompt Injection Isolation:** Incoming issue text is ingested inside a strict nonce-delimited boundary and handled entirely as passive data [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Instructions embedded within issue bodies—such as attempts to alter output formatting, call external tools, disclose credentials, or broadcast mentions (e.g., `@everyone` pings)—are treated as adversarial artifacts rather than executable tasks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60]. When adversarial behavior is identified, the skill sets `injectionSuspected: true` and logs the attempted vector in `injectionNotes` before analyzing the technical substance [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. The author's GitHub relationship (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `CONTRIBUTOR`, `NONE`) informs domain depth assumptions but does not bypass safety constraints [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
2. **Read-Only Codebase Grounding:** The agent inspects local codebase files relevant to the issue's claims [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. To guarantee containment, the environment forbids mutating the repository, running network commands, or invoking build steps [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Components must be cited by concrete paths (e.g., `src/queue/consumer.ts`) rather than vague subsystem designations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
3. **Historical Review Grounding:** The agent searches the project's `references/` directory containing past maintainer reviews [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. It evaluates frontmatter tags, severity ratings, and affected components to select 3 to 5 relevant precedents, citing them in `relatedPastIssues` along with specific relevance justifications [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Synthetic training examples (such as duplicate webhook delivery, credential logging bypasses, or configuration reloads) are explicitly excluded from being cited as live production history [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
4. **Structured Output Generation:** The triage assessment is formatted against a standardized schema containing seven required sections [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:
   - **Summary:** Single-paragraph restatement of the issue in maintainer terms.
   - **Classification:** Categorization into `Type` (`bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, `ambiguous`), `Severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `informational`), `Reproducibility` (`reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, `not-applicable`), and an explicit severity rationale grounded in blast radius and workarounds.
   - **Affected components:** Specific file paths and module identifiers.
   - **Root-cause hypotheses:** Mechanistic explanations with explicit criteria to confirm or refute each hypothesis.
   - **Suggested actions:** Sequenced operational steps for maintainers (e.g., diagnostics, log checks, targeted tests), avoiding unverified patch generation.
   - **Open questions:** Information requests needed from the reporter.
   - **Related past reviews:** Relevant past reviews with cross-cutting takeaways.

[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]: aaif/submission-analyser: src/skills/issue-analysis/template.md
[^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d]: aaif/submission-analyser: src/skills/issue-analysis/references/example-queue-duplicate-delivery.md

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions agent utilizing Copilot inference and dry-run canary pipelines to triage submissions against adversarial prompt injections.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser is a headless GitHub Actions agent utilizing inference and dry-run canary pipelines to triage and validate incoming repository issues and pull requests while isolating adversarial prompt injection vectors. The project maintains an automated test fixture suite to verify defensive boundaries against untrusted input strings submitted by external contributors.

# Architecture / Specification
The submission-analyser test suite maintains dedicated fixtures in `tests/fixtures/injections/` covering key adversarial vector classes targeted at automated triage models:
- **Direct Instruction Overrides**: Fixtures testing resilience against attempts to override system prompts, clear instruction history, or exfiltrate configuration state [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Hidden Comments**: Hidden instructions concealed within HTML comments designed to evade human inspection while directing triage models to suppress injection warnings or manipulate severity ratings [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Malicious External References**: Payloads attempting indirect prompt injection by requesting the agent fetch and execute remote files or diffs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- **Tool Call Imitation**: Injected syntaxes imitating structured tool invocations (`tool_call` JSON blocks and `<invoke>` XML tags) to trigger unauthorized operations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- **Obfuscated Encodings**: Evasion attempts utilizing Base64 encoding, ROT13 substitution, and Cyrillic homoglyphs to bypass static keyword filters [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Unicode Directionality and Role-Play**: Adversarial prompts leveraging right-to-left override characters and persona role-playing directives to induce policy violations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].

These automated checks support bounded triage execution as described in [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) and align with defensive controls defined in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).

# References
- [Submission Analyser Repository](https://github.com/aaif/submission-analyser)

proposed_concept.title: Linux Kernel Tracing Technologies Comparison
proposed_concept.description: Comparative assessment of primary Linux kernel tracing frameworks—LTTng, perf, and FTrace—evaluating architecture, overhead, and AAIF capability dimensions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Linux kernel tracing ecosystem is anchored by three primary frameworks: LTTng, perf, and FTrace[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. The [Working Group Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) evaluated these technologies across runtime overhead, data extraction mechanics, architectural design, and AAIF capability dimensions to establish architectural fit and identify universal capability gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].

# Architecture / Specification
Each framework exhibits distinct architectural tradeoffs across data acquisition, buffering, and extraction pipelines[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]:

- **[LTTng](../resources/lttng-kernel.md)**: Maintained by EfficiOS Inc. (initial release 2006, 2.0 in 2012), LTTng utilizes out-of-tree kernel modules (`lttng-modules`) and userspace daemons (`lttng-tools`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. It features lock-free per-CPU ring buffers extracted via kernel splice into standardized [Common Trace Format (CTF)](../resources/common-trace-format.md) binary payloads, achieving 50–150 ns probe latency when enabled with ~0 ns disabled overhead[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. Together with [LTTng-UST](../resources/lttng-ust.md), it provides unified kernel-userspace correlation visualized in [Trace Compass](../resources/trace-compass.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **[perf](../resources/linux-perf.md)**: Maintained in-tree by the kernel community since Linux 2.6.31 (2009), perf integrates hardware PMU counter sampling and `perf_events` with per-event mmap buffers shared directly with userspace[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. While requiring only `linux-tools`, it incurs 100–300 ns enabled probe latency and writes to proprietary `perf.data` files analyzed via `perf report`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **[FTrace](../resources/ftrace.md)**: Maintained in-tree by Steven Rostedt since Linux 2.6.27 (2008), FTrace provides zero-dependency kernel instrumentation built directly into `tracefs` and `trace-cmd`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. It offers static-branch disabled latency (1–3 ns) and low enabled latency (40–100 ns) using per-CPU lock-free buffers emitting plain text or `.dat` outputs, though it lacks native userspace tracing and hardware counter support[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].

# References
- [LTTng Kernel Tracing](../resources/lttng-kernel.md)
- [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md)
- [FTrace Architecture](../resources/ftrace.md)
- [Common Trace Format](../resources/common-trace-format.md)
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions agent utilizing Copilot inference, dry-run canary pipelines, and an adversarial injection test suite to triage project submissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated GitHub Actions agent that triages project proposals, validates schema compliance, and detects malicious prompt injections in untrusted community submissions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61]. Operating in headless automated pipelines, the analyser combines model-assisted evaluation with strict delimiter isolation and regression test suites designed to resist adversarial inputs targeting agent harnesses[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].

# Architecture / Specification
The analyser incorporates a comprehensive test fixture suite (`tests/fixtures/injections/`) specifically targeting common adversarial jailbreak and prompt manipulation vectors[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea][^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61]:

- **Delimiter Forging**: Validating that closing delimiters (such as `</untrusted-issue>`) followed by forged system prompt tags cannot trick the parser into executing attacker instructions or bypassing security scans[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61].
- **Authority and Urgency Simulation**: Resisting social engineering payloads that masquerade as repository owners, foundation security teams, or model vendors to mandate priority overrides, suppress injection alerts, or exfiltrate configuration[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31].
- **Credential and Environment Exfiltration**: Defending against exfiltration vectors attempting to reflect sensitive runtime variables (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`) via issue summaries, egress webhooks, or obfuscated base64 output payloads[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].
- **Payload Obfuscation and Polyglots**: Ensuring hidden markdown comments, collapsed HTML details blocks, and inline script hooks do not bypass input sanitization or trigger unintended side effects during intake analysis[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].

# References
- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)
- [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md)
- [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions agent utilizing Copilot inference, cross-repository workflow dispatch, and prompt-isolated evaluation to audit issue submissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser (`flue-issue-analyst`) is a headless GitHub Actions agent that evaluates issue submissions, drafts comprehensive triage reports into maintainer-accessible Google Docs, and posts summaries to Discord without write permissions to the monitored repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. Built on the Flue 2.0 framework, it isolates untrusted public input from execution privileges, strictly treating external issue contents as data rather than instructions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# Architecture / Specification
The analyzer operates across explicit security boundaries to minimize credential exposure and resist adversarial manipulation:

- **Cross-Repository Trust Boundary**: The analyzer runs in a dedicated private repository (`aaif/flue-issue-analyst`) distinct from public target repositories such as `aaif/project-proposals` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. Target repositories trigger analysis via a `workflow_dispatch` action using `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, a fine-grained personal access token granted `Actions: write` only [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]. Because `repository_dispatch` would mandate `Contents: write` (allowing arbitrary code modifications to the analyst's own workflow scripts), the narrower `Actions: write` scope is enforced [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Credential Isolation and Least Privilege**: The agent environment holds access credentials for GitHub Copilot, Google Docs (`GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`), and Discord webhooks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. All credentials are kept internal to runtime tool implementations (`analyze_and_publish`) and remain inaccessible to model context or shell sessions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. The agent cannot modify codebase files, make unauthorized network requests, or push commits to target repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Public issue titles, bodies, and comments are treated as untrusted data placed within nonce-delimited data blocks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. If adversarial manipulation is detected, the agent flags `injectionSuspected: true` and logs the vector in `injectionNotes` instead of executing conflicting directives [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Immutable CI and Dry-Run Verification**: Offline verification in CI runs entirely without secrets, pinning third-party GitHub Actions to immutable full commit SHAs to prevent supply chain substitution attacks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926]. In-memory fake provider execution (`FLUE_FAUX=1`) validates skill frontmatter schemas and exit statuses prior to deployment [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].

# References
- `../skills/issue-analysis.md`
- `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`
- `../policies/project-proposal-process.md`

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular Flue 2.0 skill providing automated GitHub issue analysis, reference corpus retrieval, and prompt injection reporting.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis skill is a modular capability package within Flue 2.0 that automates triage, technical risk assessment, and policy compliance verification for incoming GitHub issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. It executes inside the `submission-analyser` agent harness, extracting relevant architectural precedents from a local reference corpus to inform project-specific evaluations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill implements structured data retrieval, prompt isolation, and telemetry reporting:

- **Reference Corpus Retrieval**: The skill maintains a library of historical hand-written analyses in a local directory [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. Each analysis defines frontmatter metadata including `issue-number`, `date`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `tags`, and `components` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. The retrieval layer scans frontmatter across the corpus, dynamically selects the 3 to 5 most relevant reference cases using tag and component matching, and loads their full contents into context to guide decision making [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Injection Isolation and Telemetry**: The skill enforces strict prompt containment by isolating untrusted input from system instructions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. When an issue body attempts prompt override or jailbreaking, the model is instructed to mark `injectionSuspected: true` and record the incident details in `injectionNotes` while continuing to evaluate any genuine technical elements [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Tool Invocation Contract**: The skill operates via a single consolidated tool invocation (`analyze_and_publish`), enforcing a read-only stance that forbids direct file writes, environment variable inspections, or outbound network calls outside configured publishing endpoints [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# References
- `../resources/submission-analyser.md`
- `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`

mutations.rationale: Expand the Linux driver tracing reference architecture with dynamic debug mechanisms, TRACE_EVENT integration, and subsystem observability interfaces.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Linux device driver instrumentation covering dev_dbg, dynamic debug (dyndbg), TRACE_EVENT macros, and debugfs interfaces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Linux Driver Tracing provides the foundational observability and debugging architecture for device drivers across the Linux kernel subsystem layer [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. Positioned between generic kernel tracing mechanisms and specialized hardware diagnostics, it details how developers instrument driver code and how administrators dynamically control trace event streams at runtime without recompilation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# Architecture / Specification
The driver tracing architecture spans structured logging, dynamic call-site modification, and custom tracepoint infrastructure:

- **Structured Device Logging**: Drivers implement structured logging through kernel macros (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_err`, `dev_warn`) that bind device context and driver identification directly to log entries routed through `printk` and the kernel ring buffer [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: When built with `CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG=y`, debug statements (`dev_dbg`, `pr_debug`) introduce zero runtime overhead until dynamically enabled via `/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. Call sites can be queried and enabled per module, file, function, line number, or kernel boot parameter [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Custom `TRACE_EVENT()` Macros**: Drivers define high-performance, structured tracepoints using `TRACE_EVENT()` headers exported to `tracefs` under `/sys/kernel/tracing/events/` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. These tracepoints integrate with kernel tooling including `perf` and `trace-cmd` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Subsystem-Specific Tracers and Interfaces**: Subsystem diagnostics extend through specialized tools such as `usbmon` for USB request block inspection, `blktrace` for block I/O profiling, and `devcoredump` for post-mortem driver crash capture [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# References
- `linux-tracing-comparison.md`
- `ftrace.md`
- `linux-perf.md`

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions workflow agent analyzing repository issues via Copilot inference and publishing reports to Google Docs and Discord without repo write permissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated, headless GitHub Actions agent designed to process public or private repository issues, execute analysis pipelines using multi-vendor language models brokered through GitHub Copilot, and output formatted assessments to external platforms such as Google Docs and Discord [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. Built to inspect submissions across Foundation repositories without human intervention, it operates under a strictly scoped privilege boundary to mitigate prompt injection and unauthorized repository tampering [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-Repository Invocation and Permissions
The workflow relies exclusively on the `workflow_dispatch` trigger to enable cross-repository operations, where upstream repositories run lightweight dispatcher actions that target the centralized tooling repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. This dispatch model prevents event confusion and ensures uniform execution logic across projects. Execution concurrency is serialized using composite keys based on the target repository and issue number [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

To neutralize prompt injection risks inherent in parsing untrusted issue text with LLMs possessing shell access, the workflow enforces a strict privilege minimization model [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]:
- `contents: read`: Authorizes checking out workflow assets without allowing modifications to source files or workflow definitions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- `copilot-requests: write`: Grants access to make inference requests against GitHub Copilot endpoints billed to the repository organization [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- No `issues: write`: Excludes repository write tokens entirely, eliminating the vector where untrusted prompt content coerces the agent into modifying repository files or commenting maliciously back onto GitHub [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

## Copilot Authentication and Inference
Model inference is conducted exclusively through the GitHub Copilot provider, eliminating third-party API secret maintenance [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]:
- **Token Exchange**: Inference endpoints do not accept raw Personal Access Tokens (PATs) or default Actions server-to-server tokens as bearer credentials [^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]. The runtime exchanges the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (bearing `copilot-requests: write`) via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` for a short-lived session token with appropriate editor headers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].
- **Model Redundancy**: Specifiers require a `<provider-id>/<model-id>` syntax (e.g., `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]. Operational configuration defines a primary model alongside a multi-vendor fallback (e.g., `github-copilot/gpt-5.4`), both served through the unified Copilot entitlement [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- **Diagnostic Probing**: Diagnostic workflows (`probe-copilot.yml`) provide out-of-band verification of token entitlement and endpoint resolution without initiating billable inference [^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73].

## External Delivery Pipeline
The agent delivers structured outputs to out-of-band channels via distinct credentials [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]:
- `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID`: Facilitates publishing formatted assessment documents to a secure Google Drive repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`: Transmits notifications and summary links into moderation and review channels [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- Bot authors are identified and skipped prior to publishing to avoid automated recursive analysis loops [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

# References
- Related guidelines: [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)
- Operational patterns: [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, full-stack observability layers, and audit primitives for AI agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry models, runtime trace formats, semantic conventions, and audit mechanisms across agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. The group develops specifications addressing the full agent execution lifecycle, correlating high-level conversational and reasoning state with underlying infrastructure, system calls, and network boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Focus Groups
The working group organizes technical workstreams into specialized focus groups to evaluate protocol boundaries and execution state [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]:
- **Protocols and Primitives**: Evaluates data interchange standards, Merkle link graphs for tamper-evident event chains, network architecture mapping, and protocol-level tracing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **State, Context, and Reasoning**: Focuses on agent context retention, session identification, replay capabilities, dynamic verification rules, and cognitive state tracing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

## Full-Stack Observability Model
The working group examines observability requirements across a multi-layer stack [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]:
- Identifies limitations in application-centric tracing frameworks (such as OpenTelemetry), which predominantly capture Layer 5 application events while leaving lower system, runtime, and hardware accelerator layers unobserved [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- Analyzes cross-layer telemetry correlation, including per-field data encryption, semantic convention standardization for agent behavior, and dynamic compliance verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- Investigates primitives such as the Agent Action Capsule to provide structured, verifiable snapshots of agent intent and runtime side effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# References
- Specifications: [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), [Trace](../standards/trace.md)
- Telemetry models: [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md), [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)
- Working groups: [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
