proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, cross-boundary observability, and tamper-evident audit records for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral specifications, reference architectures, and telemetry conventions for monitoring, profiling, and auditing agentic AI workloads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2]. Rather than functioning as an insular standards body, the working group serves as an active coordination forum aligning telemetry models across OpenTelemetry GenAI, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and AGNTCY [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

Its technical agenda addresses full-stack execution tracking—spanning high-level agent reasoning turns down to kernel, userspace, and hardware dispatch—alongside verifiable compliance artifacts required for regulatory audits and dispute resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives across several focus areas:

- **Agent Behavior Tracing**: Developing the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to define schema standards for agent turn boundaries, causal execution links, and inter-agent communication boundaries.
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry**: Evaluating and standardizing telemetry propagation across CLI, MCP server, and containerized runtime boundaries in alignment with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) and [Context Forge](../resources/context-forge.md).
- **Safety, Compliance, and Auditability**: Establishing evidence requirements for legal and regulatory scrutiny (such as Use Case E4), mandating tamper-evident execution histories via Merkle-chained records, RFC 3161 timestamps, WORM storage, and evidence-strength gradations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Liaison Management**: Maintaining a cross-WG and external standards liaison roster to coordinate regularly with internal groups like the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-15**: Working group charter formally approved internally [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-04-21**: Charter transitioned from draft status and submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for review [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-06 to 2026-07**: Monthly progress reporting formalized under working group leadership [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-24].
- **2026-07**: Added Use Case E4 (Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution) to working documents to establish cryptographic trace integrity requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

mutations.rationale: Expand specification requirements to incorporate tamper-evident audit and dispute resolution needs (Use Case E4), including Merkle chaining, cryptographic timestamps, and evidence grading.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and behavioral trace specification defining agent turn boundaries, causal execution links, and tamper-evident audit evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification defining standardized telemetry schemas, event structures, and causal lineage records emitted across autonomous AI agent executions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. Developed under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model bridges runtime operational tracing with high-assurance tamper-evident evidence needed for regulatory compliance and dispute resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

By capturing structured execution turns, tool invocations, and governance checkpoint evaluations, the model enables external observers to reconstruct both agent reasoning intentions and concrete execution receipts.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes requirements across operational and compliance tiers:

- **Turn Boundaries and Causal Lineage**: Represents prompt ingestion, reasoning cycles, tool invocations, and delegation boundaries as a directed acyclic graph maintaining explicit parent-child causal context.
- **Declared vs. Observed Linkage**: Correlates the intent expressed in model tool-call payloads against verified execution outcomes captured at underlying runtime boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Tamper-Evident Evidence Architecture (Use Case E4)**: Formulates structural controls for regulatory auditability and legal proceedings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]:
  - **Merkle-Chained Records**: Sequentially binds execution records into signed hash chains to prevent post-hoc reordering, injection, or deletion.
  - **Cryptographic Timestamps**: Integrates RFC 3161 trusted timestamp tokens to provide non-repudiable proof of execution timing.
  - **WORM Storage Integration**: Guarantees trace serialization compatibility with write-once-read-many retention stores.
  - **Evidence-Grade Classification**: Incorporates appraisal ladders (ranging from declared outputs to anchored evidence) to validate compliance with regulatory standards such as the EU AI Act [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Attribution and Sign-Off Binding**: Links human approvals to immutable snapshots of proposed agent execution payloads, integrating with the [approval checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) and [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07**: Expanded to integrate Use Case E4 ("Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution") in the Safety and Compliance track, establishing cryptographic integrity constraints beyond standard telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

mutations.rationale: Align action record definition with post-hoc third-party verifiability models and tamper-evident dispute resolution requirements.

proposed_concept.title: Action Record
proposed_concept.description: Tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record of a single consequential action taken by an AI agent.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An action record is a tamper-evident, content-private, and independently verifiable data artifact certifying a single consequential action executed by an AI agent [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. In contrast to comprehensive session traces that record multi-turn dialogues and reasoning paths, an action record isolates an atomic state transition, external tool execution, or contractual commitment performed across an execution boundary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].

It serves as a core primitive for zero-trust dispute resolution, allowing auditors, courts, or external counterparties to verify the integrity and provenance of a reported action without relying on the credibility of the host reporting it [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
Action records function as an orthogonal accountability primitive operating beneath full-session telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23]:

- **Third-Party Verifiability**: Provides portable verification primitives (such as `action_ref` or anchored hash references) that allow third-party validation without exposing proprietary context or sensitive execution payloads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].
- **Cryptographic Provenance**: Employs Merkle chaining, cryptographic signatures, and RFC 3161 timestamps to establish non-repudiation and prevent retroactive tampering [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Declared vs. Observed Linkage**: Binds the agent's declared action intent directly to the cryptographic receipt observed at the runtime or network boundary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Trace Integration**: Acts as an anchorable leaf node within the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to support evidence-grade accountability ladders.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07**: Surveyed alongside post-hoc verifiability frameworks (e.g., `action_ref`) and established as a foundational primitive for Use Case E4 audit and dispute resolution in the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the six-stage intake, automated compliance review, TC engagement bar, and LFX voting process for AAIF project proposals.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Project Proposal Process is the operational workflow through which software projects, libraries, and specifications are submitted, evaluated, approved, and onboarded into the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Governed by the Technical Committee in coordination with the Governing Board, the process implements the entry rules set out in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) through an asynchronous, offline-first intake pipeline[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

The procedure is designed around an engagement bar rather than requiring dedicated single champions, ensuring broad Technical Committee consensus and early risk identification before advancing to a formal admission vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Roles and Responsibilities
The process assigns responsibilities across key governance actors[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:
- **Project Submitter**: Files the proposal, addresses technical inquiries on the GitHub tracking issue, conducts optional presentations, and completes contributor agreements.
- **CTO**: Oversees Step 1 intake triage, runs initial smoke tests alongside the intake agent, prepares committee briefs, and handles Q&A extension requests.
- **Intake Agent**: Automated bot executing public technical compliance checks on the proposal issue and delivering advisory compliance reviews to private Technical Committee channels.
- **TC Chairs**: Provide oversight during triage and recruit an on-demand TC Supporter if the proposal stalls at the engagement bar.
- **TC Supporter (On-Demand)**: A [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) member assigned only when baseline committee engagement is unmet, responsible for championing the proposal through a reset Q&A window.
- **Technical Committee**: Evaluates proposal architecture, asks questions during the public Q&A window, and casts votes on technical merit and initial lifecycle stage.
- **Governing Board**: Votes on budget allocation, legal exposure, and organizational alignment.
- **LF PMO, Legal, and IT**: Manage asynchronous paperwork, contribution agreements, charter drafting, and technical repository onboarding.

## Six-Stage Intake Workflow
The intake pipeline operates primarily offline and asynchronously across six sequential steps and one parallel track[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:
1. **Initial Intake**: The project proposal is submitted via GitHub. The Intake Agent performs static compliance and licensing checks, alerting the CTO and TC Chairs. The CTO verifies completeness and strategic fit.
2. **TC Q&A Window**: A time-boxed asynchronous review window on GitHub where TC members review the proposal. The proposal must satisfy the engagement bar (a mandatory quorum of distinct TC member interactions) to advance. An optional live presentation may be scheduled upon TC request. If the engagement bar is unmet, TC Chairs appoint an on-demand supporter or reject the proposal.
- **Contributor Paperwork (Parallel Track)**: Concurrently with Step 2, submitters complete Linux Foundation contributor documentation via LF PMO.
3. **TC Vote**: The Technical Committee votes asynchronously via LFX Vote to approve project admission and assign its initial lifecycle stage.
4. **GB Approval**: The Governing Board votes via LFX Vote to authorize organizational resource commitments and legal acceptance.
5. **LF Legal Formation**: LF Legal coordinates signing of technical charters, IP transfers, and contribution agreements via DocuSign.
6. **Technical Onboarding**: LF IT transfers repositories, configures access controls, and provisions foundation CI/CD infrastructure.

# Lifecycle History
Version 0.3 of the operating procedure took effect on August 28, 2026, codifying intake agent automation, replacing single-champion requirements with the engagement bar, and formalizing LFX Vote tooling[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining technical project admission requirements, the Sandbox, Growth, and Graduated lifecycle stages, and annual review cycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy defines the official maturity tiers, progression milestones, and governance expectations for open-source initiatives hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]. It establishes clear entry gates, operational requirements, and graduation criteria administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

Projects advance through defined lifecycle stages based on technical maturity, community diversity, open governance compliance, and production adoption[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Lifecycle Stages
The policy defines graduated levels of maturity[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]:
- **Sandbox**: Entry stage for early-stage, experimental, or emerging open-source technologies aligned with the foundation's mission. Provides a collaborative home under open governance with minimal adoption prerequisites.
- **Incubating / Growth**: Maturing projects demonstrating active development, multi-organization contribution, stable release cadences, and documented ecosystem evaluation.
- **Graduated**: Highest maturity stage reserved for foundational, production-proven technologies exhibiting robust multi-vendor governance, stringent security practices, and sustained adoption.

## Stage Transitions and Governance
Stage progression requires formal review and voting by the Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]:
- **Admission**: New projects enter at either Sandbox or Growth depending on existing community traction and code maturity.
- **Growth Criteria**: Stricter criteria require demonstrated neutral governance, cross-vendor maintainer distribution, and documented real-world adoption.
- **Annual Review**: Hosted projects undergo recurring reviews by the Technical Committee to ensure ongoing alignment, healthy maintenance, and progression readiness.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy schema, evidentiary standard, and empirical inventory categorizing production agentic workflows into deterministic and model-driven activities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification framework provides a taxonomy schema, evidentiary scoring standard, and empirical catalog of production agentic workflows maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32]. It standardizes how enterprise and open-source agentic deployments are decomposed into composable execution units, distinguishing deterministic components from autonomous cognitive reasoning[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

The working group aligns all use case models with standard [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) by designating core functional execution units as activities rather than steps[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Activity-Based Workflow Decomposition
Workflows are structured into distinct activities categorized by their execution mechanism[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32]:
- **Model-Driven Activities**: Unbounded or nondeterministic tasks relying on language model inference, such as context summarization, natural language reasoning, or heuristic tool selection.
- **Deterministic Activities**: Rule-based, repeatable operations such as schema validation, cryptographic policy enforcement, or transactional database commits.

By standardizing on activity terminology across the use-case schema (`schema-agentic-use-cases.md`) and inventory (`use-case-inventory.md`), the framework enables seamless mapping between empirical production patterns and formal workflow reference architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized structure, metadata headers, and section requirements for authoring AAIF workflow reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Template defines the canonical authoring structure and documentation standards for reference architectures published by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c1c1cdc015db-05940fd8]. It ensures that architectural guidance across the foundation is structured around clear practitioner jobs, explicit boundary contracts, and verifiable design invariants[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c1c1cdc015db-05940fd8].

The template enforces a user-centric documentation philosophy where practitioners can immediately evaluate whether an architecture answers their specific operational problem before diving into implementation mechanics[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c1c1cdc015db-05940fd8].

# Architecture / Specification

## Required Metadata Headers
Every reference architecture document begins with a standardized metadata header defining its high-level scope[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c1c1cdc015db-05940fd8]:
- **The job it serves**: The recurring practitioner need answered plainly.
- **Built from patterns**: Composed patterns referenced from the foundation pattern catalog.
- **Requires capabilities**: Distinct capability roles necessary to implement the architecture.
- **Audience**: Builders, reviewers, and stakeholders benefiting from the architecture.

## Canonical Structural Sections
Architectures adhering to the template must provide the following sections[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c1c1cdc015db-05940fd8]:
1. **Status**: Lifecycle status (Draft, Proposed, Approved) and decision record links.
2. **Purpose**: Plain-language description of the job and reading paths routing technical versus executive readers.
3. **Is this your architecture? (Checklist)**: Use-case routing questions answerable without prior implementation knowledge or model assumptions.
4. **Variants**: Allowable additions or subtractions of components that preserve underlying architectural invariants.
5. **Structure**: Capability-level block diagram and required-capabilities table focusing on data contracts crossing interface boundaries.
6. **Pattern Composition**: How component design patterns combine to enforce end-to-end guarantees.
7. **The Agent and Workflow-Control Boundary**: Clear delineation separating orchestrator control logic from autonomous agent loops.
8. **Choosing Deterministic and Model-Driven Activities**: Decision criteria partitioning deterministic policy gates from nondeterministic model inference.
9. **Exit States**: Complete taxonomy of terminal and intermediate execution states.
10. **Worked Scenario**: Concrete walk-through illustrating boundary crossings and failure handling.
11. **Composition Considerations & Out of Scope**: Architectural constraints, non-goals, and boundary limitations.
12. **Validation Record & Open Questions**: Empirical verification status and unresolved design items.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern enforcing authorization and attribution at protected boundaries by separating probabilistic agent proposal from workflow-controlled execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Proposal/Execution Split is an architectural pattern that enforces authorization and attribution at protected-effect boundaries by isolating probabilistic agent proposal from deterministic execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950] In production enterprise environments, agent actions carry risk exposure, audit exposure, and regulatory accountability requirements that cannot be fulfilled if a probabilistic model both decides and acts directly.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern establishes three distinct roles and separate systems of record across the execution lifecycle:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]

1. **Proposer (Agent)**: Generates candidate intent as immutable structured data, not an executable side-effect.
2. **Authorization Authority (Gate)**: Evaluates whether the exact proposed payload may proceed against policy or human oversight.
3. **Executor (System)**: A workflow-controlled component that executes the authorized payload without allowing the agent to trigger the action directly.

### Invariants

- The proposal is immutable data; the agent cannot directly invoke the executor.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]
- The authorization decision attaches strictly to the exact proposal payload (typically verified by content hash).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]
- Authorization gates must fail closed on expiration, timeout, or policy evaluation error.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]
- Workflow execution must be idempotent to prevent duplicate side-effects on retry.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]

# Related Patterns

This pattern is foundational to [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md), and coordinates directly with [Human Approval Gate](./human-approval-gate.md) and [Durable Wait](./durable-wait.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary of modular workflow building blocks, execution states, and boundary contracts for agentic AI orchestration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Workflow Primitives define the foundational vocabulary and execution building blocks for structured agentic AI workflows and orchestration systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]

# Architecture / Specification

### Foundational Concepts

- **Activity**: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f] This term replaces earlier usages of "Workflow Step" and "Workflow Task" to prevent circularity with the Workflow definition.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]
- **Workflow**: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome, composed of one or more activities, their relationships, and execution logic.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Workflow Execution**: A runtime instance of a workflow definition, maintaining its own execution state and lifecycle independently of concurrent instances.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Workflow State**: The information representing the current condition and execution progress of a workflow execution at a specific point in time.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Workflow Context**: The shared information available to workflow participants during execution, including inputs, shared metadata, history, and external references.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]

### Execution and Control

- **Control Flow**: The logic determining execution order, branching, parallelism, and synchronization of activities.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Trigger**: An event, condition, schedule, or signal initiating or advancing workflow execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Durability**: The capability of preserving execution state across system failures or interruptions without loss of progress.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Determinism**: The property whereby identical inputs, execution state, and history produce consistent execution behavior.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]

# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical working group establishing benchmarks, evaluation standards, and engineering practices to measure and improve AI agent accuracy and reliability.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group is chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]

### Key Deliverables

- **D2 (Gap Analysis and Survey Support)**: Operational survey specification gathering comparative pain-point and prioritization signals from practitioners running agent systems in production.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, ARWG consolidated review feedback across deliverable tracks, opened survey specification PR #9 for structured feedback, and queued initial D1 terminology batches for cross-WG alignment.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]

# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF working body arbitrating shared agentic AI terminology, maintaining the industry landscape, and establishing reconciled definitions across all technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

### Operating Process

Terminology candidates undergo a structured review process across participating working groups, followed by definition drafting and domain editor reconciliation:

- Domain syncs evaluate candidate terms into kept, culled, or debated statuses.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- Accepted terms advance to formal definition pull requests with explicit relationship modeling across adjacent terms.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- Cross-workgroup domain editors review terms to ensure vendor-neutral phrasing and cross-domain coherence.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the workstream evaluated 53 candidate terms across three review syncs, keeping 37 terms, culling 15, and holding multi-agent misdirection for debate.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] PR #37 merged the formal definition for Harness, while definition PRs advanced for terms including Human in the Loop, Meta-harness, and Identity & Trust vocabulary.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] In addition, Leonardo Galesky joined to represent [Agentic Commerce](./agentic-commerce.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body establishing capability maps, gap analyses, and protocol architectures across commercial agent interactions, automated transactions, and post-purchase lifecycles.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Deliverables

- **Deliverable 1 (Agentic Commerce Capability Map)**: Comprehensive architectural mapping of commercial agent capabilities, spanning pre-purchase inquiry through post-purchase settlement.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
  - **Post-Purchase Slice (P1–P7)**: Capability proposals covering eligibility inquiry, remedy negotiation, buyer authorization and consent evidence, state-change execution signals, evidence binding, dispute claims, and adjustment ledgers.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
  - **Evidence and Auditability Contract**: A proposed 8-field bounded verdict envelope linking verification records with witness scopes, signatures, and evidence fingerprints.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
- **Deliverable 2 (Gap Analysis)**: Identification of standardization and protocol coverage gaps across existing specifications including UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]

# Lifecycle History

In August and September 2026, initial post-purchase capability proposals were introduced in PR #6 to address expertise gaps identified earlier in the workgroup.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6] Working group participation in cross-cutting taxonomy alignment expanded with Leonardo Galesky representing the group in the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and behavioral trace specification defining agent turn boundaries, causal execution links, and multi-trace session correlation across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and behavioral trace specification defining how agent turn boundaries, causal execution links, and session continuity are recorded across independent agent runtimes and provider APIs. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model establishes a vendor-neutral schema for tracking multi-turn interactions, tool executions, and pause/resume lifecycle transitions without mandating artificial session-long spans.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification addresses agent execution through structured baseline captures and correlation mechanics across distinct operational layers:

- **Baseline Runtime Validation**: Evaluates agent behavior across distinct runtimes, such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and independent agent SDKs, distinguishing between instrumentation gaps, unsupported runtime capabilities, documentation guidance, and semantic model requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Session and Turn Continuity**: Connects completed conversation turns across independent distributed traces without depending on an unbroken parent span [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]. Native session identifiers, conversation threads, and pause/resume lifecycle states are correlated using contextual trace linking, allowing agents to resume historical tasks after process restarts while preserving causal lineage [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].
- **Provider API and Integration Fixtures**: Defines standardized test fixtures and reproducible harness examples covering streaming completions, provider errors, tool-call requests, and token usage accounting [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]. Telemetry semantics explicitly distinguish between a provider emitting a tool invocation request and the subsequent client-side execution of that tool [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

# Lifecycle History
The model's development is structured under a nine-task execution plan coordinated by the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]. Key implementation phases include establishing comparative runtime baselines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40], implementing cross-trace session continuity verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43], and packaging portable fixtures to facilitate community extensions across diverse model providers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Resource Discovery
proposed_concept.description: Specification and observability framework for discovering, evaluating, and admitting AI skills and resources through policy gateways and agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) is an open specification and protocol observability framework for dynamically discovering, verifying, and admitting agent skills, tools, and endpoints across policy enforcement boundaries. By defining telemetry across discovery, provenance, governance, and policy evaluation phases, ARD allows agent gateways and execution environments to make verifiable admission decisions and correlate admitted capabilities with subsequent skill execution.

# Architecture / Specification
The ARD lifecycle instrumentation framework standardizes telemetry and state evaluation across five sequential stages [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]:

1. **Discovery**: Querying and locating candidate agent resources, endpoints, and tool packages.
2. **Provenance**: Validating origin manifests, signatures, and publisher attestation records.
3. **Governance**: Evaluating capabilities against local policy engines and organizational constraints.
4. **Trust**: Appraising cryptographic assertions, delegation credentials, and trust scores.
5. **Decision**: Emitting an admission determination, resulting either in capability enablement or quarantine.

Observability data across these stages is exported via standard [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) (OTLP) pipelines using the experimental `ard.*` namespace [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]. To maintain end-to-end lineage, admission records propagate W3C Trace Context headers into runtime environments such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) to correlate admitted skills with downstream execution spans (`gen_ai.skill.*`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]. Quarantined or rejected capabilities record evaluation decisions without generating synthetic execution spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

# Lifecycle History
Tracking under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), an active proof of concept validates ARD lifecycle telemetry across Agent Gateway and Goose, testing cross-agent portability and standard OTLP JSON export compatibility [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practitioner guide and static-analysis rule catalog defining defensive controls, failure patterns, and architectural mitigations across agent lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide is a comprehensive practitioner resource and static-analysis rule framework detailing defensive controls, failure patterns, and architectural mitigations for deploying AI agents in high-consequence environments. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline translates high-level security principles into actionable implementation checklists and machine-evaluable rules for static analysis tools.

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline synthesizes defensive patterns across core architectural boundaries:

- **Defensive Boundary Controls**: Establishes mandatory containment strategies including out-of-band [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) capabilities, memory isolation boundaries, and least-privilege tool execution interfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Static Analysis Rule Conversion**: Translates textual best practice guidelines into machine-actionable static analysis rules, facilitating automated validation of agent SDKs and configurations against known vulnerability patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Scope Demarcation**: Specifically focuses on runtime execution security, threat mitigation, and containment boundaries; identity delegation, cryptographic credential handoffs, and trust arbitration are scoped out of the initial release to align with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
The working group established an initial version freeze to release the core guideline as its first major deliverable, accompanied by a static-analysis rule set and comparative assessments against major cloud provider agent SDKs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation tasked with establishing threat models, practical security guidelines, architectural design patterns, and automated evaluation rules for agentic systems. The working group coordinates defensive architectures, analyzes vulnerability vectors across agent tool-use and memory tiers, and conducts cross-group security reviews across foundation workstreams.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output across four primary active workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]:

- **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Developing practitioner guides and static-analysis rules evaluating agent SDKs against defensive criteria, scoped to complement identity standards defined by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curating operational patterns for agent safety and control, including [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) architectural patterns and upcoming cognitive memory protection models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Coordinating systemic security reviews and alignment surveys across Foundation groups including Observability, Governance, Agentic Commerce, and Accuracy and Reliability [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Taxonomy and Vocabulary**: Formalizing standardized definitions for security and privacy concepts in coordination with the broader foundation landscape effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group froze the initial draft of its Security Best Practices document for release as its inaugural public deliverable, expanded its pattern catalog with formal kill-switch patterns, and launched cross-working group review outreach [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation brand guidelines specify visual identity rules, typographic constraints, token management, and asset usage standards across foundation repositories, reports, and public media [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Architecture / Specification
## Design System and Token Architecture
All human-facing layouts, reports, and documents consume tokens extracted from the centralized design bundle at `design/aaif-design-system.html` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]:
- **Color System and Accents**: The primary accent color is ink black (`--accent: var(--ink)`). Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) provide internal component accents, with coral designated as `--spec-8` rather than an organizational brand color [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Page grounds use `--paper`, section banding uses `--paper-2`, and tinted panels use `--paper-3` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Surfaces and Dark Mode**: The system defines two explicit surfaces: white editorial and black plate [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Automated dark mode or `prefers-color-scheme` CSS blocks are strictly prohibited; visual elements must respect designer-selected surface polarity [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Depth and Corner Geometry**: Visual presentation remains flat without drop shadows [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Depth is established via 1px hairlines and background tints. Structural containers such as cards, tables, and chips remain square (`border-radius: 0`), whereas badges and buttons retain `--radius-pill` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Typographic Hierarchy
- **Typeface**: Instrument Sans (OFL) is the sole typography standard across display, headings, and body copy in weights 400, 500, 600, and 700 [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Headings and Mono**: Standard display headings use weight 500 with tracking set to `-0.02em` and line height between 1.05 and 1.15 [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Monospace typography is restricted strictly to technical metadata, commit IDs, and eyebrows, and must never be applied to body copy [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Asset and Motif Constraints
- **Official Mark**: Official vector marks (`aaif-mark.svg`, `aaif-mark-square.svg`, `aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be used verbatim, permitting only fill color modifications without geometry alteration [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Agent Motif**: The agent motif is restricted to empty states, loading sequences, event graphics, and dividers [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. It is explicitly prohibited on official governance, Technical Committee, board, or press deliverables [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry models, causal trace specifications, and cross-boundary execution records for agentic software stacks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification
## Focus Groups and Initiatives
- **Primitives and Protocol Observability**: Led by Trace, this focus group defines core tracing primitives and expands observability downward below L7 into network and kernel syscall layers to achieve end-to-end execution tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent State Context and Reasoning**: Focus group developing behavioral trace representations for multi-turn reasoning and runtime context changes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent Action Capsule Exploration**: Reviewing cryptographic proof capsules demonstrating verifiable dispatch logging, policy allowance enforcement, and ledger-based execution reconstruction [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

## Coordination and Liaisons
Per WG liaison tracking, formal coordination is maintained across internal and external bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]:
- **External Liaisons**: OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, Agent Trace (`agent-trace.dev`), Monocle, and AGNTCY [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **Internal Touchpoints**: Coordination with the `../governance/technical-committee.md`, `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`, and `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

proposed_concept.title: Single Agent with Enforceable Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate between an agent proposal and external system publication.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The single-agent human approval reference architecture establishes an enforceable, verifiable boundary separating autonomous agent proposal generation from publication or state mutation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification
## Boundary Architecture
The architecture decouples the agent execution lifecycle using core control patterns:
1. **Proposal Phase**: The agent completes task execution in an unprivileged runtime, emitting a structured, immutable candidate output [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]. See `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`.
2. **Approval Gate**: Execution enters an enforced wait state requiring an authenticated human operator to review and sign the proposed state change [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]. See `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`.
3. **Publication Phase**: Upon explicit authorization, an execution runner publishes the payload to target production environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

## Validated Scenarios
The pattern is validated against real-world production use cases in the Use Case Inventory [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:
- **FAQ and Knowledge-Base Updates**: Autonomous drafting of support articles held at an approval boundary prior to knowledge-base publishing [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Release Notes Generation**: Automated synthesis of code commits and ticket metadata into draft release notes requiring engineering maintainer sign-off [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Listing Description Updates**: Generation of commercial catalog entries gated by human lead authorization before public catalog indexation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Its focus centers on enabling agents to be discovered across platforms, prove their provenance, declare whom they act for, verify human approvals, and operate securely across trust domains[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Architecture / Specification
## Leadership and Governance
The working group is led by appointed chairs serving terms from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]:
- **Chair:** Grant Miller (IBM)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Co-Chair:** Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

## Working Group Breakouts
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into three dedicated breakout tracks[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases:** Grounds identity and trust requirements in real-world enterprise and consumer scenarios, coordinated by Wei Chen[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Reference Architecture:** Models actors, trust relationships, architectural components, and interoperability gaps for delegated agent authority, coordinated by Brian Malone[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Taxonomy Coordination:** Develops identity and trust terminology and aligns definitions with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), liaised by Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

## External and Referenced Prior Work
The group's investigations evaluate several established industry designs and specifications[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) for agent capability and resource federation[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- Workload attestation and token-exchange patterns using SPIFFE/SPIRE and Uber Engineering's agent identity framework[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace layered policy and delegation reference architecture[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization Internet-Draft (`draft-klrc-aiagent-auth`)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

## Operations and Meetings
The working group holds public meetings every Thursday, alternating between 6:30 AM PT and 9:00 AM PT, with running notes, recordings, and transcripts hosted via the Linux Foundation LFX platform[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

proposed_concept.title: Agent to Tool CLI Boundary Observability Deep-Dive
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and telemetry propagation model analyzing the direct agent-to-tool local CLI subprocess boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The direct Agent → Tool CLI boundary analyzes telemetry propagation, context preservation, and identity continuity when an AI agent invokes an external tool realized as a local CLI subprocess[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. While the semantic boundary represents the agent-level tool decision (`gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`), the operational boundary crosses from the agent runtime to the local operating system process (`process.pid`, executable path)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Architecture / Specification
## Boundary Hierarchy and Span Structure
The reference trace hierarchy establishes causality across two distinct execution surfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
```text
optional upstream caller
  └── agent turn / invocation
      └── tool execution span              (Agent → Tool semantic boundary)
          └── [optional CLI caller span]
              └── local CLI execution span (Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary)
                  └── CLI sub-operations and downstream calls
```
The agent execution surface selects tools and schedules calls, whereas the operating-system process surface resolves the binary, prepares the environment, launches the process, and captures standard streams and exit status[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

## Telemetry and Context Propagation Matrix
Across the local CLI boundary, observability requirements map across six primary dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
- **Identity:** Correlates agent, session turn, tool name, and tool call ID with child process ID, resolved executable path, and digest. While OpenTelemetry GenAI covers tool identity and CLI conventions cover PIDs, cross-runtime binding across the agent decision and child executable remains an open gap[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Context:** Carries active W3C Trace Context and baggage across normalized environment variables (`TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`). Because local subprocesses lack network headers, context must be injected into the environment before process launch; late transcript parsing cannot retroactively establish parent spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Relationship:** Preserves caller-to-child causality. Synchronous processes exist as children of the tool or CLI caller span, whereas detached or background executions require Span Links to avoid misrepresenting task lifecycles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Lifecycle:** Maps execution phases (`selected` → `authorized` → `context prepared` → `spawn requested` → `process started` → `running` → `exited`/`timed out`/`canceled`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Outcome:** Records process exit codes, error classifications, side-effect manifests, and partial tool results while avoiding sensitive credential leakage in stdout/stderr[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Provenance:** Captures tool origin, instrumentation scope, runtime wrappers, and shell expansions to ensure the executed binary matches the agent's intended invocation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

## Implementation Validation
The boundary mechanics are validated by the LoongSuite Pilot reference implementation, demonstrating pre-execution reservation of tool call IDs, environment-variable carrier injection prior to child fork/exec, and post-execution transcript reconciliation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy schema, evidentiary standard, and empirical inventory categorizing production agentic workflows by execution pattern, coordination model, and autonomy requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation use case classification framework provides an empirical schema and evidence-based inventory for mapping commercial and open-source agentic deployments to standardized workflow archetypes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]. Governed by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), the framework establishes criteria for discerning between single-agent scripts, parallel fan-out systems, and deterministic convergence loops based on verified architectural documentation.

# Architecture / Specification
The framework pairs an evidentiary schema (`schema-agentic-use-cases.md`) with a live inventory evaluating real-world deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48]. 

### Evidentiary Classification Standards
Workflows are classified across three core dimensions:
1. **Execution Structure**: Distinguishes sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out splits, and iterative loops. Classifications require verified vendor documentation of execution flow; where citations only show trial-and-error without a deterministic acceptance test, entries are explicitly held as unspecified [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
2. **Coordination Model**: Identifies whether orchestration is static/scripted or dynamically AI-coordinated with multi-turn planning.
3. **Agent Multiplicity**: Evaluates whether tasks are single-agent sufficient or inherently multi-agent due to context-window exhaustion or security boundary splits [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

### Documented Deployments
- **Lead Research & Enrichment**: Categorized as a sequential pipeline following documented waterfall provider lookups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **On-Call Incident Summary**: Categorized as an inherently multi-agent, AI-coordinated parallel fan-out architecture based on supervisor agent root-cause hypothesis generation and sub-agent dispatch [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Contract Review & Red-Lining**: Categorized as AI-coordinated planning workflow [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
- Initial use case taxonomy and inventory established under the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.
- Citations and unresolved classifications tightened in pull requests #39 and #48 to eliminate broken internal references and enforce strict deterministic criteria before classifying iterative workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practitioner guide and static-analysis rule catalog defining defensive controls, workload identity standards, failure patterns, and operational boundaries for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes normative security principles, baseline controls, and defensive threat models for deploying autonomous agents in enterprise environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) in consultation with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), it covers credential delegation, execution sandboxing, tool boundary enforcement, and workload identity lifecycle management.

# Architecture / Specification
### Workload Identity and Token Lifecycles
The baseline guidance specifies least-privilege identity boundaries and bounded token lifecycles for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]:
- **Single-Cloud Baseline**: Default workload identities constrained to short-lived credentials (default 1-hour cloud expiry or lower) bounded by scoped IAM role designs.
- **Multi-Cloud & Federated Deployments**: Scoping guidelines for agent workloads that access resources across multiple cloud providers and IAM domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]. Key areas under development include OIDC-based workload identity federation, cross-cloud role assumption, cross-provider blast radius evaluation, and secure token propagation across non-native on-premises environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

### Boundary Protection Patterns
Integrates architectural patterns such as [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and out-of-band [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) controls to prevent untrusted agent actions from propagating into core infrastructure.

# Lifecycle History
- Established as foundational guidance for the Security & Privacy WG.
- Scope expanded via issue #23 to address cross-cloud workload identity federation, hybrid cloud/on-prem role assumption, and cross-trust boundary delegation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and behavioral trace specification defining agent turn boundaries, causal execution lineage, and upstream contributions to OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification defining telemetry semantic conventions, causal trace context propagation, and structured execution graphs for multi-agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]. Governed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the trace model provides consistent instrumentation rules for agent conversation boundaries, internal reasoning loops, tool dispatch calls, and upstream OpenTelemetry integration.

# Architecture / Specification
### Behavioral Spans and Boundaries
The specification structures agent executions into discrete, causally linked spans:
- **Agent Turns**: Boundary markers capturing turn-entry spans, conversation identifiers, and actor roles across distributed contexts.
- **Tool and Subagent Invocations**: Structured spans capturing tool input/output payloads, latency, and invocation identities.

### Upstream Contributions Pipeline
Under Task 9 of the execution plan, empirical findings from trace model implementations are fed back into upstream specifications and standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]:
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions**: Contributing turn-entry span conventions and clarifying agent execution attributes in the upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Runtime Fixes**: Contributing conversation ID and trace context propagation fixes directly to agent runtime maintainers.
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinating terminology proposals with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

# Lifecycle History
- Drafted under the Observability and Traceability Working Group as part of the nine-task execution plan.
- Task 9 established upstream contribution protocols targeting OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and agent runtime instrumentation fixes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, cross-boundary observability, and agent identity propagation across distributed runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry formats, lineage graphs, cross-boundary context propagation, and operational metrics for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]. Its focus includes developing the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), aligning with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md), and defining telemetry hygiene standards to observe multi-agent systems without exposing sensitive runtime state.

# Architecture / Specification
### Active Workstreams
1. **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A nine-task execution initiative creating structured schemas for agent execution spans, turn boundaries, and upstream contributions to OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
2. **Agent Identity Telemetry Propagation**: Defining OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for agent identity attributes (e.g., `agent.id`, `agent.role`, `agent.invocation_id`, `agent.principal.type`, `agent.delegation_depth`) and W3C Baggage propagation across asynchronous job queues, event streams, and sandbox boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
3. **Telemetry Sanitization & Boundary Controls**: Specifying data redaction rules to prevent raw cryptographic tokens, authorization proofs, and private keys from leaking into APM backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

### Cross-Group Collaboration
The working group cross-reviews identity propagation and security boundary policies in collaboration with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

# Lifecycle History
- Charter approved by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).
- August execution plan formalized nine execution tasks for trace model standardization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- Scoping initiated in issue #50 for agent identity telemetry and baggage propagation rules across distributed agent topologies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for resolving bounded operational problems autonomously through isolated execution, deterministic acceptance gating, and safe escalation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is an AAIF reference architecture that resolves bounded operational tasks autonomously by relying on independent acceptance evidence and safe escalation when convergence fails[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. Positioned as a companion to the [single-agent human approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) architecture, it permits iterative autonomous problem-solving without requiring human approval for every attempt, provided the task operates under explicit resource limits, isolated execution, and constrained downstream effects[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

Typical use cases include preparing remediation pull requests, generating draft records, reconciling correction batches, or performing maintenance tasks where acceptance criteria can be verified programmatically without subjective human judgment[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
### Pattern Composition
The architecture integrates three primary workflow patterns:
- [Bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Drives iterative agent problem-solving within strict iteration limits, credentials, and time budgets[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- [Deterministic acceptance gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Evaluates candidate outputs against explicit, repeatable verification rules rather than relying on agent self-evaluation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- [Proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Separates candidate generation in non-authoritative scratchpads from the final application of effects on external systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

### Required Capabilities
1. **Execution Engine**: Manages admission, step sequencing, retry bounds, and termination[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
2. **Bounded Agent Environment**: Constrains agent reasoning, tool access, and operational credentials[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
3. **Isolated Work Area**: Non-authoritative environment hosting intermediate work without touching production state[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
4. **Deterministic Acceptance Gate**: Validates tests, schemas, contracts, or policies; all criteria must pass conjunctive verification[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
5. **Constrained Effect Executor**: Applies only the exact accepted result to external systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
6. **Escalation Surface and Audit Log**: Records execution evidence and routes unresolvable or exhausted attempts to human operators[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

### Scenario Validation
- **Autonomous Maintenance Run**: Validated as an operational scenario for routine hygiene, automated refactoring, and test-suite confirmation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
- **Weekly Staff Schedule Generation**: Validated against a unified Schedule Acceptance Gate enforcing multi-constraint satisfaction[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# Lifecycle History
- Drafted and refined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group as a peer architecture to human-approved flows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, proposed action lifecycles, and causal relationships aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry framework managed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) establishing consistent causal relationships across agent conversation scopes, turns, calls, and observations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. It provides a crosswalk connecting AAIF behavioral concepts with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic conventions to enable vendor-neutral tracing across heterogeneous agent environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification
### Scope and Identity Model
The trace specification structures agent telemetry along defined relational layers:
- **Conversation Scope**: Covers multi-turn sessions where distinct turns (such as T1 and T2) may emit separate trace identifiers while preserving causal continuity within a single conversation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Turns and Tool Calls**: Delimits discrete LLM reasoning cycles and downstream tool invocations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Proposed Actions and Approvals**: Binds proposed actions (such as ticket creation or API mutations) to human or policy approvals; approvals explicitly link to proposed actions even when denied and no tool execution span is generated[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Durable Waits and Resumption**: Accommodates operational waits during out-of-band approval gates, maintaining context when execution resumes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

### OpenTelemetry Alignment
The specification defines crosswalk mappings between AAIF trace constructs and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, supporting incomplete observations, standalone turn traces, and multi-agent delegation traces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History
- Progressing under Task 3 of the nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan initiated in the Observability and Traceability Working Group[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agentic Use Case Classification provides an empirical catalog and taxonomy schema maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to evaluate and classify production agent implementations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. It serves as the evidentiary baseline for deriving reference architectures and analyzing operational patterns across industry deployments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification
### Pattern Classification Ambiguities
Analysis of the empirical inventory identified classification tensions between two core workflow patterns:
- **Parallel Fan-Out**: Historically defined by wall-clock concurrency (concurrent sub-tasks)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
- **Sequential Pipeline**: Historically defined by functional dependency (dependent activities where each step feeds the next)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

Because concurrency and dependency are not strict logical opposites, workflows may exhibit both or neither characteristic, stalling classification across 20 of 24 previously unspecified inventory entries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

### Evaluated Readings
The working group evaluates three interpretations to resolve boundary ambiguity:
1. **Timing as Observed**: Based strictly on measured runtime execution overlap[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
2. **Agent Count**: Differentiating architectures by single-agent execution versus multi-agent delegation topology[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
3. **Dependency**: Based strictly on data dependency DAGs regardless of whether scheduling happens sequentially or concurrently[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
- Open question raised to determine whether taxonomy classification columns reflect an individual organization's implementation choices or the intrinsic structure of the underlying use case[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing shared agentic AI vocabulary and curating ecosystem taxonomy data through working-group domain editors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group workstream within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) that operates as a horizontal architectural bridge connecting the seven top-level Technical Working Groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Rather than authoring vertical subject-matter definitions from scratch, the workstream coordinates domain sovereign representations, ingestions, and harmonizations across AAIF working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. The workstream is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

While the workstream's long-term charter encompasses both an ecosystem market landscape and a pre-competitive terminology index, the workstream's current active scope is strictly limited to the **Taxonomy**[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Landscape contributions remain deferred on the future roadmap until review processes are established[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

### Working Group Domain Editors
Terminology governance relies on appointed delegates from each vertical working group known as **Domain Editors**[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- **Accuracy & Reliability**: Casper Nielsen, Matthew Khouzam[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- **Agentic Commerce**: Leonardo Galesky[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- **Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment**: Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- **Identity & Trust**: Julianna Mealin[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- **Observability & Traceability**: Pavan Sudheendra, Matt Lee[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- **Security & Privacy**: Jautau White, Katherine Druckman[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- **Workflows & Process Integration**: Sumanth Sathyanarayana[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]

### Terminology Lifecycle and Governance Policies
1. **Intake and Triage**: Candidate terms are logged in the Taxonomy Working Spreadsheet and triaged as *Debate*, *Keep*, or *Cull*[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Established cross-domain terms without agentic specificity (such as general cybersecurity "Red teaming") are culled, while AI-distinct operational concepts (such as "Guardrails") are retained[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
2. **Horizontal Index Principle**: The workstream captures foundational cross-cutting terms affecting two or more working groups. Deep technical whitepapers, internal wire protocols, and implementation payloads remain inside vertical WG repositories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
3. **Paired Contrast Disambiguation**: When concepts represent adjacent operational contrasts (e.g., *Tool* versus *Skill*, *Deterministic workflow* versus *Agentic workflow*), they must not be merged into generic aliases. Definitions must explicitly state counter-boundaries and link using `relatedTerms` or `contrastsWith`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
4. **Anti-Erasure Guardrail**: Terms cannot be deleted or aliased without explicit written approval from the owning working group's Domain Editor[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
5. **Two-Pass Ingestion Policy**: The workstream admits approved terms first and agrees on definitions second. In the initial check-in stage, `definition`, `category`, and `broaderTerm` fields are deliberately deferred or populated with pending placeholders to avoid premature structural disputes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-27**: Workstream adopted a flat schema policy deferring `definition`, `category`, and `broaderTerm` hierarchies during initial term ingestion[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- **2026-09-03**: Workstream Domain Editor roster ratified across all seven technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing evaluation benchmarks, practitioner surveys, and testing coverage standards for production agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) evaluates the operational correctness, robustness, and determinism of agentic AI systems. The group formulates benchmark taxonomies, empirical evaluation suites, practitioner research surveys, and test coverage methodologies to measure system behavior under production conditions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Deliverables
- **AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey**: A 16-question platform-neutral survey evaluating real-world practitioner experiences with agentic systems deployed across serious pilot, limited deployment, and broad deployment tiers[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. The instrument measures organizational size, human verification gates, frequency of unacceptable results, failure recognition prior to impact, and industry testing priorities[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Coverage and Defect-Detection Reporting Standards (D1 §9.4)**: Reporting criteria for coverage and mutation evaluation in agent test panels. The specification mandates separating the declared inventory, the selected evaluation subset, what was exercised, and what was excluded or uncompleted[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11]. To prevent distorted metrics across mutation tools, reporting distinguishes detected, exercised-but-undetected, and unexercised defects, while explicitly labeling timeouts, runtime errors, and equivalent mutants rather than silently merging them into a single aggregate mutation score[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].

### Cross-Workstream Coordination
The working group appoints Domain Editors to the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (represented by Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam) to shepherd domain terms into the shared vocabulary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
