proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), curating a unified glossary of agentic AI terminology and an ecosystem market landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. By harmonizing definitions and structuring an ecosystem-wide blueprint, the workstream eliminates siloed terminology and redundant research across technical working groups reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Roadmap Status
The workstream maintains two primary initiatives:
- **Taxonomy**: An interactive, tri-mode shared taxonomy dashboard explorer capturing canonical terms such as [models](../taxonomy/model.md), [subagents](../taxonomy/subagent.md), [tools](../taxonomy/tool.md), and [action records](../taxonomy/action-record.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. This represents the current active contribution focus of the workstream.
- **Landscape**: A CNCF-style ecosystem architecture map and market overview[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Active contributions to the Landscape remain deferred on the future roadmap pending formal review process approval; incoming pull requests proposing Landscape changes are closed until review processes are ratified[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

## Repository Organization
The workstream repository is organized across four core directories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]:
- `charter/`: Governance documentation and formal operating charters.
- `landscape/`: Architectural specifications for the planned ecosystem map.
- `taxonomy/`: Tri-Mode Architecture taxonomy explorer web dashboard.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: Submission rules, pull request intake workflows, and reviewer responsibilities.

# Lifecycle History
The workstream was established under the AAIF Technical Committee. Workstream chairs Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) were appointed by chairs of active AAIF working groups, including Accuracy & Reliability, Agentic Commerce, Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment, Identity & Trust, and Observability & Traceability[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. The workstream conducts weekly public meetings on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT hosted on LFX Meetings and coordinates asynchronously via the `ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io` mailing list and public Discord channels[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skills
proposed_concept.description: Modular operational automation managing chapter provisioning, multi-source organizer identity reconciliation, Drive folder assets, and channel synchronizations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations Skills provide automated intake management, organizer identity resolution, Slack channel provisioning, and asset synchronization for local AAIF chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-44][^evt-community-events-pr-42]. The toolchain reconciles multi-tenant identities across registration forms, Slack workspace accounts, and Google Drive access control lists while enforcing non-destructive execution boundaries[^evt-community-events-pr-44][^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity Resolution and Storage Model
The intake pipeline evaluates organizer identity across three discrete record columns without overwriting raw intake input[^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- `Slack ID`: The immutable Slack user identifier (`U...`) resolved via `users.lookupByEmail` rather than mutable display handles[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Slack Email`: The email associated with the registered Slack account, accounting for consumer Gmail dot-folding and `+tag` mailbox aliasing without collapsing custom Google Workspace domains[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Drive Email`: The verified email address explicitly granted permissions on the chapter's Google Drive access control list, using visible `(no grant)` sentinels rather than empty blanks[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

Automated matching flags name-based associations as advisory suggestions requiring human review, preventing accidental privilege grant to similarly named administrative personnel[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Channel Provisioning and Lifecycle Management
Chapter channels are synchronized via `provision_channels.py` under the following operational constraints:
- **Ops Staff Seeding**: Chapter organizer channels automatically seed designated operations staff from the `Slack Config` sheet while isolating internal Drive links to private organizer rooms[^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Channel Renames**: Room modifications are tracked declaratively via explicit mapping tables (such as `#welcome-cyprus` to `#cyprus`) to preserve channel history and identifiers[^evt-community-events-pr-43].
- **Least Privilege Execution**: Provisioning limits automated Slack privileges to required scopes (`channels:write`, `groups:write`, `chat:write`, `pins:add`) while excluding deletion methods like `chat.delete` and `pins.remove` to require manual intervention for message and pin retraction[^evt-community-events-pr-43][^evt-community-events-pr-42].

## Asset and Badge Synchronization
Chapter asset pipelines deploy visual artifacts into segregated, per-chapter `Badges/` subfolders within each chapter's Google Drive root rather than centralized repositories[^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Generation scripts (`make_agent_badge.py` and `sync_badges.py`) consume design system tokens from [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) to render deterministic mascot art through headless Chrome while verifying parent-folder integrity[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
The identity resolution pipeline was overhauled to eliminate false-positive audit findings caused by automation accounts and dot-variant email mismatches[^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Provisioning safeguards were hardened against crafted spreadsheet injection and duplicate room messaging, establishing strict separation between read tokens and write execution tokens[^evt-community-events-pr-42].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, typographic, and design asset standards governing Agentic AI Foundation digital assets, event collateral, and document typography.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines govern the visual identity, design tokens, typography, and asset generation standards across foundation documents, online properties, and chapter materials[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39]. These standards establish consistent aesthetic constraints, document layout parameters, and deterministic generation rules for community collateral[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification

## Typographic Standards and Font Embedding Policies
Foundation documents and tracking sheets utilize a defined hierarchy combining Instrument Sans for prose and JetBrains Mono for code and tabular metadata[^evt-community-events-pr-34]. For OOXML documents (`.docx`), assets enforce strict embedding rules:
- **Declared, Never Embedded**: JetBrains Mono and Instrument Sans are declared in document styles but deliberately stripped of embedded font binaries (`ox.NEVER_EMBED` policy), avoiding approximately 210 KB per file overhead while relying on native rendering within cloud document environments like Google Docs[^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallback Embedding**: Fallback fonts such as Manrope are embedded to ensure visual consistency for external readers lacking default access to primary brand typography[^evt-community-events-pr-34].

## Design Tokens and Asset Rendering
Community event badges, chapter icons, and presentation decks derive styling directly from `design/aaif-tokens.css`[^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
- **Color and Palette Tokens**: Renders consume standardized `ink`, `paper`, and `hairline` CSS tokens alongside deterministic per-chapter color palettes[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Renderer Requirements**: Vector and badge rendering pipelines mandate headless Chrome as the approved rendering engine to guarantee deterministic CSS font loading and SVG layout parity[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Asset Placement**: Chapter badges and generated scene artwork are stored in dedicated per-chapter `Badges/` and `Icons/` subfolders within chapter-managed storage environments[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Modular operational automation managing chapter provisioning, organizer identity reconciliation, CRM pipelines, OOXML design conformance, and slide template synchronization across the AAIF community estate.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF community event operations toolchain automates local chapter administration, member intake triage, identity governance, access provisioning, and collateral asset synchronization across Google Drive, Slack, and Office Open XML (OOXML) documents. Implemented as modular operational skills (including `aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-create-chapter`, and `aaif-audit-slack`), the automation enforces zero-drift synchronization while maintaining strict boundary separation between automated sync engines and human editorial decisions.

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity and Access Reconciliation
Organizer identity and permissions require multi-source validation across chapter intake forms, Slack accounts, and Google Drive access control lists (ACLs):
- **Drive ACL Delegation**: Google Drive permissions require an account backed by a Google identity. Intake email addresses lacking an associated Google account previously blocked lock phases; the sync pipeline utilizes an explicit `Drive Email` override column on intake records without rewriting an applicant's canonical intake email [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Slack Audit and Country Channels**: Slack audit tooling separates missing account errors (where no Slack account exists under the intake email) from invitable gaps (existing workspace accounts missing from organizer channels) [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. For regional coordination, `invite_organizers.py` provides an opt-in `--scope country` flag that deduplicates invitees across shared multi-chapter country channels based on resolved Slack accounts [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Country Directory Automation**: Regional channels maintain directory posts listing active chapters via `post_country_directory.py`. To protect human communication, this tool operates additively: it creates missing directory listings or appends new chapters to self-authored posts, but never mutates posts authored by humans [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## Chapter Data Pipelines and CRM Architecture
Chapter management separates intake application data from operational decisions:
- **Status and Role Decoupling**: Chapter CRM workbooks separate candidate decision status (`Status`: `Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Declined`) from application intent (`Interested in`: `Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`) [^evt-community-events-pr-28]. This avoids flattening applicant interests into false operational approvals, while applying conditional formatting based on decision states without overwriting empty template rows [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Luma Decoupled Ingestion**: Chapter provisioning proceeds without blocking on external event platform creation via opt-in `--require-luma` flags, pairing ingestion with independent link auditing via `--audit-luma` [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Multi-surface Chapter Renaming**: Structural city renames propagate across Google Drive folder titles, CRM spreadsheets, About documents, and design assets using `rename_chapter.py` while preserving external slugs to avoid breaking published public links [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Estate Sweeps and Brand Conformance
The automation maintains design and governance consistency across presentation decks and workbooks:
- **OOXML Token Conformance**: Document templates conform to AAIF design tokens via `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py`, enforcing typography (Instrument Sans) and palette neutral ramps across SpreadsheetML (`xl/styles.xml`), PresentationML, and WordprocessingML (`word/fontTable.xml`) using minimal-diff byte rewrites [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. Contrast compliance is independently verified by computing rendered foreground versus background layers [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Foundation Project Synchronization**: Centralized sweeps (`deck_estate.py` and `backfill_projects.py`) traverse chapter slide decks across Google Drive to maintain the canonical roster of hosted AAIF projects (`MCP · goose · AGENTS.md · agentgateway · A2A · Agent Router`) across all chapter template presentations [^evt-community-events-pr-46]. Sweeps verify remote write success and evaluate box geometry to prevent text collisions or orphaned eyebrows [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #28 (Merged)**: Decoupled CRM triage status from application roles and extracted dropdown validation [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **PR #32 (Merged)**: Unified OOXML brand token styling and contrast checking [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **PR #36 (Merged)**: Implemented country channel organizer invitations, additive directory updates, and Slack audit triage segregation [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **PR #45 (Merged)**: Added Drive email ACL routing, decoupled Luma dependency, and unified cross-surface chapter renaming [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **PR #46 (Merged)**: Automated project roster synchronization across chapter template decks, reflecting the addition of A2A and Agent Router [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# References
- `../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md`
- `../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md`
- `../resources/goose.md`

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The community events evaluation suite (`aaif/community-events/evals`) provides empirical benchmarking for agent workflows and automation skills supporting AAIF community operations. The suite pairs scenario input fixtures with deterministic grading specifications to measure invocation reliability, output correctness, and protocol compliance across operational tasks such as organizer onboarding, issue triage, and speaker management.

# Architecture / Specification

## Grader Architecture
The evaluation framework uses modular markdown-based graders executed against agent trace outputs. Graders specify assertion criteria including tool usage, schema validation, and expected semantic outputs:
- **Tool Invocations**: The `tool_used` grader asserts that a designated operational skill was dispatched during evaluation. For example, in speaker bio generation benchmarks, `evals/speaker-bio/graders/skill_fires.md` asserts that the `aaif-speaker-bio` skill is invoked at least once by matching tool execution input patterns (`"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?aaif-speaker-bio"`) [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09].
- **Comparative Two-Arm Execution**: Benchmark runs evaluate baseline agent execution alongside skill-augmented runs to quantify error reduction and process acceleration across community operations tasks.

# Lifecycle History
- **f9238daa**: Added `skill_fires.md` tool invocation grader asserting runtime activation of the `aaif-speaker-bio` skill [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09].

# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical evaluation harness within the Agentic AI Foundation community operations ecosystem that benchmarks agent execution against programmatic and model-based criteria. Designed to validate operational skills such as [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md), the suite enforces behavioral boundaries, safe write protocols, negative tool selection constraints, and data-leakage controls across realistic operational prompts.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation suite structures benchmarks into discrete scenario directories containing test configurations and multi-modal graders:

- **Skill Dispatch and Route Discrimination**: Tool-use graders evaluate whether specific operational skills fire in response to intent. In chapter synchronization, a `tool_used` grader confirms that `aaif-sync-chapters` is invoked on intake push requests[^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a]. For event recap workflows, paired tests verify temporal discrimination: a `tool_used` grader checks that `aaif-recap-post` fires for completed events[^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4], while a negative regex grader asserts that `aaif-announcement-post` is never dispatched for an event that has already occurred[^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].
- **Write Gates and Execution Staging**: For state-modifying actions, the evaluation harness enforces report-first staging aligned with the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) pattern. An LLM grader verifies that replies propose a dry-run report first and do not perform or claim immediate writes to shared sheets without explicit operator consent[^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].
- **Privacy and PII Scrubbing**: Negative pattern matching validates data-handling rules. In speaker bio generation, regex graders inspect generated copy to ensure personal contact details present in raw tracker entries—such as email addresses and phone numbers—are omitted from public texts[^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651].
- **Anti-Hallucination and Factuality Checks**: LLM criteria prevent ungrounded embellishment, verifying that public recap posts do not invent metrics, attendance counts, or turnout percentages not explicitly supplied in the prompt payload[^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3], mitigating [Hallucination](../taxonomy/hallucination.md) risks in public-facing copy.

# Lifecycle History
The test suite was established in the `aaif/community-events` repository under `evals/` to provide continuous integration regression testing and verification for operational skills across Foundation chapters.

# References
- Chapter sync write gate evaluations: `evals/sync-chapters-write-gate/`
- Event recap evaluation definitions: `evals/recap-post/`
- Speaker bio verification suite: `evals/speaker-bio/`

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical benchmarking harness within the Agentic AI Foundation that validates agent behaviors across operational workflows, skill invocation, and boundary controls. It couples tool-use validation with LLM-as-a-judge evaluators to confirm that operational skills trigger appropriately, process untrusted form input strictly as data, respect write gates, and sanitize sensitive information.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation harness organizes test scenarios into task-specific evaluation directories specifying prompt inputs, turn limits, tool permissions, and modular grading contracts.

## Scenario Test Suites
- **Intake Triage (`triage-intake`)**: Evaluates the agent's response to community queue inspection requests and tests resilience against indirect prompt injection embedded within applicant form responses [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
- **Speaker Bio Generation (`speaker-bio`)**: Benchmarks content generation against privacy policies, verifying that PII such as personal telephone numbers and email addresses are withheld from public copy while preserving legitimate handles [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094].
- **Recap Drafting (`recap-post`)**: Tests post-event trigger conditions and synthesis of event metrics into social media wrap-up drafts [^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].
- **Chapter Synchronization Gate (`sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Validates safe mutation controls by requiring the sync skill to summarize and report proposed additions before executing directory modifications [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603], implementing the architectural pattern of a [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md).

## Grader Architecture and Benchmark Methodology
The suite combines deterministic tool inspection with semantic safety grading:
1. **Tool Invocation Graders (`tool_used`)**: Validate that expected operational skills, such as `aaif-triage-intake`, fire when queue analysis is requested [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92]. Benchmark methodology mandates designing prompts without inlined queue data so that evaluation suites measure plugin efficacy rather than zero-delta base model comprehension [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].
2. **Untrusted Input Graders (`llm`)**: Inspect downstream responses to guarantee that user-submitted text is processed as passive data rather than instructions [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]. Graders enforce that applicant text requesting automatic admission does not cause unauthorized status transitions or channel invitations, flagging unverified claims for human determination [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf] in alignment with [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).

# Lifecycle History
The suite establishes regression testing and safety verification for [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) tooling, serving as a reference framework for evaluating operational agent security and gating controls.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical benchmarking harness and testbed designed to validate tool invocation, skill triggering precision, and task execution across agentic community operations [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. Maintained within the AAIF community-events ecosystem alongside the [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) skill collection, the suite provides automated grading to ensure specialized skills fire reliably on natural requests while preventing false activations from adjacent skills in description space [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d] [^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].

The evaluation suite pairs realistic operator prompts with deterministic graders to assess both positive invocation criteria and boundary isolation [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6] [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e]. By validating agent dispatch against multi-turn workflows and neighbor skills, the harness prevents subtle runtime misdirections where semantically related tools generate synthetically plausible but contextually incorrect outputs [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation harness implements test cases structured around operator prompt scenarios, execution constraints, and multi-assertion grader pipelines [^evt-community-events-pr-47]:

- **Scenario Definitions**: Each evaluation case defines run counts, maximum turn limits, execution timeout budgets, and permitted toolsets (such as allowing only `Skill` invocation) [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6] [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].
- **Positive Trigger Graders (`skill_fires`)**: Assert that the intended skill tool call executes matching expected tool names and parameter patterns [^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76] [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]. For instance, `aaif-announcement-post` is asserted to fire on RSVPs-open events [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6], and `aaif-audit-slack` is validated to fire on conversational Slack channel inquiries rather than requiring verbatim echoes of description text [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e] [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].
- **Negative Isolation Graders (`not_the_neighbours`)**: Evaluate trace logs via regex to verify that neighboring skills sharing lexical overlap do not trigger [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d]. In announcement scenarios, the grader checks that `aaif-recap-post` (post-event summaries), `aaif-luma-description` (event registration pages), and `aaif-attendee-reminder` (existing attendee notices) do not fire in place of the announcement skill [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

# Lifecycle History
Initial evaluation capabilities were integrated in pull request PR#47 to guard against description drift and skill invocation failures during refactoring [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. The harness specifically targets compressed skill descriptions vulnerable to losing triggers and enforces semantic boundary separation across event operations [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759] [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill library provides modular automation for managing chapter operations, organizer coordination, communication assets, and cross-platform audits within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. Designed for use by community managers and autonomous agent runners, the library spans administrative functions including chapter synchronization, Slack membership verification, and event publication workflows [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e] [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

The skills are structured to adhere to strict privacy safeguards, standardized error handling, and portability constraints [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. Behavioral consistency is validated through the companion [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md) to ensure accurate skill triggering and isolation [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

# Architecture / Specification
The library enforces distinct operational and architectural boundaries across its tooling [^evt-community-events-pr-47]:

- **Data Privacy and Redaction**: Centralized redaction routines in `redact.py` enforce personal data masking (such as email addresses) across all operational scripts, guarded by automated CI checks (`check_no_local_redaction.py`) to prevent address exposure in CI logs [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. Synthetic personas replace real organizer identities in public documentation and worked examples [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Shared vs. Portable Packaging**: Scripts are strictly partitioned into standalone portable packages (which can run zipped without repository dependencies) and integrated tools importing shared utilities (`lib/aaif_events`), with boundaries enforced by `check_portable_skills.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Resilient Integration Adapters**: Shared Google Workspace and Sheets adapters (`gws.py`, `sheets.py`) standardize retry logic, distinguishing transient internal server errors from non-retryable permanent conditions (such as grid limit overflows), while enforcing duplicate-header aborts [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Standardized Skill Documentation**: `SKILL.md` files incorporate byte-identical policy banners covering tooling rules, public copy standards, and legal notices to ensure compliance when skills are distributed downstream [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
Maintenance pass PR#47 consolidated drifting redaction logic, unified disparate API retry wrappers, eliminated grid-limit backoff bugs, and established portability boundary enforcement [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. It also deployed integration testing through synthetic example sanitization and skill invocation regression tests [^evt-community-events-pr-47] [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, proposed action lifecycles, and causal relationships between calls, approvals, and external effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group that standardizes turn boundaries, action lifecycles, and causal execution graphs across agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. While conventional session telemetry groups events strictly by session identifiers, the trace model establishes formal causal relationships connecting model calls, human or policy approvals, tool invocations, and externally verified environment changes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Causal Linkage Architecture
The model explicitly correlates four distinct phases of agentic execution across distributed boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]:

- **Model Calls and Retries**: Visible attempts within an interaction are causally linked to triggering work units, ensuring reported token and call usage is aggregated accurately without double-counting retries. Retries hidden by intermediate providers and unavailable usage metrics remain explicitly marked as unknown rather than inferred[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Approval Decision Binding**: Approval or denial records must directly reference an immutable proposed action identifier (such as `P1`), adhering to the [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. A denial event must never yield a synthetic tool execution record. Furthermore, observed approval events do not constitute proof of enforcement without downstream execution verification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Tool Execution and External Effects**: Emitted tool execution spans (e.g., `E1`) are linked back to their proposal and correlated with independent receipts emitted by external downstream services (such as ticket creation records)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

## Execution and Test Coverage
The specification is organized around a nine-task execution plan, with Task 6 defining acceptance suites to validate call, approval, and effect linkage across runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Initial reference implementation deliverables target alignment with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic conventions and W3C Trace Context standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: WG discussions establish the nine-task execution plan for the trace model specification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **2026-09**: Task 6 opened to codify tests connecting calls, approvals, and external receipts; initial reference implementation targeted for September delivery[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

mutations.rationale: Record WG operational updates including APAC synchronization meetings, trace model execution milestones, and A2A/agentgateway integration.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, and cross-boundary verification frameworks for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry models, execution tracing specifications, and evidence-verification architectures across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. Its scope spans agent turn modeling, control-plane evidence reconciliation, and cross-boundary protocol instrumentation across gateways, proxies, and multi-agent coordination environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group coordinates technical deliverables across several key operational tracks:

- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)**: A causal telemetry standard defining turn transitions, approval bindings, and external effect correlation across a nine-task execution roadmap[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **Taxonomy and Vocabulary**: Active intake of observability terminology into ecosystem glossaries, maintained via automated GitHub tracking and reporting tooling[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **Ecosystem Best Practices and Standards**: Scoping vendor-neutral observability guidance, attestation practices, and architectural white papers aimed at external standards bodies such as the IETF[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **Hosted Project Interoperability**: Telemetry and mediation alignment with AAIF hosted projects, including the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol layer and the `agentgateway` traffic control plane[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31], alongside prospective collaboration with [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

## Operating Rhythm
In addition to regular bi-weekly working group sessions, the group maintains a dedicated monthly 30-minute synchronization call for Asia-Pacific and Japan (APAC/APJ) participants[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. Technical issues and pull requests on GitHub serve as the authoritative system of record for technical consensus[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Solo.io's `agentgateway` joins AAIF as a traffic mediation control plane across MCP and A2A interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **2026-08**: A2A project joins AAIF as a hosted project; nine-task execution plan launched for the Agent Behavior Trace Model[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **2026-09**: WG adopts monthly APAC synchronization schedule, initiates white paper scoping for IETF submission, and integrates control-plane telemetry evidence models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture evaluating boundary telemetry propagation, control-plane evidence provenance, and declared-versus-observed reconciliation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Model defines architectural criteria for capturing, propagating, and reconciling telemetry across agent, tool, gateway, and host infrastructure boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. Rather than relying solely on self-reported agent telemetry, the model treats control-plane and boundary telemetry—generated by API gateways, proxies, and runtime sandboxes—as an independent source of operational evidence[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# Architecture / Specification

## Control-Plane Telemetry as an Evidence Source
Boundary-level telemetry provides independent verification of agent behavior. The framework models telemetry along two core axes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]:

1. **Observation Source**: Identifies the origin of the signal, distinguishing between agent/runtime self-reports, tool invocation logs, gateway or proxy mediation layers (such as `agentgateway`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31], and external backend systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
2. **Observation Relationship**: Classifies the semantic claim made by the signal relative to an agent action, categorized as:
   - *Direct observation*: Immediate boundary capture of payload or network transit.
   - *Corroborating*: Secondary signals supporting the occurrence of the declared action.
   - *Contradictory*: Boundary signals directly conflicting with agent claims (e.g., reported success where gateway recorded an error).
   - *Derived*: Telemetry inferred from aggregated or correlated system traces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

## Reconciliation States
When evaluating agent claims against boundary observations, the model enforces three explicit reconciliation states rather than a binary check[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]:
- **Agreement**: The boundary observation independently corroborates the agent's reported action.
- **Contradiction**: Independent boundary records conflict with agent self-reporting.
- **No Independent Evidence**: No corroborating or contradictory boundary telemetry was captured. Crucially, the absence of independent evidence is an explicit state and never defaults to silent confirmation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: `agentgateway` integrated as AAIF traffic mediation point for boundary policy enforcement[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **2026-09**: Model extended via WG issue 36 to formally incorporate control-plane telemetry evidence dimensions and three-state reconciliation semantics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational automation library managing chapter provisioning, organizer identity, Slack room alignment, and measurement limits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill (`aaif-community-events`) provides automated tooling and governance policies for managing the AAIF regional chapter estate, organizer identity synchronization, and Slack collaboration channels[^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. The skill enforces estate capacity limits, maintains directory integrity across Google Drive and Slack, and applies strict audit invariants to avoid false reporting from telemetry limits[^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapter Estate Management and Lifecycle
To prevent sprawl, the chapter estate is capped at 100 chapters (`CHAPTER_CAP = 100`)[^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Estate expansion requires coalescing or retiring existing chapters. Chapter records follow a formal lifecycle with five human-assigned states[^evt-community-events-pr-48]:
- `Active`: Verified active chapter with ongoing community activity.
- `Provisioned`: Initialized folder and channel resources awaiting launch.
- `Dormant`: Inactive chapter identified for community triage or reactivation.
- `Merged`: Consolidated into another regional chapter (recorded in the `Merged Into` column).
- `Deprecated`: Decommissioned chapter.

Chapter founding dates are deliberately omitted from automated inference due to bulk provisioning timestamp clustering; health tooling (`chapter_health.py`) ranks observed activity without mutating status records[^evt-community-events-pr-48].

## Organizer Channel Alignment
The skill synchronizes accepted organizers into the global `#local-champs` Slack room via `invite_organizers.py` and audits discrepancies with `audit_organizers.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Members who are not accepted organizers but reside in the leadership room are excluded from cross-chapter mismatch tallies to prevent alerting on legitimate leadership roles[^evt-community-events-pr-48].

## Audit Invariants and Measurement Limits
The audit system enforces the principle of "silence versus ignorance" when interpreting Slack and workspace activity[^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- **Silence vs. Ignorance**: Partial sweeps, stale sweeps, missing token scopes, or archived channels must produce an explicit "cannot say" state rather than an inference of inactivity or missing accounts[^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Scope Verification**: Scopes (such as `groups:read` or `users:read.email`) are validated prior to execution to prevent operational failures from being misreported as member non-compliance[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Anti-Proxy Invariant**: Channel or member `updated` timestamps are never used as activity proxies due to bulk migration artifacts; only genuine human edits (`topic.last_set`, human-dated messages, or admin Analytics CSV exports) serve as evidence floors[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Estate capped at 100 chapters; lifecycle statuses introduced; `#local-champs` automated reconciliation and measurement-limit guardrails deployed[^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate v0.1 draft shared contract identities, causal relationships, interpretation rules, and OpenTelemetry crosswalks from PR #51.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and behavioral identity hierarchies across agent sessions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and behavioral specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize identity hierarchies, turn boundaries, and causal execution graphs across multi-turn agent sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. It establishes common semantic relationships between agent conversational contexts, execution runtimes, model calls, and external side effects.

The specification harmonizes distributed tracing paradigms with agentic control flows, aligning with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI semantic conventions while accommodating non-linear agent behaviors such as human checkpoints and asynchronous tool invocations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity Hierarchy
The trace model formalizes eight distinct entity identities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Conversation**: The persistent conversational scope spanning one or more user interactions.
- **Runtime Session**: The underlying agent process execution lifecycle hosting model loops and tool invocations.
- **Turn**: The distinct conversational turn demarcated by input receipt and agent response synthesis.
- **Model Call**: Individual foundation model inference requests and responses.
- **Proposed Action**: Structured requests formulated by the agent prior to evaluation or execution.
- **Approval Decision**: Gatekeeper determinations recorded at an [approval checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) or [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Tool Execution**: Concrete execution instances of invoked tools or subagents.
- **External Effect**: Quantifiable side effects applied to external systems and environments.

## Relationships and Graph Traversal
The model articulates six core relationships among identities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
1. Structural nesting (conversations encompass runtime sessions, which encapsulate turns).
2. Model invocation causality (turns trigger model calls).
3. Action synthesis (model calls emit proposed actions).
4. Governance resolution (proposed actions require approval decisions where boundary policies dictate).
5. Tool dispatch (approved actions trigger tool executions).
6. State impact (tool executions produce external effects).

## Interpretation Rules
The contract establishes rigid interpretation constraints to preserve causal fidelity across heterogeneous collectors [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Unknown over Zero**: A missing observation MUST be interpreted as an unknown state rather than an assertion of zero events or absence of activity.
- **Correlation Deduplication**: Duplicate event observations deduplicate deterministically using their canonical correlation key.
- **Order Invariance**: Out-of-order trace ingestion or reordered event arrival MUST NOT alter the derived causal resolution or evaluation answer.

## Semantic Crosswalks
The trace model maps directly to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and standard AAIF vocabulary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51], allowing OTel-compliant collectors to project agent execution graphs into standard tracing backends without losing behavioral context.

# Lifecycle History
The shared contract was introduced as v0.1 draft in PR #51 within the Observability and Traceability Working Group to establish shared identity definitions and baseline turn boundary rules [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation suite and multi-type grading harness benchmarking agent skill selection, pipeline sequencing, and governance compliance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical evaluation harness used to benchmark and validate agent operational workflows, skill invocations, and policy compliance across community operations [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]. The suite pairs synthetic and historical operational scenarios with deterministic and model-based grading criteria to prevent operational drift and security violations.

The suite measures agent behavior against foundational patterns, including [deterministic acceptance gates](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [proposal-execution splits](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), ensuring agents report proposals prior to executing external modifications.

# Architecture / Specification

## Evaluation Scenarios

### Sync Front Door (`sync-front-door`)
The front door synchronization evaluation tests agent behavior when operational stores (spreadsheets, Google Drive folders, and Slack channels) drift out of synchronization across the estate [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]:
- **Invocation Scope**: Runs within a 16-turn budget and 600-second timeout, restricted to authorized operational skills [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a].
- **Sequence Verification (`order_is_respected.md`)**: An LLM-based grader verifies that the agent proposes or runs the pipeline as an ordered sequence rather than arbitrary steps [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
- **Read-Before-Write Enforcement**: The grader strictly penalizes any agent claiming to write data prematurely; chapter records and CRM listings must be validated before proposing Google Drive access grants or Slack modifications [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

### Legal Footer Compliance (`announcement-post`)
Evaluates public announcement copy generation against mandatory legal and community governance disclosures [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]:
- **Deterministic Regex Grading (`legal_footer.md`)**: Asserts that attendee-facing copy contains standing links to both the [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and the Privacy Policy in either order (`code-of-conduct[\s\S]*privacy-policy|privacy-policy[\s\S]*code-of-conduct`) [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].
- **Drift Prevention**: Verifies that neither link is dropped during copy drafting or summarization passes [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

# Lifecycle History
The evaluation suite was authored to guard operational automation across AAIF community chapters against unauthorized writes and compliance degradation [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a, ^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5, ^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational automation skill managing chapter room mapping, spreadsheet-driven configuration, and human-gated alias resolutions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill provides modular automation and audit tooling for managing AAIF community chapters, channel discovery, and organizer access across collaboration platforms [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]. The skill relies on live, sheet-managed configuration rather than static repository files, keeping configuration authority directly with community organizers.

In alignment with the [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), the skill prohibits autonomous mapping of channel aliases, requiring human confirmation whenever non-exact matches occur [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapters List Configuration Schema
Audit and sync engines read chapter assignments directly from three core columns on the Community Chapters List spreadsheet [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:
- **`Slack Channel`**: The chapter's primary local channel when it deviates from standard naming (e.g., `San Francisco -> bay-area`). Country-level channels are explicitly excluded to avoid false local coverage reporting [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **`Organizer Channel`**: The private organizers' room when differing from `<city>-organizers` [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **`Country Channel`**: Regional channels serving the broader territory (e.g., `india` or `africa`). Recorded strictly as regional coverage, never local chapter coverage [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **`Ops Notes`**: Free-text manual annotations displayed in health reports but never programmatically written or parsed [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

A literal `none` acts as a sentinel indicating that no channel exists, preventing fallback guessing, while blank cells trigger standard heuristic scanning [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

## Deterministic Prefix and Suffix Resolution
Heuristic matching settings reside in a dedicated `Slack Config` tab on the spreadsheet [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:
- **Load-Bearing Order**: Rows are scanned top-to-bottom in explicit priority order. The sentinel `(none)` represents a bare city slug, followed by prefixes like `meetup-` and `aaif-` [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Fail-Safe Aborts**: A blank value cell or an unrecognized `Setting` key aborts execution immediately to prevent silent matching expansion or dropped rules [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

## Human Approval on Alias Matches
The skill mandates an explicit proposal-execution boundary:
- Automated writes are permitted solely on exact channel name matches [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- Any near-miss, alias, or inferred channel mapping must be proposed to a human operator with full context (chapter, candidate channel, and member count) and await explicit confirmation before committing changes [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

# Lifecycle History
The configuration mechanism was migrated from hardcoded repository JSON (`scripts/channel_map.json`) to the Community Chapters List spreadsheet to empower non-technical organizers to maintain room mappings directly [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational automation skill and multi-phase sync pipeline managing chapter lifecycle, CRM data validation, and workspace governance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite orchestrates chapter synchronization, intake triage, directory health, and Google Workspace provisioning across the Agentic AI Foundation's local chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. Re-architected following procedural guidelines from the [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) specification, operational workflows are consolidated under a unified sync pipeline (`aaif-sync`) that strictly segregates execution phases while enforcing an explicit [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) for chapter and organizer triage[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Architecture / Specification

## Pipeline Model: Phases and Stages
Operational synchronization is structured along two orthogonal dimensions—phase (the operational subject) and stage (execution progression)[^evt-community-events-pr-49]:
- **Phases**: Dedicated modules covering chapter lifecycle, organizers, Slack membership, CRM synchronization, and badge allocation[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Stages**: Every phase executes strictly through `gather`, `plan`, and `execute` stages, asserted at import time to prevent out-of-order execution[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

A central runner (`aaif-sync/scripts/sync.py`) orchestrates execution across all phases. In `--unattended` mode, approval-gated steps execute in read-only reporting mode to permit automated continuous monitoring without unintended state mutations[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

## Human Gates and Separation of Authority
- **Triage Gate**: Automated sweeps calculate intake and application queue depth but never decide approvals autonomously. If pending triage items exist, the runner exits with status code 2 to mandate human adjudication[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Ops Notes Guard**: Spreadsheets contain a designated `Ops Notes` column maintained exclusively by human administrators; scripts quote and surface these notes in reports but are prevented from modifying them[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

## Idempotency and Non-Idempotent Write Protection
To prevent resource proliferation and workspace corruption during network timeouts, Google Workspace (`gws`) calls enforce strict idempotency boundaries[^evt-community-events-pr-51]:
- **Non-Idempotent Retries**: Verbs that create resources (`drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, `addSheet`) enforce `aaif_events.gws.NO_RETRY` so failed responses are never re-sent without verification[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Static Guardrails**: A dedicated checker (`scripts/check_non_idempotent_retries.py`) verifies call sites to prohibit default retry budgets on non-idempotent operations[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Telemetry and Credential Scrubbing**: Execution errors scrub sensitive environment variables (such as OAuth tokens and Slack credentials) from tracebacks and log child processes only by verb, suppressing payload bodies from stderr logs[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

## Data Validation and Findings Reporting
- **Findings Schema**: Operational tools emit standardized finding records (`lib/aaif_events/findings.py`) with `--json-out`, capturing finding kind, target entity, detail, severity, and suggested remediation steps into an aggregated `report.html`[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Data Validation Unioning**: Data validation lists across fragmented `sqref` ranges are unioned to resolve split column ranges correctly, eliminating false-positive stale dropdown alerts in chapter CRM workbooks[^evt-community-events-pr-50].
- **Ephemeral Caches**: Ephemeral caches (such as Slack directory dumps) enforce a 24-hour expiration (`jsoncache.MAX_AGE`) and are validated against git inclusion via `check_state_never_committed.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #49 (2026-09)**: Rewrote skills to be procedural, established the two-axis `aaif-sync` pipeline, standardized finding outputs, and enforced the human triage gate[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **PR #50 (2026-09)**: Corrected CRM dropdown handling for split single-column `sqref` ranges in Excel workbooks[^evt-community-events-pr-50].
- **PR #51 (2026-09)**: Consolidated GWS wrapper scripts into `lib/aaif_events/gws`, introduced `NO_RETRY` for non-idempotent write operations, and implemented credential scrubbing in tracebacks[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting technical group within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for standardizing terminology, curating shared taxonomies, and maintaining an ecosystem map of agentic AI frameworks and tools[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]. Reporting directly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group processes terminology proposals through structured review syncs and coordinates publication of the Foundation's landscape catalog[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Architecture / Specification

## Terminology Review Cadence
The workstream operates a phased backlog evaluation model to process candidate agentic terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]:
- **Review Syncs**: Multi-session community review calls systematically assess terms against existing taxonomy entries to eliminate duplication and refine scope[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **Batch Approval**: Accepted concepts are batched into formal pull requests and presented to the Technical Committee for consensus approval votes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **Reporting**: Monthly summary reports document term progression, review velocity against the backlog, and schema updates for the landscape web portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Secured charter approvals, established core metadata schemas, and launched web portal deployment pipelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **2026-07**: Evaluated 46 candidate terms across four review syncs and admitted 13 in the workstream's initial taxonomy PR, completing review for 67 terms in the 128-term backlog[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **2026-08**: Screened 53 terms across three review syncs, retaining 37, and prepared four PRs for a Technical Committee approval vote scheduled for 14 September 2026[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and behavioral identity across multi-turn agent sessions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) that defines how to trace an AI agent's execution across interactive turns, interruptions, and distributed system boundaries using OpenTelemetry conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The specification establishes a shared contract governing which relationships to record, how to correlate work across boundaries, and how downstream ingestion systems should interpret turn states [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Verification Questions

The trace model is anchored on four operational questions evaluated across test scenarios [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity:** Identifying which conversational or execution turns belong together across session pauses, process restarts, and resumptions without querying private runtime state.
- **Calls and retries:** Accurately attributing foundation model calls and retries to their initiating turn without double-counting work.
- **Approvals:** Correlating human or automated approval decisions to specific proposed actions, tracking whether execution was authorized and dispatched [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831] (see [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)).
- **Effects:** Linking external side effects and mutated state back to the corresponding tool execution via independently instrumented services.

### Trace Boundaries and Vocabulary Alignment

The model adopts a candidate baseline convention of emitting one trace per turn while strictly preserving existing caller trace contexts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The telemetry schema separates conversation continuity, protocol sessions, and the broader agent trajectory, coordinating canonical naming with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Under the evidence model, missing observations indicate unknown state rather than success or zero, observed approval does not imply policy enforcement, and payload content capture remains strictly opt-in [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

### Implementation Scope

The reference test scenario models a support workflow: investigating a delayed order, proposing a ticket, requesting explicit human approval, executing ticket creation against a mock backend, and resuming the conversation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Portability is validated across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and a second independent agent runtime or SDK, tested against multiple model providers and evaluated with dual independent trace readers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Lifecycle History

The nine-task execution plan was established through August 2026 working group consensus and formally merged into the working documents repository [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]. Tasks span baseline capture, shared contract definition, test suites, multi-runtime implementations, query readers, and upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention contributions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body advancing shared telemetry standards, vendor-neutral trace formats, and diagnostic conventions across agent reasoning and execution lifecycles [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The working group convenes practitioners, enterprise vendors, and standards organizations (notably OpenTelemetry) to close observability gaps across heterogeneous agent frameworks, protocols, and tool execution boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Architecture / Specification

### Governance and Operations

The working group operates under leadership appointed by Platinum and Gold Foundation members, serving terms from March 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:
- **Chair:** Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco)
- **Co-Chair:** Matthew Lee (Datadog)

The group holds biweekly public meetings on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT, using GitHub issues and pull requests as the authoritative record for durable decisions, roadmaps, and monthly Technical Committee reports [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

### Primary Deliverables

1. **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** A nine-task implementation plan correlating agent turns, model calls, approval decisions, and external system effects using OpenTelemetry semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
2. **Landscape Survey and Use Cases:** Maintained empirical inventories analyzing existing agent tracing architectures and practitioner requirements across model runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
3. **Cross-Group Harmonization:** Collaborative taxonomy crosswalks with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define standard interaction turn boundaries and state definitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical group standardizing workflow patterns, orchestration primitives, and integration architectures connecting AI agents with business processes and external systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. The group establishes reference models that harmonize human-in-the-loop approvals, autonomous convergence loops, and enterprise system boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Architecture / Specification

### Governance and Work Streams

The working group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. Technical activities are organized across three formal work streams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:
- **Reference Architectures:** Scoping and standardizing recurring architectural templates such as [Single Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md).
- **Critical Use Cases:** Identifying and prioritizing production agentic integration scenarios.
- **Taxonomy:** Defining workflow domain vocabulary in alignment with the global [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

### Inter-Group Coordination

In its governance reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the working group highlighted the operational risk of divergent, overlapping definitions emerging across different technical working groups, advocating for empowering the global taxonomy workstream to enforce consistent terminology across the Foundation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations Skill (`aaif-sync`) is an operational toolchain and automation skill used by the Agentic AI Foundation to synchronize community chapters, organizers, event platforms, and CRM spreadsheets across Google Workspace and Slack [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. The pipeline automates multi-step intake, reconciliation, and reporting across local chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-52].

# Architecture / Specification

### Pipeline Execution and Performance Architecture

The synchronization workflow executes as an 18-step sequential pipeline [^evt-community-events-pr-52] [^evt-community-events-pr-53]. Key execution controls include:
- **Per-Run Ephemeral Memos:** To prevent redundant network lookups across steps, report runs utilize append-only `jsoncache.RunMemo` files with restricted permissions (0600) for Slack (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO`) and Google Workspace (`AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`) [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. The memo files are deleted immediately upon pipeline completion or interruption; `--write` runs bypass read caching to guarantee write-read consistency [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Parallelized Workbook Fetching:** The `sync_crm` engine queries chapter Drive workbooks concurrently through a six-worker thread pool while preserving sequential planning and scoping downloads by folder ID to eliminate path collision risks [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Process Sleep Prevention:** On macOS hosts, the runner executes `keep_awake()` via `caffeinate -i -w <runner pid>` to prevent workstation sleep and credential expiration during multi-step runs [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural guideline organizing workflow reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs while evaluating machine-readable workflow design specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model structures workflow reference architectures around recognizable, practitioner-centric jobs rather than abstract orchestration mechanics. It establishes a multi-tiered hierarchy linking reusable workflow patterns, such as [durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) and [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), into composed job-oriented reference architectures evaluated against real-world use case scenarios [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

# Architecture / Specification
Under the job-oriented model, architectural artifacts are organized across three primary strata:
- **Reusable Patterns:** Granular solutions solving recurring workflow challenges, such as the [approval checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) or [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].
- **Job-Oriented Reference Architectures:** Compositions of patterns, capability roles, boundary controls, guarantees, and exit states tailored to a defined operational task [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Empirical use cases that validate whether a reference architecture satisfies concrete operational requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

## Evolution and Workflow Design Specifications
The workstream is evaluating two north-star trajectories regarding the long-term artifact model [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]:
- **Option A (Reusable Guidance Only):** The reference architecture repository remains a human-readable knowledgebase of patterns, architectures, and validations, leaving implementation-specific documentation formats to adopting organizations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].
- **Option B (Workflow Design Specification - WDS):** The reference architecture also produces a formal, versioned, schema-validated, machine-readable specification (such as YAML) serving as the canonical source of truth from which diagrams, architectural reviews, and execution handoffs can be derived [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

proposed_concept.title: PostHog Observability and Behavioral Analytics
proposed_concept.description: Product analytics and telemetry platform evaluated for AI agent telemetry, addressing pseudonymous identifier classification and cross-border transfer requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
PostHog is an open-source product analytics and event capture platform evaluated as a telemetry backend for AI agent workflows. Architectural assessments examine its event ingestion pipelines, user session tracking, and the jurisdictional implications of its client identification model [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference implementation captures interaction telemetry via persistent installation identifiers (`installation_id`), assigned as random UUIDs intended to trace journeys across agent sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

## Privacy and Jurisdictional Classification
While initial implementation documentation characterized random installation UUIDs as anonymous-by-design and free of personally identifiable information (PII), architectural reviews have highlighted key jurisdictional tensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55]:
- **Pseudonymous Data Under GDPR:** Under EU and UK GDPR (Recitals 26 and 30), persistent identifiers used for longitudinal session tracking constitute pseudonymous personal data rather than anonymous data [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Data Residency and Cross-Border Transfers:** Hardcoded transmission to US endpoints (such as `us.i.posthog.com`) triggers cross-border data transfer compliance obligations for deployments operating under European privacy regimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Regime-Keyed Classification:** Architectural feedback proposes integrating explicit classification metadata into the [reference architecture template](../guidelines/reference-architecture-template.md) to categorize identifier types across personal data, personal information, and PII standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining agent identity, credential delegation, decentralized trust, and multi-jurisdiction legal role mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group defines technical standards and reference architectures for autonomous agent identity, credential delegation, and verifiable operational boundaries. The group evaluates identity lifecycle management, cryptographic trust verification, and regulatory alignment across sovereign jurisdictions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group develops models governing how agents establish provenance, obtain delegation mandates, and interact with protected boundaries.

## Jurisdictional Terminology and Legal Roles
A primary workstream review focuses on disambiguating common engineering terms from defined legal concepts across regulatory jurisdictions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]:
- **Operator:** Contrasting general operational descriptions with EU AI Act Article 3(8), which defines an umbrella covering providers, deployers, authorised representatives, importers, and distributors [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Relying Party:** Distinguishing generic service consumers from the registered entity under eIDAS 2 (Regulation 2024/1183, Article 5b) requiring pre-declared use cases prior to wallet interaction [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Consent and Consent Receipts:** Reconciling basic authorization records with statutory definitions in GDPR Articles 4(11) and 7, ISO/IEC 27560 structures, and PSD2 Article 64 strong customer authentication [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Attestation:** Separating IETF RATS architectural evidence from electronic attestations of attributes defined under eIDAS 2 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Mandates and Agency:** Disambiguating protocol delegation payloads from civil-law contracts of agency and EUDI power-of-representation attestations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Log Holder and Cross-Organization Hops:** Incorporating legal-role designations (controller, processor, provider, deployer) into delegation chains and evidence models such as the [evidence record specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate multi-jurisdictional audit log retention rules and pseudonymity requirements from Issues 54 and 55.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, trace specifications, cross-boundary verification, and regulatory audit compliance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group develops open telemetry models, execution trace specifications, and verification mechanisms for agentic systems. It oversees standards such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) while aligning telemetry lifecycles with international audit and data retention mandates [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

# Architecture / Specification
The group addresses technical and legal requirements governing the capture, storage, and exchange of agent execution evidence:
- **Regulatory Retention Mapping:** Disambiguating system design requirements from retention duties under the EU AI Act, separating Article 12 logging capabilities from Article 19 and Article 26(6) retention duties imposed on providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].
- **Audit-Required Event Schema:** Formalizing event envelope requirements—covering timestamps, system identity, actor attribution, human oversight interventions, input/output references, and affected-person links—keyed by jurisdiction and legal role [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].
- **Multi-Regime Consent and Residency Envelopes:** Expanding envelope metadata beyond single-regime assumptions to accommodate jurisdictional differences including US state opt-out structures, South Korea PIPA, Singapore PDPA, and Japan APPI purpose constraints [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].
- **Pseudonymous Identifier Governance:** Establishing classification criteria for persistent identifiers to reflect that longitudinal pseudonymous identifiers constitute personal data under GDPR Recital 30, directly affecting telemetry routing in tools such as [PostHog](../resources/posthog.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group defines empirical evaluation methodologies, quality benchmarks, and verification frameworks for autonomous AI agents. The group coordinates technical deliverables including foundational taxonomies, quality threshold frameworks, and self-assessment evaluation artifacts [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-8][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its outputs across several core deliverables while ensuring alignment with international regulatory and metrology terminology:
- **D1 Deliverable - Taxonomy:** Establishing standard definitions and classification schemes for agent accuracy, failure behaviors, and reliability metrics [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-8].
- **D4 Deliverable - Quality Thresholds:** Authoring baseline quality thresholds with explicit jurisdictional coverage statements to avoid conflation with EU AI Act Article 15(1) robustness requirements or Article 40 harmonised standards (CEN-CENELEC JTC 21), while contrasting with voluntary frameworks like the NIST AI RMF [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].
- **D6 Deliverable - Evaluation and Consistency Guidance:** Creating self-assessment guidance, conformance validation artifacts, and consistency verification suites, with naming calibrated to prevent unintended confusion with statutory "conformity assessment" procedures under EU AI Act Article 43 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].
