proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group bridges international artificial intelligence regulatory policy developments with technical implementations across the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319] Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann and Deborah Eng, the group evaluates regional legal frameworks and translates statutory mandates into concrete operational controls, risk tiers, and architectural verification requirements for autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its comparative regulatory gap analysis against 16 core baseline themes:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]
- **Governance & accountability**: Ownership structures, RACI matrices, sign-offs, and formal risk acceptance.
- **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Categorization of permissible versus prohibited behaviors and tiered control thresholds.
- **Architecture**: Reference deployment patterns, trust boundaries, and control placement.
- **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication and authorization models, acting-on-behalf-of assertions, and agent registries.
- **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Machine-enforceable business rules, policy-as-code, and hard boundaries.
- **Data protection & privacy**: PII handling, data minimization, retention schedules, and data residency.
- **Security & access controls**: Least privilege, credential management, boundary segmentation, and scoped tool permissions.
- **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, robustness benchmarks, drift detection, and change control.
- **Human oversight**: HITL/HOTL escalation pathways, override mechanisms, and automated supervision.
- **Action management**: Pre-execution validation checks, dual control patterns, and reversibility mechanisms.
- **Monitoring & logging**: Tamper-evident audit trails, prompt/tool invocation logs, and decision journals.
- **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection testing, tool abuse simulations, and autonomous failure evaluations.
- **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence, model provenance, and tool supply chain verification.
- **Incident response**: Autonomous anomaly detection, runtime containment protocols, and regulatory breach notification.
- **Transparency & user disclosure**: End-user notices, model explanations, and disclosure of synthetic interaction.
- **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Retention schedules and deterministic execution reproducibility.

The group evaluates geographical policy instruments against these themes using a standardized "golden source" AI prompt to extract statutory requirements uniformly across international jurisdictions.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group ratified the 16-theme baseline and finalized the golden-source extraction prompt to initiate phase two comparative and gap analysis across regional AI governance frameworks.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops threat models, security controls, architectural patterns, and practical implementation guidelines to secure agentic systems and safeguard user data.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] The group operates cross-cutting workstreams focused on agentic security best practices, threat modeling gap analysis, design patterns, and cross-working group alignment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates four primary technical deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: A practitioner catalog formatted as actionable static-analysis rules and defense patterns covering workload identity, least privilege, and prompt injection defense.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: An architectural gap analysis mapping agentic attack surfaces, sandbox escape vectors, and control placements.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: A library of architectural templates, including isolated runtimes and microVM-based isolation approaches such as Eclipse Enclave.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An alignment framework tracking dependency boundaries and security posture across AAIF technical groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

The group collaborates externally with standard bodies and industry initiatives, including ETSI TC SAI regarding cybersecurity requirements for AI agents, OpenSSF on secure agentic framework tooling, and OWASP's agentic top-10 projects.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the group initiated integration of Erin Farr's security best practices guide and established the cross-WG review checklist.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] In September 2026, the group concluded review comments on the initial Best Practices guide release, adopted a standing PR review window convention in contributing documentation, and opened discussions on microVM isolation frameworks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and behavioral identity verification across agent boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification standardizing agent turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, behavioral identity assertions, and boundary-crossing interactions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42] Developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, the model provides an interoperable schema for evaluating distributed agent reasoning traces and verifying output integrity across runtime environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model standardizes causal telemetry validation through a multi-task execution roadmap. Task 4 defines a vendor-neutral conformance test kit and contribution template designed to verify telemetry relationships when exported across distributed backends:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Relationship Conformance Checks**: Tests validating trace behavior under degraded network conditions, including dropped, out-of-order, or duplicated event payloads. Telemetry consumers must preserve causal state (e.g., verifying that duplicate receipt delivery leaves one confirmed receipt, while dropped receipts register creation as unconfirmed rather than absent).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Synthetic Data and Content Opt-In**: Test fixtures utilize synthetic event records with explicit opt-in flags for sensitive payload content capture to ensure compliance with privacy boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **OTel Conformance Extension**: Extends OpenTelemetry conformance tooling with specialized agent relationship assertions, decoupling test execution from specific runtime implementations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Test Segmentation**: Separate labeling and evaluation harness tiers for deterministic offline unit tests versus live integration scenarios.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

# Lifecycle History
In August and September 2026, the working group ratified the nine-task execution plan for the trace model and established Task 4 (Issue #42) to provide automated relationship verification fixtures and contribution templates.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture evaluating boundary telemetry propagation, control-plane evidence provenance, and kernel-enforced runtime tracing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Model is an evaluation matrix and reference architecture analyzing telemetry propagation, security attestation, and evidence provenance across critical agentic boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52] Developed within the Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group of the Observability and Traceability Working Group, the model categorizes telemetry expectations between agents, runtimes, external tools, gateways, and human supervisors.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]

# Architecture / Specification
The model standardizes telemetry and security attributes across four primary operational boundaries:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]
- **Agent → Tool (MCP / CLI)**: Evaluates command payload logging, tool provenance, and security isolation at the invocation boundary.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]
- **Agent → Gateway / Runtime**: Covers interactions with policy gateways and execution engines (such as the SAF-M-74 class and the nono runtime). It models enforcement layers categorized as kernel, broker, or proxy, alongside cryptographic execution hashes and golden vector validation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]
- **Agent → Human (HITL)**: Captures human-in-the-loop approval relationships, tracking approval checkpoints, delegation chains, and decision attribution records.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]
- **Agent → Agent (A2A)**: Evaluates mutual identity verification, authorization delegation, and distributed turn tracking.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]

A key technical challenge identified in kernel-enforced sandboxed runtimes (such as nono) is that W3C distributed trace context (`TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`, `BAGGAGE`) is not automatically propagated into the execution sandbox by default, requiring explicit environment allow-lists to correlate in-sandbox telemetry with outer workflow traces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, PR #52 expanded the model by formalizing below-L7 kernel-enforced runtime rows, defining the Agent → Gateway/Runtime and Agent → Human matrix mappings, and documenting trace propagation boundaries in sandboxed environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]

proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy schema and empirical inventory categorizing real-world production agentic workflows, execution topologies, and boundary controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification framework is a structured taxonomy and empirical inventory documenting production agentic workflows across industry deployments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51] Maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, it classifies workflows across architectural dimensions including trigger mechanism, human-in-the-loop patterns, agent cardinality, coordination topologies, and boundary controls.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Architecture / Specification
The inventory classifies production workflows across standardized dimensions:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
- **Trigger**: Invocations triggered by webhooks, manual human dispatch, event streams, or scheduled cron routines.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
- **HITL Pattern**: The level of human intervention, spanning explicit approval gates, exception escalations, or none (fully informational outputs).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
- **Agent Cardinality & Coordination**: Evaluates single-agent sufficient deployments versus multi-agent swarms, contrasting fixed sequential pipelines against dynamic autonomous graphs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
- **Enforcement Boundary**: Distinguishes between runtime-enforced gates and job-level permission isolation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

### Production Inventory Cases
- **Upstream SDK Release Impact Analysis**: Sourced from MCP Inspector (`sdk-watch.yml`), this sequential SDLC workflow evaluates upstream dependency changes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51] A scheduled cron trigger launches a deterministic script to file an upgrade issue. An analysis agent runs in an isolated job with read-only tokens and restricted search tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`), preventing shell execution or outbound network writes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51] The generated report is scanned for verbatim credentials before passing as an artifact to a separate write-scoped job, illustrating a permission-enforced proposal/execution split without requiring convergence loops or runtime gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, PR #51 contributed the Upstream SDK release impact analysis case study to the SDLC section of the inventory, formalizing permission-isolated analysis pipelines.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, cross-boundary verification, and interoperable observability specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to survey, coordinate, and standardize agent observability, causal trace formats, and telemetry schemas across the foundation's projects and member ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24] and stewards core foundational artifacts including the Prior Work landscape survey, the agent observability use case inventory, and the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) execution plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

The group collaborates across peer bodies including the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) to align security event normalization, evidence grades, and audit logging with runtime telemetry [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

# Architecture / Specification

## Landscape and Upstream Alignment
The working group maintains an active survey of industry specifications and multi-agent frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]:
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI:** Tracking the dedicated `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` repository covering agent lifecycle, workflow execution, tool dispatch, and plan spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Protocol Interoperability:** Integrating instrumentation across Agent-to-Agent (A2A), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and AGNTCY Observe protocol specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Security & Event Schemas:** Mapping agent operations to the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF v1.9) AI Agent profile and OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Environment Telemetry:** Correlating agent self-reporting with trusted environment telemetry such as OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (OBI) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

## Use Case Taxonomies
The group's standard requirements derive from an empirical taxonomy across nine operational domains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
1. **Debugging and Root Cause Analysis:** Explaining non-deterministic outcomes, decision context, and retry bottlenecks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
2. **Cost Management and Optimization:** Tracking token consumption, step latency, and cost per successful outcome [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
3. **Code Attribution and Provenance:** AI-generated source tracing and differential code security reviews [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
4. **Evaluation and Quality Assurance:** Continuous benchmark grading, model regressions, and configuration comparisons [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
5. **Safety and Compliance:** Real-world action audit trails, authorization scope enforcement, and tamper-evident evidence logs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
6. **Multi-Agent Systems:** Tracing cross-boundary messaging, state delegation, and causal cascades [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
7. **Operational Monitoring:** Real-time health metrics, active session counts, and queue capacity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
8. **Research and Improvement:** Failure-mode discovery, synthetic trajectory harvesting, and cross-framework benchmarks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
9. **Identity and Ownership:** Cross-surface identity resolution across execution environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-15:** Initial publication of the Prior Work landscape survey and Use Cases catalog [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **2026-08-13:** Major refresh of the Prior Work landscape documenting OTel GenAI's dedicated repository migration, AGNTCY Observe 1.0.43, and OCSF 1.9 agent structures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **2026-08-18:** Cross-boundary observability framework coordination reviewed by the Technical Committee in conjunction with the Security and Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **2026-08:** Launch of nine-task implementation roadmap for the Agent Behavior Trace Model, including dual-reader independent interoperability verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and behavioral identity across heterogeneous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and tracing specification developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and cross-agent behavioral identity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It enables tools, gateways, and analysis engines to reconstruct the sequence of intent, approval, execution, and observed effect across distributed agentic workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

The specification addresses the limitations of conventional APM span trees by establishing causal graph mechanics capable of representing asynchronous, suspended, resumed, and delegated agent operations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements
The trace model requires implementations to conform to five architectural baselines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
- **Source and Trust Distinction:** Telemetry records must identify their producer observation point, strictly differentiating agent self-reporting from framework, gateway, sandbox, OS, or security-sensor evidence, including signing and attestation metadata [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Privacy and Governance:** Context fields must support redaction, data minimization, classification tags, access controls, and retention markers while prohibiting raw credential or secret capture [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Completeness and Sampling Declaration:** Telemetry records must explicitly indicate sampling decisions, collection gaps, and dropped-event counts to distinguish complete audit trails from opportunistic diagnostic traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Schema and Environment Versioning:** All traces carry explicit schema versions, semconv releases, runtime instrumentation versions, and model configurations to ensure longitudinal comparability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Causality and Non-Linear Ordering:** Causal graph ordering is preserved using stable identifiers across sessions, tasks, messages, and delegations rather than relying solely on wall-clock timestamps or strict parent-child hierarchies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

## Interoperability Verification
To ensure the trace model is not bound to a single vendor implementation, the execution roadmap mandates independent interpretation verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. Two distinct, independently written readers or query engines must parse exported agent telemetry without private runtime state or shared reconstruction code, verifying [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:
1. Consistent identification of proposed actions and explicit approvals despite differing record arrival orders [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
2. Attribution of execution steps to confirmed environmental effects versus unconfirmed effects when receipts are withheld [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
3. Graceful handling and surface reporting of incomplete or conflicting evidence streams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-15:** Observability use-case and requirement mapping initiated in the working group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **2026-08:** Nine-task execution plan formulated by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, establishing Task 7 independent reader validation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining shared workflow models, common terminology, and reference architectures for agentic process integration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group establishes standardized workflow patterns, common execution models, and reference architectures for deploying agentic AI systems within enterprise processes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group focuses on architectural clarity, separating agent proposal generation from controlled execution boundaries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

In August 2026, the working group delivered the Foundation's first shipped artifact with the formal plenary approval of its Phase One Core Terms taxonomy draft.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical outputs across three primary workstreams:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

- **Reference Architectures**: Develops vendor-neutral architectural templates and boundary definitions. The deliverable scope locks to two foundational architectures—`../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md` ("human-approved operation") and `../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md`—supported by core principles in `../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md` and contributing guidelines.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] It employs a four-outcome architectural validation framework (`validated`, `partial`, `candidate`, `no fit`) to test designs against empirical use cases.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Taxonomy**: Establishes formal terminology for process primitives in `../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md`. The Phase One vocabulary adopted "activity" over "step" and defines a workflow as a composition of activities, while intentionally scoping out gate and evaluation terms to partner working groups such as `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` and `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Critical Use Cases**: Maintains the empirical catalog of production agentic workflows, categorizing deployments into human-approved operations, bounded autonomous remediations, and exception detection/escalation cohorts.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Lifecycle History

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry structures, execution tracing specifications, and evidence verification mechanisms for AI agents operating across distributed tool and framework boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group harmonizes runtime monitoring with open standards, including OpenTelemetry and the Common Trace Format.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

The group coordinates core specifications including `../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md` and boundary observability matrices across agent, model, and gateway execution planes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's technical initiatives span several key areas:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Standardizes portable telemetry context across agent harnesses, SDKs, gateways, and collector backends to trace causal execution graphs without exposing raw model chain-of-thought reasoning.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Maps telemetry metadata and context propagation across agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP boundaries (`../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md` and `../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **ARD Trust-Pipeline Observability**: In collaboration with `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` and `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`, provides proof-of-concept instrumentation tracing the `../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md` lifecycle from client discovery through identity verification to skill execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Taxonomy Contributions**: Curates observability vocabulary for `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`, securing consensus on terms including Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Finalized Agent Behavior Trace Model initial scope and scheduled reference library development led by Matthew Lee; completed cross-boundary metadata mappings; demonstrated ARD trust-pipeline observability with Agent Gateway; and folded the Orchestration & Coordination focus group into the primary working group track.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification defining turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and portable context propagation across agents and gateways.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification that standardizes the capture of execution context, causal relationships, and decision outcomes across heterogeneous agent frameworks, SDKs, and telemetry backends.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Developed within the `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`, the model relies on portable telemetry context to link planning and decisions to downstream execution and results without requiring the capture of raw model chain-of-thought text.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

Rather than replacing existing industry standards such as OpenTelemetry GenAI, the specification complements them by identifying semantic gaps and providing conformance tests for complex multi-agent and cross-boundary workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model architecture is structured around core operational requirements:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

- **Portable Telemetry Context**: Preserves cross-system causal lineage across autonomous agent steps, gateway hops, and external service invocations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Canonical Identity and Correlation**: Defines standard identifiers for agent instances, turns, and delegations to support multi-agent context reuse and correlation across long-running tasks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Privacy-Preserving Evidence**: Captures cryptographic or verifiable execution evidence and structured decision rationale while honoring privacy controls by suppressing sensitive prompt payloads or unverified thoughts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Reference Implementation & Testing**: Comprises a reference instrumentation library, synthetic multi-agent test workloads, and automated conformance suites to benchmark telemetry completeness.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Initial specification scope formally agreed by the Observability & Traceability WG; implementation plan established combining a reference library and conformance suite led by Matthew Lee, targeting alignment with OpenTelemetry GenAI.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body responsible for defining threat modeling frameworks, security best practices, privacy design patterns, and cross-cutting security review checklists across agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the working group focuses on mitigating vulnerabilities unique to autonomous decision-making, model tool use, and multi-agent coordination[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The group structures its core initiatives across several designated workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating industry frameworks (OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Systems, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) against STRIDE and PASTA methodologies, incorporating Human-User-Agent (HUA) interactions and Model Context Protocol (MCP) telemetry[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Authored by Fernando Lucktemberg, Matthew Khouzam, and Erin Farr, establishing defensive engineering practices, baseline hardening, and static analysis recommendations while coordinating identity delegation with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, authoring structured templates and reference patterns for containment, tool privilege bounding, and safe multi-agent collaboration[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing security overlap criteria and joint review requirements with peer AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Coordinated through delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman to review and harmonize security and privacy terms within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group moved its meeting archives to a public-by-default posture and opened review on initial PR drafts for its Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22]. Concurrently, the group requested guidance from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to reconcile cross-WG ownership boundaries in response to protocol donations such as A2A[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing reusable orchestration patterns, execution profiles, and specification-driven reference architectures for deploying AI agents across enterprise business processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group harmonizes deterministic workflow systems with stochastic, agentic decision loops[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification
The group executes its charter through three primary workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]:

- **Reference Architectures**: Led by Mario and Zayne, this stream develops a specification-driven design pipeline converting business use cases into machine-readable YAML specifications, architectural diagrams, and documentation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The stream established seven discrete execution profiles (ranging from Profile 1: fully deterministic, to Profile 7: fully agentic), enforcing a "least agentic default" architectural recommendation, and defined six charter-derived architectural archetypes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Led by Kevin Ng (Telus) and Jodee Varney (Cisco) with contributions from Rocky Zhang (SAP), this track compiled and categorized an inventory of 89 enterprise use cases evaluated across primitives such as trigger mechanisms, human-in-the-loop patterns, agent count, coordination schemes, and workflow styles, converging on fewer than 10 reusable patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinated with Gala (co-chair of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)), aligning short-code workflow primitives and pattern definitions against foundation-wide taxonomy models prior to binding machine-readable schemas[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group completed an end-to-end demonstration of its specification-driven generation flow across invoice processing and autonomous maintenance workflows across deterministic and agentic execution profiles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The group scheduled joint cross-validation between its 89 use case inventory and reference architecture archetypes to prevent primitive divergence prior to formal WG adoption[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing interoperable telemetry standards, causal execution traces, and verification frameworks for tracking autonomous agent reasoning, tool invocations, and distributed task delegation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]. The group coordinates cross-cutting observability requirements across internal AAIF working groups and external standards bodies to ensure verifiable telemetry across execution boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains several active technical initiatives and governance frameworks:

- **Liaison Management**: The group operates a structured liaison tracker connecting internal Foundation workstreams (including MCP, Goose, and the Technical Committee) with external industry standards groups such as OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, Agent Trace, Monocle, and AGNTCY[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].
- **Trace Model Recommendation Framework**: The group manages the decision framework for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), employing candidate comparison criteria and an explicit adopt / extend / new-artifact evaluation path before standardizing new trace formats[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Evidence-Grade Ladder and Jurisdictional Requirements**: The group's telemetry requirements distinguish between technical record integrity mechanisms and legal evidentiary effect[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]. Evidentiary rungs are classified as explicit grades rather than use case identifiers, and normative telemetry mandates require recording the jurisdiction and statutory role of the record holder because the legal admissibility and weight of a record (including RFC 3161 timestamps) are determined by the relying party's legal regime rather than purely by technical integrity proofs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# Lifecycle History
The working group formalized cross-body tracking with its liaison roster in PR #18[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18]. In PR #19, it introduced a decision-neutral recommendation plan for agent tracing standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19], followed in PR #56 by normative clarifications qualifying evidence-grade rungs and decoupling technical timestamping from jurisdictional legal weight[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification and evaluation framework defining turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and portable context for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardization initiative under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) designed to capture multi-turn reasoning steps, subagent delegations, tool calls, and causal execution graphs across heterogeneous agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]. The initiative operates under a decision-neutral recommendation process that evaluates existing industry standards and candidate models prior to committing to a net-new specification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification framework and its governing recommendation plan define the following architectural components[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]:

- **Candidate Model Evaluation**: Comprehensive comparison of existing telemetry formats, including OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, W3C Trace Context, and domain-specific trace representations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Evaluation Criteria**: Multi-dimensional benchmark criteria measuring support for multi-turn boundary delineation, cross-boundary causal graphs, tool invocation tracing, replay fidelity, and runtime overhead[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Decision Path**: A structured adoption framework mapping whether the Foundation should adopt an existing open standard unchanged, define an extension profile, or author a standalone AAIF specification artifact[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Multi-Workstream Integration**: Integration of empirical inputs from working group use-case inventories, gap analyses, taxonomy harmonizations, and focus group reviews prior to milestone votes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

# Lifecycle History
Established under working group issue #12, the project adopted a formal recommendation plan in PR #19 to govern the evaluation of candidate standards and avoid premature specification fragmentation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

proposed_concept.title: Context
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining the information assembled and available to an agent when making a decision during an execution step.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Context is the information available to an agent when making a decision during an execution step [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82]. Within the Agentic AI Foundation taxonomy schema, context represents the assembled operational view presented to a model, encompassing incoming user messages, execution results from tools, retrieved external documentation, short- or long-term memory records, and system instructions configuring agent boundaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

# Architecture / Specification
Context functions as the bounded runtime information payload supplied to an agent at a given turn [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82]. Under the taxonomy definition, the scope of context covers:
- User messages and direct input directives (see `../taxonomy/prompt.md`).
- System prompts, policies, and behavioral instructions configuring agent governance.
- Tool invocation outputs, API responses, and observation feedback (see `../taxonomy/tool.md`).
- Retrieved knowledge artifacts, database records, and persistent memory segments.

Related terms within the AAIF taxonomy include context assembly, context exhaustion, context propagation across system boundaries, memory access, and information retrieval [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed as an open universal taxonomy entry in `ws-taxonomy-landscape` PR #82, bringing the taxonomy schema inventory to 38 entries and passing validation test suites [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing within hardware-attested enclaves to secure untrusted infrastructure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern—also known as a TEE-isolated agent runtime, confidential agent execution, or an attested enclave gateway—isolates policy enforcement points and evidence signing within hardware-protected Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) while leaving untrusted host systems and agent logic outside the enclave boundary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]. This pattern addresses multi-tenant and untrusted host environments where the infrastructure operator is inside the threat model, preventing tampering with policy evaluation, audit trails, and execution evidence [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb].

It forms a foundational building block within the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` design patterns catalog under privacy-preserving execution, complementing software-only controls such as `../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md` and `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`.

# Architecture / Specification

## Stakeholder Roles
The pattern explicitly models four distinct organizational roles with diverging security interests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]:
- **Data Owner**: Ensures input data and prompts are not exposed in plaintext during agent processing.
- **Agent Operator**: Deploys and executes the agent workload while seeking operational adoption and trust.
- **Infrastructure Operator**: Manages physical compute, hypervisors, and orchestration platforms; treated as untrusted and inside the threat model.
- **Relying Party**: An external auditor, consumer, peer agent, or downstream tool evaluating agent integrity without direct inspection capabilities.

## Core Mechanisms
1. **Enforcement Point Isolation**: Policy evaluators and policy bundles run strictly within the enclave, while model inference and agent reasoning loop components remain outside [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb].
2. **Internal Key Generation**: Cryptographic signing keys are generated inside the hardware boundary and bound to the enclave measurement; the private key never leaves the boundary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb].
3. **Measurement-Sealed Policy and Attested Release**: Execution policies are cryptographically sealed to enclave hardware measurements; secret keys and sensitive data are released only upon successful remote attestation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb].
4. **Per-Unit Verifiable Evidence**: The runtime produces verifiable evidence tokens per operational unit of work, which are submitted to independent relying parties for appraisal [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb].

# Lifecycle History
Contributed to the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` design patterns workstream as a foundational pattern for privacy-preserving execution, spanning compatibility across major hardware attestation stacks including Intel SGX/TDX and AMD SEV-SNP [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security and privacy as shared disciplines across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. It produces open threat models, taxonomies, design patterns, and defensive implementation guidelines that agent providers, platform consumers, and peer foundation working groups adopt to distribute responsibility for secure agent execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

The group collaborates closely with `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md` and `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` on shared security baselines, protocol boundaries, and cross-working group audit checklists [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Cadence
- **Chairs**: Alex Frazer (Runlayer, Chair) and Junjie Bu (Google, Co-Chair) for the term March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].
- **Meeting Cadence**: Regular biweekly meetings held Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT, supplemented by an alternate-week APAC time slot at 10:00 PM ET [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Repository Governance**: PRs to the deliverables repository enforce peer review where authors cannot self-approve or self-merge their deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

## Workstreams and Deliverables
- **Threat Modeling**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, producing gap analyses evaluating CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against agentic threats such as multi-agent persuasion and delegated tool invocation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
- **Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing the practitioner guide and feature matrix in `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan and Sagar, curating privacy-preserving execution architectures including `../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md` and operational patterns like `../patterns/kill-switch.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Cross-cutting collaboration with `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`, maintaining security and privacy definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing a unified security review process across Foundation workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Comprehensive practitioner guidelines, operational controls, and feature matrix for securing agent runtimes, credentials, and tool interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide establishes operational controls, verification workflows, and architectural safeguards for deploying autonomous agents into production environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]. Developed by the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` and synthesized with industry frameworks like Google ADK Safety, it establishes concrete controls spanning secrets lifecycle management, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool security, skill supply chains, and execution isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

The guideline aligns closely with runtime defense patterns, including `../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md` and `../patterns/kill-switch.md`, translating threat models into verifiable technical requirements.

# Architecture / Specification

## Control Areas and Feature Matrix
The baseline encompasses ten essential control disciplines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Secrets Management**: Eradication of long-lived, static environment credentials in favor of short-lived workload identities (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity), dynamic secrets engines with auto-expiry, sidecar proxy injection, and enclave-attested key release via confidential computing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Secure Tool Invocation (MCP Protocol Security)**: Pre-connection server evaluation (repository verification, activity thresholds, vulnerability tracking), encrypted OAuth 2.1 PKCE transport with RFC 8707 audience binding, stdio sandbox isolation, centralized MCP gateway routing, and runtime tool description hashing to defeat prompt and schema rug-pull attacks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Supply Chain and Skill Verification**: Multi-tiered skill validation using static pattern matching and behavioral dataflow scanning, manual permission reviews for elevated tool entitlements, and detection of obfuscated code (`eval`, Base64 payloads) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Guardrails, Evals, and Forensics**: Pre-execution input validation, continuous red-teaming harnesses, immutable audit logging with non-repudiable tracing, and deterministic policy enforcement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Sandboxed Execution and Network Perimeters**: MicroVM or container sandboxing for untrusted code execution, egress traffic filtering, and zero-trust identity enforcement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# Lifecycle History
The guide was drafted by Fernando Lucktemberg, Matthew Khouzam, and working group contributors, culminating in v1.0 final review under PR #9 in September 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]. It operates as a living deliverable, with rules maintained in code and synchronized with static analysis analyzers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-working-group review standards for agentic AI deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing practical threat models, security design patterns, and defensive guidelines for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Led across deliverables by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), and Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), the working group focuses on mitigating vulnerabilities unique to autonomous decision loops, multi-agent interactions, and dynamic tool invocation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical output into a sequential five-part deliverable portfolio [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:

- **D1: Taxonomy of Terms**: Core shared vocabulary defining agentic-specific threats, initially established within the working group before transitioning to the cross-working-group [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: A comparative assessment evaluating frameworks including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight distinct agentic risk domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **D3: Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural patterns addressing structural security voids identified in the gap analysis [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **D4: Best Practices Guide**: Operational practitioner guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].
- **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Governance criteria and handoff checklists for architectural domains owned by peer groups such as the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History

The working group initially managed taxonomy terms locally before migrating broad terminology definitions to the cross-foundation taxonomy workstream in June 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]. Deliverables 2 and 4 entered initial draft review in September 2026, establishing mandatory review requirements for ongoing updates under Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practitioner guide and operational controls for secrets management, tool invocation security, guardrails, evaluations, and post-incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide defines operational controls and architectural defenses for organizations deploying autonomous AI agents in production [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Authored as Deliverable 4 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and maintained by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the guidance addresses vulnerabilities across secrets management, tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation suites, and forensic analysis [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

# Architecture / Specification

The framework provides concrete implementation patterns structured around primary threat vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:

- **Secrets Management**: Replaces static, long-lived credentials (API keys, service passwords) with short-lived, ephemeral attestations. Priority controls mandate platform-native workload identities (e.g., AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity), dynamic secret generation (HashiCorp Vault), network-layer proxy credential injection, and hardware-attested confidential computing (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Tool Invocation Security**: Addresses security gaps in the Model Context Protocol (MCP), where stdio transports bypass authorization and OAuth 2.1 is optional. Prescribes pre-deployment server scanning, public vulnerability ledger validation, and RFC 8707 audience-bound token verification across user-direct, shared identity provider, and machine-to-machine trust topologies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Boundary Exclusions**: Delegated identity models, SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation, and RFC 8693 delegation-chain mechanics are formally scoped out of this guide and delegated to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Lifecycle History

Draft v0.1 of Deliverable 4 was submitted for working group review in September 2026, transitioning into a living document governed by mandatory lead sign-offs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation of AI threat modeling frameworks identifying structural gaps in multi-agent persuasion, tool risks, and excessive agency.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis evaluates the adequacy of existing cybersecurity frameworks—specifically OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—for addressing threat models unique to autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Authored as Deliverable 2 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor, the analysis establishes an evidence baseline to determine where existing industry taxonomies suffice versus where new Foundation specifications and patterns are required [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation synthesizes developer-facing vulnerability models (OWASP), SOC-facing adversarial technique taxonomies (MITRE ATLAS), and architectural layer models (CSA MAESTRO) across eight core domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:

1. **Memory and Context Poisoning**: Long-term state manipulation and memory corruption.
2. **Multi-Agent Persuasion**: Covert or cascading manipulation across interconnected agents.
3. **Agent Sabotage, Derailment, and Rogue Agents**: Intentional behavioral subversion or non-adversarial execution drift.
4. **Tool Invocation Risk**: Malicious MCP tool definitions, rug pulls, and unconstrained API execution.
5. **Excessive Agency and Blast Radius Containment**: Autonomous privilege escalation and unbounded blast radiuses.
6. **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Multi-hop delegation chains (cross-referenced with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)).
7. **Supply Chain Integrity**: Tampering with system prompts, skill registries, and runtime manifests.
8. **Commerce and Payment-Agent Risk**: Unauthorized transactions and financial delegation hazards.

The report concludes that while existing frameworks provide adequate classification for standard model failures, five concrete technical voids require new Foundation pattern design, two require inter-WG architectural handoffs, and one poses an unresolved scope interface with the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History

Deliverable 2 was submitted as Draft v0.1 in September 2026, serving as the architectural baseline for the subsequent Design Patterns Catalog and Best Practices Guide [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry specification and causal execution trace standard defining turn boundaries and cross-boundary agent observations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define turn boundaries, causal execution graphs, and runtime behavior tracking across agentic workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]. The model establishes vendor-neutral telemetry conventions that map multi-turn agent deliberation, tool calls, and delegated task handoffs into structured trace events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification

The trace model development lifecycle is structured around four sequential, evidence-first execution phases [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:

- **Phase 1 (Agree)**: Align on core dimensions, milestone scope definitions, and evaluation metrics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
- **Phase 2 (Evidence)**: Empirical capture and analysis of telemetry emitted by production agent frameworks, utilizing [Goose](../resources/goose.md) as the initial reference implementation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
- **Phase 3 (Interpret)**: Maintain a shared register of observed telemetry gaps, inconsistent OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention implementations, and missing behavioral attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
- **Phase 4 (Contribute)**: Formulate formal OpenTelemetry upstream proposals and Foundation trace specifications backed by validated runtime traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Lifecycle History

In September 2026, the working group restructured the project's execution plan from parallel theoretical tracks to a four-phase evidence-driven methodology anchored by an empirical gap register and a Goose reference implementation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Execution Standards
proposed_concept.description: Standards for packaging multi-client portable agent plugins, resolving skill root paths, and structuring progress and authorization boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Plugin Portability guidelines define standards for authoring multi-client agent plugins and packaging modular skills across supported environments such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Standardized packaging prevents tool and client lock-in by decoupling execution rules from client-specific user interface artifacts.

# Architecture / Specification

### Manifest Structure

Portable plugins declare a root `plugin.json` manifest as the canonical source for shared identity, versioning, and tool declarations [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Specific host manifests (e.g., `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) are maintained strictly when required for client catalog discovery, while avoiding client-specific runtime overlays like `.codex-plugin` unless component configurations differ [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

### Skill Path Resolution and Capabilities

In accordance with [Agent Skills Standards](../standards/agent-skills.md):
- All references within a `SKILL.md` or companion script must use relative paths anchored to the skill root directory [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Command-line invocations reference the directory using the `<skill-root>` placeholder, which agents resolve dynamically at load time rather than treating as an environment variable or literal shell string [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Skill instructions define required capabilities (e.g., run Python, read bundled files, show local files, request approval) rather than hardcoded client tool names [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

### Authorization and Mutation Boundaries

Invocation of a skill must not confer implied authorization to mutate external systems [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- Operations default to plan/dry-run mode; mutation flags (e.g., `--write`, `--apply`, `--create`) require explicit human confirmation [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69], aligning with [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- Approval assertions such as `--i-have-approval` must only be provided through genuine human operator action and never synthesized autonomously by the agent [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Secrets must never be passed via shell arguments (`argv`), prompts, tracked files, or public logs; they must be provided strictly through environment variables, gitignored local envs, or system keychains [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

# Lifecycle History

- Formalized via merged community event operations and pre-commit verification workflows, standardizing CI validation (`claude plugin validate`, ruff, gitleaks, YAML schema checks) across all plugin repositories [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational automation skill and multi-phase sync pipeline managing chapter lifecycle, CRM data validation, estate backfills, and presentation asset surgery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill coordinates administrative workflows for AAIF local community chapters, including chapter provisioning, estate-wide slide backfills, CRM integration, and multi-surface metadata reconciliation [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Principles

1. **Plan-by-Default Execution**: Destructive or estate-wide write actions default to a dry-run plan output. Applying mutations requires explicit `--write` confirmation flags [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3], enforcing [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
2. **Multi-Surface Renames**: Renaming an existing chapter involves four distinct operational surfaces that must be modified in synchrony: folder paths, file names, OOXML internal document text (`.docx`/`.pptx`/`.xlsx`), and `docProps` metadata [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]. Luma platform slugs and `.rels` identifiers remain decoupled from plain city renames to prevent dangling links or 404 errors [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
3. **Estate Slide Backfills**: Sweeping existing chapter presentation decks applies direct OOXML manipulation (e.g., Gall Stereographic coordinate projection for map dot placement) while asserting idempotent tolerances (e.g., skipping templates within 1 px threshold) [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
4. **Credential Isolation**: Automated CI verification workflows running on pull requests must never receive production credentials, reserving sensitive execution to explicit workflow dispatches under gated environments [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

# Lifecycle History

- Expanded to cover production estate backfills (`backfill_map_dots.py`, `backfill_host_footer.py`, `backfill_projects.py`) and four-surface chapter renaming scripts [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing compliance frameworks, policy baselines, regulatory gap analyses, and runtime regulatory data schemas.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group develops vendor-neutral compliance architectures, regulatory taxonomies, and policy interchange standards across global AI governance regimes.

# Architecture / Specification

### Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Regulatory Theme Cards & Schemas**: Standardizing schema definitions for mapping binding AI legal obligations to operational agent guardrails [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].
- **Separation of Schema and Regulatory Data**: Under proposed Phase 2 architectures, the working group standardizes open data schemas (incorporating jurisdiction, binding roles such as provider/deployer/user, instrument citation, statutory duties, scope, and status) under CC-BY-4.0, while delegating live requirement data feeds to pluggable external runtime registries [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]. This structural decoupling mimics the OpenSSF OSV and CNCF Open Policy Agent models, avoiding static out-of-date legal snapshots within the repository and adhering to charter boundaries prohibiting formal legal advice [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].
- **Compliance Boundary Controls**: Coordinating with [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to integrate legal audit trails into [Evidence Record Spec](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) and runtime verification pipelines.

# Lifecycle History

- Proposal initiated on Issue #11 evaluating Phase 2 theme card row formatting and runtime pluggable legal data providers across rapidly changing legal regimes (e.g., EU AI Act revisions and state statutory updates) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Classification schema and empirical inventory mapping real-world production agentic workflows across structural dimensions and verified deployment criteria.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory is a reference catalog and structural analysis framework maintained by the Critical Use Cases Workstream within the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. It provides a standardized schema for describing, comparing, and designing real-world agentic workflows across cross-industry and domain-specific contexts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]. Rather than functioning as a ranked or exhaustive registry, the inventory focuses on capturing diverse pattern coverage across real implementations to aid architectural design and scenario analysis[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

# Architecture / Specification

### Classification Dimensions

The framework organizes workflow records across twelve attributes, separating structural classification dimensions from supporting contextual fields[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]:

- **Trigger:** Identifies the initiating event of the workflow, categorized by external system signals, scheduled recurring timers, or manual human prompts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **HITL Pattern:** Defines points of mandatory human intervention, distinguishing autonomous execution from explicit [human-approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Agent Count:** Quantifies discrete reasoning entities and captures the architectural rationale for splitting duties (e.g., model specialization, bounded tool permissions, or domain separation)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Coordination:** Specifies whether multi-step or multi-agent progression is orchestrated by static deterministic code or runtime language model reasoning[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Workflow Pattern:** Details the execution topology, spanning linear sequences, concurrent fan-out/fan-in branching, or iterative [bounded convergence loops](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

Supporting attributes document observed duration (strictly measuring active agent execution time), target tools and systems, key failure modes, execution preconditions, and empirical notes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

### Evidentiary Standard

Entries in the inventory must satisfy strict sourcing requirements to mitigate link rot and speculative marketing claims[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Preferred:** Primary vendor product pages or official announcements demonstrating a named customer production deployment[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Acceptable:** Vendor product pages showing verifiable feature evidence operating in production at scale without a named client[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Unacceptable:** Secondary blog posts, speculative analyst projections, academic preprints, or personal implementer write-ups lacking production confirmation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

### Domain Coverage

The inventory categorizes implementations across horizontal enterprise capabilities (Sales, Marketing, Customer Support, Finance & Operations, HR & Recruiting, Research & Intelligence) as well as specialized industry verticals (Engineering, IT & Network Operations, SDLC, Platform Engineering, Healthcare, Supply Chain, Legal, Education, and Real Estate)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

# Lifecycle History

The initial classification schema was drafted within the Critical Use Cases Workstream to structure workflow comparisons across industries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. Under PR #41, the workstream executed an evidentiary cleanup across all entries: speculative citations and defunct vendor references were excised, multi-agent classification rationales were standardized, and the evidentiary baseline requiring verified production deployments was codified[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]. Alignment with the Reference Architecture Workstream remains active[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining shared workflow models, common terminology, execution profiles, and production use-case taxonomies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group defines shared agentic workflow models, standard orchestration terminology, execution profiles, and reference architectures across the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. Its focus centers on analyzing how autonomous agents transition between task states, coordinate across system boundaries, and interact with human oversight in production environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group drives several core technical tracks:

- **Critical Use Cases:** Developing the [Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md), an empirical schema evaluating production workflows across five structural dimensions (Trigger, HITL Pattern, Agent Count, Coordination, and Workflow Pattern)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Production Evidentiary Standards:** Establishing strict provenance baselines that mandate primary product documentation and confirmed production deployments while rejecting speculative analyst write-ups and unverified claims[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Reference Architecture Harmonization:** Linking classified workflow topologies with core architectural guidelines, including the [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md) and [Job-Oriented Architecture Model](../guidelines/job-oriented-architecture-model.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

# Lifecycle History

The working group originated as a foundational body within the Foundation's technical governance structure. In 2026, the Critical Use Cases Workstream finalized an audited production use-case inventory and codified formal evidentiary criteria via PR #41, establishing ongoing alignment with reference architecture deliverables[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
