proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-surface boundary controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, security best practices, architectural defense patterns, and boundary protection standards for agentic AI deployments across the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-29]. The group's scope covers runtime isolation, tool invocation controls, prompt defense, and multi-agent network boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group actively researches and standardizes key security deliverables:

- **Cross-Surface Security Floors:** Evaluating design patterns (such as 'declare-pin-inherit-prove') where node publishers declare their exposed interaction surfaces in discovery documents and inherit a single unified security floor rather than managing divergent safety baselines across interfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-29].
- **Tool and Payload Strictness:** Defining input validation standards where tool arguments require typed identifiers over raw paths or shell commands, JSON output envelopes maintain fixed untrusted trust annotations, and natural language fields are treated strictly as data[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-29].
- **Network and SSRF Mitigations:** Formulating transport constraints for peer discovery and task delegation, including mandatory HTTPS, IANA special-purpose address rejection, hop-by-hop redirect evaluation, and post-connection socket address re-verification to counter DNS rebinding[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-29].
- **Boundary Authorizations:** Coordinating with governance patterns such as the [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [human-approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) to ensure external modifications require explicit, reviewable human sign-off[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-29].

# Lifecycle History

Chartered to deliver foundational threat models and operational security guidance, the group regularly reviews community contributions. Issue #29 introduced proposals for inherited surface security baselines and strict payload controls as prospective inputs for the group's design-pattern deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-29].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining agent identity, credential delegation, decentralized trust, and verifiable discovery metadata.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group defines technical standards, protocols, and architectural patterns for AI agent identity, cryptographic attestation, credential delegation, and decentralized trust establishment across the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-11]. Its scope spans agent-to-agent verification, runtime attestation, and pre-connection trust metadata.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's technical agenda encompasses:

- **Discovery and Trust Metadata:** Developing standards for how agents and node publishers publish pre-connection manifests and descriptive metadata to facilitate secure evaluation before interaction begins[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-11].
- **Digest-Bound Integrity:** Evaluating mechanisms such as well-known knowledge link sets carrying cryptographic target digests, allowing clients to independently verify published artifacts before parsing regardless of transport security[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-11].
- **Federation Models:** Defining requirements for mutual peer naming and boundary marking to guarantee that artifacts derived from external nodes maintain immutable provenance and untrusted classifications[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-11].
- **Protocol Coordination:** Investigating integration pathways with emerging endpoint discovery formats, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) server cards, to support verifiable publisher trust claims[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-11].

# Lifecycle History

The group operates under the Technical Committee to define foundational trust architectures. Issue #11 initiated group deliberation regarding whether publisher-level discovery documents bound by cryptographic digests fall within the working group's charter scope or should be advanced as direct protocol extensions[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-11].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate the security best practices feature matrix classifying controls across people, process, and technology capability dimensions.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practitioner guide and operational controls organizing security best practices across people, process, and technology capability dimensions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes operational and architectural controls for securing autonomous agent environments across model interaction, tool invocation, and credential boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20] It provides engineering teams and security practitioners with concrete requirements to mitigate risks in agent deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), these practices complement threat models by mapping defensive measures to concrete operational capabilities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

# Architecture / Specification
The framework structures security controls using a feature matrix that classifies required capabilities across three operational dimensions:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

- **People**: Capabilities focusing on workforce skills, security training, institutional knowledge, and operational awareness necessary for operators and engineers managing agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]
- **Process**: Documented policies, formal governance strategies, escalation paths, and standard operating procedures governing how security controls are executed and validated across the lifecycle.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]
- **Technology**: Physical or digital tools, hardware protections, software mechanisms, and automated guardrails that actively enforce boundary isolation, secrets management, and access controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

Each documented best practice identifies corresponding baseline features across these three dimensions to ensure defenses are not limited to software controls alone but supported by organizational governance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

# References
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy)

# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill provides automated workflows and synchronization pipelines for managing chapter lifecycles, event scheduling, and organizer rosters across Agentic AI Foundation community systems.[^evt-community-events-pr-55] It automates data hygiene across tracking sheets while enforcing human-in-the-loop review for critical chapter transitions.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]

The skill enforces safety constraints to prevent accidental loss of chapter history, operational metadata, and roster records during automated sync runs.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]

# Architecture / Specification
The chapter synchronization pipeline (`sync-chapters`) implements a non-destructive lifecycle model for chapter records:[^evt-community-events-pr-55]

- **Non-Destructive Retention**: Automated synchronization runs never delete or clear existing chapter rows from the Chapters List, preserving manually maintained summaries, chapter artwork, and operational notes.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Retirement Candidates**: When a chapter city lacks a qualifying active organizer, the pipeline flags the entry as a retirement candidate rather than executing an automated purge.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Human Governance Gate**: Candidate retirement requires human administrative action to update the chapter status to `Deprecated` or `Merged` (with a designated target `Merged Into` chapter).[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Ambiguity Holding**: Rows with ambiguous organizer city data—such as near-miss name matches, malformed rows, or unresolved organizers—are held without mutation or deprecation proposals until resolved.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Drift Reporting**: Retirement candidates surface on the pipeline run page Drift tab for human disposition without perturbing tool exit codes or generating false positive drift alerts during `--write` passes.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between agent proposal generation and protected execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Process with Human Approval reference architecture defines an operational model where an autonomous agent prepares a candidate action, an authorized human reviews and decides on the proposal, and a decoupled executor enacts the effect only after recording explicit approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]. It enforces behavioral boundaries whenever an agent's reasoning may alter external systems—such as disbursing refunds, updating production configurations, or publishing public communications—requiring non-repudiable human ownership and strict regulatory defensibility.

The architecture establishes a strict conceptual distinction between the overarching business task (the client request or incident being managed) and the discrete workflow activities executed to satisfy it [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-50]. By default, workflows route through a single reasoning agent unless concrete constraints—such as mandatory separation of duties, independent concurrent reasoning streams, or cross-organizational domain boundaries—compel multi-agent topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

# Architecture / Specification

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                             Workflow Engine                              |
|                                                                          |
|  [Business Task]                                                         |
|         |                                                                |
|         v                                                                |
|   +-----------+      Proposal       +-------------------+                |
|   |   Agent   | ------------------> |   Human Approval  |                |
|   | Activity  |   (Payload Hash)    |        Gate       |                |
|   +-----------+                     +-------------------+                |
|         |                                     |                          |
|         | Read-only / Sandbox                 | Approved Verdict         |
|         v                                     v                          |
|   +-----------+                     +-------------------+   Side-Effect  |
|   | Context & |                     | Workflow Executor | -------------> |
|   |   Tools   |                     |     Activity      |                |
|   +-----------+                     +-------------------+                |
|                                               |                          |
|                                               v                          |
|                                        +--------------+                  |
|                                        |  Audit Log   |                  |
|                                        +--------------+                  |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Pattern Composition

The architecture composes three core workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]:
1. `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`: The agent investigates context, synthesizes arguments, and formats the proposal payload, but lacks direct access to external mutation capabilities.
2. `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`: A designated individual inspects the immutable proposal, evaluating its rationale and execution parameters before emitting a cryptographic or non-repudiable verdict.
3. `../patterns/durable-wait.md`: Because human evaluations introduce asynchronous delays ranging from minutes to days, workflow state persists durably across system restarts, process crashes, or infrastructure deployments.

### Architectural Invariants

- **Zero Protected Effects Without Human Approval**: The workflow-controlled executor will not fire absent an authenticated approval token bound to the exact payload hash [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- **Resilience Across Wait States**: Process interruption or orchestrator redeployment during approval wait states retains pending proposal integrity without triggering orphaned or duplicate actions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- **Deterministic Audit Binding**: Every run concludes in a verifiable state recording the full lineage chain—proposer agent identity, human decision authority, and executor confirmation—into the system of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

# References

- Composed pattern specifications: `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`, `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`, `../patterns/durable-wait.md`
- Taxonomy primitives: `../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md`

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for resolving bounded operational problems autonomously through isolated execution, deterministic acceptance gates, and convergence loops.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Bounded Autonomous Remediation provides a reference framework for allowing software agents to remediate operational failures and execute constrained system mutations without synchronous human approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]. Remediation workflows operate strictly within bounded execution sandboxes, iterating across convergence loops and submitting proposed changes against strict deterministic acceptance criteria before effects are merged or promoted into production.

To balance operational autonomy with safety, the architecture scales verification intensity against the blast radius and reversal cost of the permitted effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

# Architecture / Specification

### Minimum Evidence for Deterministic Gates

While deterministic gates scale their verification hurdles according to the risk of the action, the evidence model preserving gate verdicts enforces three universal invariants across all tiers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]:

1. **Determinism of the Verdict**: The acceptance check must evaluate repeatable, deterministic criteria (such as test suites, linters, schema validators, or static analysis runs) where identical candidates and test inputs yield identical verdicts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
2. **Binding of Verdict to Candidate**: The emitted acceptance record is cryptographically bound to the specific immutable candidate artifact (via content digests), ensuring verification cannot be forged or transferred to unvetted revisions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
3. **Preservation as Execution Evidence**: Gate verdicts, captured logs, and evaluation metrics persist permanently within the execution ledger to provide auditability and post-mortem transparency [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

### Scaling Gate Strength

Gate validation criteria scale dynamically based on two structural properties of the target effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]:
- **Blast Radius**: The potential scope of operational impact (e.g., local process restart versus cross-region routing updates).
- **Reversal Cost**: The complexity, financial impact, or latency required to roll back the applied change if unexpected degradation occurs.

# References

- Composed patterns: `../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md`, `../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md`
- Boundary guidance: `../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md`

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practitioner guide and operational controls organizing security best practices across secrets auditing, sandbox boundaries, and approval mechanisms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide outlines operational controls, threat assessments, and implementation baselines required to secure agentic systems across development and deployment lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]. It addresses risks unique to agent autonomy, including config-borne credentials, transcript context leakage, host sandbox escapes, and human-in-the-loop review fatigue [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

# Architecture / Specification

### Secrets Auditing and Context Leakage

Auditing procedures must extend beyond environment variables and container image layers to encompass agent-specific surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]:

- **Configuration and Plugin Bundles**: Model Context Protocol (MCP) client files (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`) and portable agent skill repositories frequently leak hardcoded API tokens and credentials in environment definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Context and Transcript Leakage**: Tool executions returning configuration files or bearer tokens risk exposing sensitive values in conversational memory, execution traces, and system transcripts. Controls must mandate output redaction prior to context ingestion and restrict long-term memory systems from retaining credentials (addressing OWASP MCP01 and ASI03 memory-based privilege retention) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Host Credential Isolation**: Because developer coding agents frequently operate on local machines hosting private SSH keys, cloud profiles, and browser sessions, hook-level deny rules and sandbox restrictions must enforce short-lived credentials and prevent directory traversal escapes to user home directories [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].

### Human Approval and Fatigue Dynamics

Relying on undifferentiated manual approval prompts introduces systematic verification decay [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]:

- Empirical research indicates that human review catch rates fall precipitously over repeated interactions (dropping from ~13.6% to ~5% after 50 prompts, while upwards of 97% of standard prompts are rubber-stamped without scrutiny) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- To counter approval fatigue, organizations should avoid treating manual checkpoints as universal fail-safes and instead combine them with automated deterministic policy filters that intercept destructive commands before human presentation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

# References

- Human approval patterns: `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`
- Threat modeling resources: `../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`
- Governing group: `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines, threat taxonomy mappings, and runtime defense architectures defining security baselines for agent deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide establishes architectural controls, runtime invariants, and defense-in-depth requirements for securing autonomous agents and tool-use environments. Developed under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide specifies defensive baselines spanning credential management, tool sandboxing, gateway routing, and in-loop execution governance.

# Architecture / Specification

## In-Loop Hooks vs. Gateway Enforcement
While centralized network checkpoints (such as Model Context Protocol gateways) facilitate payload capture and remote authentication, active working group discussions emphasize that comprehensive policy enforcement belongs at an in-loop hook within the agent execution loop [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]. Network gateways only observe remote traffic; they miss local stdio transport servers, framework-level connectors, direct SDK calls, and shell commands, and lack the user prompt context needed to evaluate policy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]. Under this model, runtime policy-as-code must be evaluated at the in-loop hook, with network gateways functioning as telemetry relays and perimeter authentication checkpoints rather than the primary enforcement layer [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

## Sandbox Blast Radius and Containment Limits
Execution sandboxing for agent tools restricts filesystem access to working-directory scope, but working group reviews emphasize that it does not inherently eliminate blast radius [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]. Sandboxed agents can bypass egress blocks by invoking high-level network utilities (such as Python urllib) or write poisoned files into shared project workspaces that unsandboxed host tools subsequently execute [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]. Comprehensive isolation requires addressing host trust handoffs and egress controls alongside filesystem restrictions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].

## Confidential Computing and Credential Lifecycles
Within [Attested Isolated Runtimes](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), hardware enclaves isolate guest memory from host and hypervisor inspection [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. However, hardware isolation does not truncate credential exposure windows if guest software leaks a bearer token [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. Confidential computing deployments must therefore combine hardware isolation with short-lived, minimally scoped tokens and strict controls on which guest components may access them [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

## Threat Taxonomy Alignment
The guide maps defensive requirements against standard industry taxonomies, including MITRE ATLAS (v5.6.0) and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32]:
- **Tool Poisoning and Supply Chain**: AI Agent Tool Poisoning (AML.T0110) and Indirect Prompt Injection (AML.T0051.001) map to ASI02 and ASI04 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Credential Access**: Unsecured Credentials (AML.T0055) and Agent Configuration Harvesting (AML.T0083) map to ASI03 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Exfiltration and Context Poisoning**: Tool Invocation Exfiltration (AML.T0086) and Context/Memory Poisoning (AML.T0080.000) map to ASI01, ASI06, and ASI10 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].

# Lifecycle History
The guide was developed by the Security and Privacy Working Group. Ongoing issues #30, #32, #34, and #37 track open refinements addressing in-loop enforcement hooks, sandbox containment limits, confidential computing exposure models, and formal ATLAS/ASI threat taxonomy tagging.

mutations.rationale: Refine confidential computing threat boundaries to account for guest-level bearer token exposure and runtime attestation claims binding.

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern isolating policy enforcement, secret handling, and execution within hardware-attested confidential environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern executes agent reasoning, policy enforcement, or sensitive tool invocations inside a hardware-isolated confidential computing environment (such as a confidential virtual machine or enclave). By generating cryptographic attestation reports verifying guest software integrity, the pattern protects execution state against untrusted host operators and co-located workloads.

# Architecture / Specification

## Host vs. Guest Threat Boundaries
Hardware attestation guarantees memory encryption and guest execution integrity against host-level hypervisors, firmware, and physical access [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. However, guest software operating within the isolated environment remains part of the trusted computing base [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. If guest software exposes a bearer token, hardware isolation does not constrain the resulting blast radius or shorten the token's validity window [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. Confidential runtime architectures must enforce:
- **Short-Lived Token Lifecycles**: Provisioning short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials whose maximum exposure window is governed by token validity and revocation mechanisms rather than hardware boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].
- **Internal Guest Restrictions**: Partitioning guest processes to restrict which software components can read, process, or release credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].
- **Attestation Claims Binding**: Cryptographically binding attestation payloads (such as REPORT_DATA) to hashes of runtime claims, including vTPM keys, virtual machine configurations, and user data [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

## Integration with Governance Patterns
Attested isolated runtimes frequently pair with [proposal-execution splits](./proposal-execution-split.md) and [human-approval gates](./human-approval-gate.md) to ensure high-risk agent operations cannot execute without verified attestation boundaries. Guidelines for credential exposure within confidential boundaries are maintained in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

# Lifecycle History
Established as an architectural pattern under the Security and Privacy Working Group. Refined in issue #37 to clarify the platform threat model regarding guest-level token exposures and report payload claim bindings.

## Inclusion Criteria and Taxonomy Categories
The landscape organizes projects into functional domains, including Orchestration & Multi-Agent systems, protocols, evaluation frameworks, and security layers. General admission for open-source ecosystem tools maintains a baseline threshold (such as a 1,000 GitHub star general threshold for independent projects) alongside requirements for schema compliance in `landscape.yml` accompanied by vector (SVG) brand assets [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22]. Projects governed directly under AAIF repositories (such as [Goose](./goose.md) at `aaif-goose/goose`) serve as canonical references within the catalog [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing shared agentic AI vocabulary, taxonomies, and the open-source landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) workstream standardizing shared terminology, classification schemas, and ecosystem landscapes across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79]. The workstream harmonizes domain-specific concepts developed across Foundation working groups, including the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), ensuring consistency across all published taxonomy assets [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains the central taxonomy data repository and automated CI validation pipelines. As part of structural refactoring, the taxonomy data format migrated from executable JavaScript files (`taxonomy-data.js`) to standard JSON (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) backed by Zod schema validation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79]. This transition removes custom parser maintenance in continuous integration, avoids executing contributor-provided script code, and yields deterministic field-level validation errors for pull requests [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

Active taxonomy definitions integrated from domain working groups include:
- **Agent-completed transaction**: Captures transactions finalized autonomously by an AI agent [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].
- **Agent-in-the-loop transaction**: Renamed from agent-mediated transaction following community review, defining transaction flows wherein an agent participates alongside human actors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71].
- **Agent-initiated transaction**: Classifies transaction cycles originated or triggered by autonomous agent decisions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72].

# Lifecycle History
The working group moved taxonomy data storage to schema-validated JSON to resolve CI syntax-checking fragility and standardize the contributor intake process [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing capability maps, operational protocols, and transactional architectures for AI-driven commerce. The group collaborates closely with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define standard terminology for autonomous transaction workflows [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group has advanced standard taxonomy classifications categorizing distinct operational modes of commercial agent interaction:
- **Agent-completed transaction**: Focuses on transactions where execution and final settlement are carried out autonomously by the agent [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].
- **Agent-in-the-loop transaction**: Renamed from agent-mediated transaction based on working group feedback, classifying transactions where an agent operates as an intermediary or collaborative participant within a human-supervised workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71].
- **Agent-initiated transaction**: Identifies transactions originated or triggered by an agent based on autonomous evaluation or programmatic thresholds [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72].

# Lifecycle History
The group submitted formal definitions for agent-completed, agent-initiated, and agent-in-the-loop transactions to the unified taxonomy repository to establish shared baseline commerce vocabulary across AAIF projects [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72].

# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill automates chapter lifecycle management, intake parsing, CRM validation, Google Drive folder provisioning, and access enforcement across the Agentic AI Foundation event ecosystem[^evt-community-events-pr-57]. The pipeline processes contributor and organizer applications through deterministic sync engines, mapping applicant inputs to authorized chapter roles and maintaining consistency across registration sheets, Luma pages, Drive folders, and Slack channels[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

The system enforces regional and administrative boundaries, including the automatic consolidation of municipal applications into country-level chapters (such as folding Tokyo into AAIF Japan and Wellington or Auckland into AAIF New Zealand) to allow distributed organizer teams to operate under unified jurisdictional and communication structures[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Architecture / Specification

The event operations workflow is organized as a sequential sync and validation pipeline operating across shared data stores and third-party collaboration tools:

1. **Intake and City Resolution**: The intake ingestion module extracts city data from application submissions and passes values through `lib/aaif_events/cities.py:chapter_for()`[^evt-community-events-pr-57]. This canonical fold normalizes individual city applicants into their respective country chapters, preventing duplicate chapter rows or fragmented permissions across downstream consumers[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
2. **CRM and Access Synchronization**: `sync_crm` updates relationship records, which downstream feeds `sync_access` to manage workspace role tabs and enforce role-based access control gates[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
3. **Data Hygiene and Reclaim Prevention**: The `clean.py` engine defines `COUNTRY_CHAPTER_FOLDS` overrides that supersede the Chapters List, ensuring that retired city rows cannot inadvertently reclaim applicants or split identity mappings[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
4. **Channel and Workspace Governance**: The Slack audit subsystem reconciles active membership across community channels (such as `japan-organizers` and `new-zealand-organizers`) against verified roster manifests[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #57** (Authoritative): Formalized country chapters for Japan and New Zealand, adding centralized runtime city folding in `chapter_for()` and preventing cross-chapter duplicate assignments across CRM and access syncs[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing capability maps, gap analyses, and protocol architectures for autonomous commerce transactions, cross-boundary evidence binding, and post-purchase settlement.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical working group establishing standardized capability maps, gap analyses, protocol architectures, and audit mechanisms for autonomous agent commerce[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]. The group evaluates interaction standards spanning product discovery, agent-negotiated purchases, payment authorization, and post-purchase accountability across agent, merchant, payment processor, and risk-system boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

The working group coordinates cross-cutting concerns with sibling foundation efforts, delegating telemetry and causal audit structures to the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and identity binding and delegation primitives to the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its core deliverables around an overarching Capability Map and Gap Analysis, targeting full lifecycle transaction coverage across pre-purchase, point-of-sale, and post-purchase operational phases[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]:

- **Evidence Binding**: Constructing verifiable receipts and audit records that cryptographically bind execution claims to transaction identifiers, agent identities, shopper identities, and delegation scopes to enable deterministic dispute resolution[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Signal Provenance**: Establishing explicit markers distinguishing self-reported signals from independently observed signals across platforms, payment providers, and merchants[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Authorization Strength**: Formulating evidentiary thresholds and renewed approval requirements for state-changing remedies, including cancellations, returns, refunds, and disputes[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Auditability and Verdict Envelopes**: Defining bounded verification results via machine-readable verdict envelopes containing:
  1. `verdict`: Tri-state classification (`supported`, `contradicted`, or `unresolvable`)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  2. `verifier`: Distinct entity identifier computing the classification[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  3. `verifier_signature`: Digital signature computed over verdict and evidence fingerprints[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  4. `evidence_refs`: Canonical references to transaction, delegation, and consent claims[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  5. `evidence_fingerprints`: RFC 8785 canonical hashes ensuring deterministic replay[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  6. `verification_basis`: Specification of evaluated policy checks[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  7. `witness_scope`: Scope limitations and boundaries of the verification verdict[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
  8. `timestamp`: Freshness assertion[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

# Lifecycle History
- **Issue #5**: Proposed capability row and machine-readable verdict envelope contract for post-purchase cross-boundary evidence, auditability, and dispute reconciliation[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, cross-boundary verification, and the five-tier tracing reference architecture stack.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing telemetry specifications, execution trace models, and evaluation frameworks for AI agent infrastructure[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]. The working group standardizes how agent execution state, tool interactions, multi-agent coordination, and underlying hardware operations are captured, correlated, and audited across multi-tenant environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

The group maintains structured reference architecture assessments spanning foundational binary formats up through runtime agent tracing, establishing unified evaluation dimensions for performance, overhead, and semantic fidelity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its technical assessments along a bottom-up five-layer observability stack[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]:

1. **Layer 01 — Foundations**: Baseline binary trace encodings and comparative evaluation frameworks, including the [Common Trace Format](../resources/common-trace-format.md) (CTF), the [Linux Tracing Comparison](../resources/linux-tracing-comparison.md), and [Trace Compass](../resources/trace-compass.md) for cross-domain state system analysis[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].
2. **Layer 02 — Kernel Tracing**: Operating system instrumentation and execution dynamics, evaluating [FTrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), [LTTng Kernel](../resources/lttng-kernel.md), [LTTng-UST](../resources/lttng-ust.md), device driver instrumentation ([Linux Driver Tracing](../resources/linux-driver-tracing.md)), [Virtualization Tracing](../resources/virtualization-tracing.md), [Container Orchestration Tracing](../resources/container-orchestration-tracing.md), [Tracy Profiler](../resources/tracy.md), and syscall inspection frameworks including [Sysdig](../resources/sysdig.md) and [Falco](../resources/falco.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].
3. **Layer 03 — Hardware Accelerators**: GPU kernel dispatches, tensor core utilization, and host-device synchronization profiled via [NVIDIA Nsight](../resources/nvidia-nsight.md), [AMD ROCprofiler](../resources/amd-rocprofiler.md), [PyTorch Profiler](../resources/pytorch-profiler.md), and hardware processor tracing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].
4. **Layer 04 — Network**: Wire-level protocol inspection, packet capture via [Wireshark](../resources/wireshark.md), and distributed communication fabrics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].
5. **Layer 05 — AI Agent Observability**: High-level agent runtime telemetry, model interaction traces, and semantic metrics captured via [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md), [Langfuse](../resources/langfuse.md), and [PostHog](../resources/posthog.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

# Lifecycle History
- **Authoritative Assessment**: Established the structured narrative and five-tier bottom-up stack in `tracing_landscape/README.md` to catalog observability technologies against agentic infrastructure[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group that bridges emerging global AI policy developments and technical implementations in agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]. Approved by the foundation on June 1, 2026, the working group addresses the absence of cohesive regulatory guidance, develops risk mitigation strategies, and identifies gaps in agentic standards and interoperability[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

# Architecture / Specification
The GRRA WG operates under an explicit charter detailing leadership structure, technical scope, and operational boundaries[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]:

- **Leadership**: Chaired by Deborah Eng (JPMorgan) with Co-chair Sriram Natarajan (Google)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Core Technical Scope**:
  - Monitoring global regulations, standards, and policy frameworks affecting the treatment of agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
  - Examining organizational implementations of agent protocols, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) deployments at boundaries like the [Agent-MCP Boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
  - Formulating standards for [AI Agent Bill of Materials](../taxonomy/ai-agent-bill-of-materials.md) (AIBOM) covering foundation models, scaffolding, tools, APIs, and provenance tracking[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
  - Establishing formal protocols and reversibility characterization frameworks for undo infrastructure[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
  - Evaluating risk classification schemas, incident reporting baselines, and human-in-the-loop controls such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
  - Aligning with sector-specific governance frameworks, such as the FINOS AI Governance Framework[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Boundary Exclusions**: The working group explicitly excludes offering formal legal advice or commercial compliance products[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-01**: Working group charter approved by the foundation[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **2026-10-09**: Charter updated with formalized leadership assignments and expanded scope deliverables[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

proposed_concept.description: Operational automation skill and multi-phase sync pipeline managing chapter lifecycle, CRM validation, and multi-role submission data integrity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill provides automated workflow tooling and multi-phase synchronization pipelines to manage AAIF chapter lifecycle tracking, participant intake, and CRM data integrity[^evt-community-events-pr-58]. It enforces validation rules across volunteer, organizer, and speaker submissions to maintain clean cross-tab event registries[^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill includes data sanitization routines executed by `clean.py` and downstream issue generation components[^evt-community-events-pr-58]:

- **Decided-No Multi-Tab Filtering**: The `scan` routine skips flagging submissions when every role tab where an applicant appears (e.g., organizer, speaker) reflects a definitive terminal verdict of `Denied`, `Inactive`, or `Duplicate`[^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Cross-Verdict Consistency**: If a candidate holds mixed statuses across tabs (such as organizer `Denied` but speaker `Prospect`), the submission remains flagged to ensure pending reviews are completed[^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Live Spreadsheet Formula Synchronization**: The `install_flags` command configures `issues_formula()`, rendering decided-no rows blank instead of generating error highlights in the live intake sheets[^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Defensive Fallback**: If an intake sheet tab omits expected header metadata (`Status`, `Timestamp`, or `Email`), suppression logic is bypassed to prevent silent omission of unverified records[^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #58**: Merged suppression logic ensuring applicants with uniform `Denied`, `Inactive`, or `Duplicate` verdicts across all role tabs are not flagged as active data errors[^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group within the Agentic AI Foundation establishes technical specifications, evaluation methodologies, and architectural patterns for agent identity verification, delegated authority, and decentralized trust.

# Workstreams and Technical Focus

The working group evaluates delegation, attestation evidence, and execution authority across agent and service boundaries:

- **Authority at Dispatch and Effect Separation**: Examining decoupling between dispatch decisions, committed system effects, and task execution outcomes[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-13]. This includes handling edge cases where a write action successfully commits but downstream communication fails, preventing erroneous publication while preserving committed effect records across comparative implementations such as Proofable, Alakris, and MintID[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-13].
- **Evidence Review and Attestation Standards**: Assessing author-operated implementation evidence and witness models to determine appropriate categorization across Use Cases, Reference Architecture, and Attestation/Evidence workstreams[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-15].
- **Human-Backed Agent Credentials**: Reviewing execution runs and verifiable delegation frameworks connecting authenticated human principal credentials to agent-directed operations[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-16].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation suite and dual-arm grading harness benchmarking agent skill triggering, token privacy, and instruction compliance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical evaluation harness designed to test whether AI agents trigger the correct modular skills and comply with behavioral boundaries defined in `SKILL.md` specifications [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Unlike deterministic unit tests that validate code parsing and YAML schema compliance, the eval suite exercises non-deterministic model decision boundaries to verify that skill descriptions trigger accurately without overlapping neighbor skills or leaking sensitive user credentials [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07][^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Dual-Arm Evaluation Harness
The test harness runs each case through two execution arms: one with the plugin skills active and one baseline arm without the plugin [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]:
- **With-Plugin Arm**: Evaluates whether the presence of skill instructions causes the agent to follow domain rules (such as redacting PII or rejecting write operations without confirmation).
- **Without-Plugin Arm**: Serves as a baseline control to evaluate inherent foundation model behavior. If an assertion passes in both arms, it measures base model capabilities rather than skill efficacy.
- **Delta Scoring (`Δ`)**: Differentiates rules enforced strictly by the skill definitions from standard model predispositions. Graders targeting rules present only in `SKILL.md` are tagged `arm: with-only` [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

## Targeted Evaluation Cases
The suite focuses on high-risk regression boundaries and observed operational failures [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]:
- **`announcement-post` & `recap-post`**: Disambiguates closely adjacent public-facing writing skills across temporal event boundaries (opening RSVPs versus post-event recaps).
- **`speaker-bio`**: Validates privacy enforcement rules by confirming that private phone numbers and email addresses provided in input prompts are omitted from generated copy [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **`triage-intake`**: Checks resistance to untrusted prompt injection and user inputs asking for automated acceptance.
- **`sync-chapters-write-gate`**: Ensures agent adherence to write-approval governance patterns such as [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md).
- **`audit-slack`**: Benchmarks triggering resilience against colloquial user requests without relying on skill-specific keywords.
- **`check-setup`**: Tests readiness diagnostics for non-technical users while enforcing token hygiene [^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1][^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed].

## Credential and Telemetry Safety
To mitigate token leakage into chat history and model context, the `check-setup` grader enforces that agents explicitly refuse pasted authentication secrets (such as Slack tokens) and instruct users to utilize platform secret stores like local keychains [^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1][^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed]. Evals are decoupled from continuous integration fork pull requests (`validate.yml`) to maintain credential isolation [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

# Lifecycle History
Authored as part of the `aaif/community-events` operational tooling to validate skills such as [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) before production release [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

proposed_concept.title: legacy2mcp
proposed_concept.description: Open-source adapter framework and CLI generating typed, read-only Model Context Protocol servers from legacy enterprise SOAP, database, and REST interfaces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
legacy2mcp is an open-source integration framework and command-line tool designed to expose legacy enterprise architectures—such as SOAP/WSDL web services, relational databases, and older REST APIs—as typed Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54]. Proposed as an Agentic AI Foundation Sandbox project, legacy2mcp enables AI agents to query enterprise data safely without requiring developers to write custom glue code or grant broad backend privileges [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54].

# Architecture / Specification

## Dynamic Tool Generation and Schema Validation
legacy2mcp inspects backend systems directly (parsing WSDL service definitions or querying live relational database schemas) to generate typed MCP tool definitions with structured JSON Schemas [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54]:
- **Schema Validation**: Every incoming tool invocation from an MCP client is validated against the generated schema before any backend payload dispatch occurs.
- **Read-Only Defaults**: The framework enforces read-only access by default; write operations must be explicitly configured, and relational database adapters restrict queries to configured allowlists of tables and named parameterized queries, preventing arbitrary agent SQL execution [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54].
- **Audit Logging**: Every tool call and dispatched request is logged for traceability.

## Extensible Adapter Architecture
The framework core manages tool validation, dispatch, and logging while exposing a lightweight `BaseAdapter` interface requiring two methods [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54]:
- `discover_tools()`: Discovers backend endpoints and generates MCP tool schemas.
- `invoke()`: Executes validated calls against the upstream service.

Initial adapters support SOAP/WSDL endpoints, SQL relational databases (PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle), and REST APIs, alongside a scaffolding command (`legacy2mcp init`) to bootstrap configurations from existing codebases [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54].

## Ecosystem Integration
The generated servers run over stdio and are compatible with MCP-compliant agents, such as [goose](../resources/goose.md) and IDE client protocols [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54].

# Lifecycle History
Created by Venkata Bhupalam under the Apache-2.0 license, reaching version 0.2.1 and indexed on the MCP Registry prior to submission for AAIF Sandbox project intake in October 2026 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-54].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to standardize agent identity mechanisms, cryptographic delegation frameworks, decentralized trust models, and verifiable authority specifications across multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]. The working group evaluates decentralized identifiers, delegation chains, and verification harnesses that govern how autonomous agents establish, prove, and constrain authority during execution [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Focus Areas
The working group coordinates technical specifications and empirical evaluation across several domains:
- **Decentralized Agent Identity**: Standardizing verifiable credential profiles and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) interoperable across platforms, complementing efforts such as [agent-network-protocol](../standards/agent-network-protocol.md).
- **Delegated Authority and Consent**: Defining schemas for bounded delegation, subagent credential scopes, and user consent verification.
- **Authority-at-Dispatch Verification**: Benchmarking and cataloguing mechanisms that verify agent authority at the moment of tool or task dispatch [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

## Authority-at-Dispatch Catalogue and Testing
The working group maintains a reference catalogue and verification workflow evaluating authority-at-dispatch implementations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]:
- **Contract Identifier Enforcement**: Execution traces must include a versioned contract identifier; trace readers reject submissions lacking this explicit identifier [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Freshness Limits**: Authority evidence structures must record assertion age against deployed freshness thresholds to prevent replay of stale delegation authorizations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Reference Comparative Benchmarks**: Standardized reference cases map authority assertion runs across distinct systems, integrating readers from tooling such as `agent-evidence-observer` [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

# Lifecycle History
Active within the AAIF governance structure, collaborating with related efforts such as [evidence-record-spec](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) and [governance-risk-and-regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill and multi-phase sync pipeline managing AAIF chapter lifecycles, intake data normalization, immutable backups, and design system conformance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill packages operational workflows for managing Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) local chapters, community intake queues, event trackers, and digital asset synchronization [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04]. Built to operate across agent runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop according to the [Agent Skills specification](../standards/agent-skills.md), the skill implements human-in-the-loop governance where the assistant autonomously drafts communications, audits discrepancies, and prepares proposals, but requires explicit human confirmation before executing any state-mutating or externally visible operations [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

# Architecture and Execution Pipeline
The toolkit structures community administration through a multi-phase operational pipeline covering data ingestion, pre-flight backups, intake normalization, chapter generation, and design system sweeps [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

## Multi-Phase Estate Sync and Intake Normalization
The core synchronization process executes in distinct sequential phases, beginning with intake data remediation via `clean.py` [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. City resolution serves as a prerequisite for all downstream community operations: an unextracted or ambiguous city (`City="Other"`) prevents candidate records from routing to chapter registries, local CRMs, or Google Drive workspace grants [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

The normalization workflow enforces a strict [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]:
1. **Scan (`clean.py scan`)**: A read-only analysis phase detecting malformed LinkedIn URLs, inconsistent casing, duplicate emails, and unmapped locations. It produces structured diff proposals (`scan --json`) without writing [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
2. **Approval Gate**: Proposed changes must be explicitly reviewed by an operator before applying changes [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
3. **Apply (`clean.py apply`)**: Consumes verified diff payloads stored in isolated temporary directories (`mktemp -d`), recording each modification in an immutable `Autofixes` audit column on the source `Form Responses` sheet [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

## Immutable State Backups
Before executing destructive or schema-altering edits, `backup.py` generates timestamped snapshots formatted as `<dest>/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>` [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Backups are write-only and immutable; existing snapshots are never overwritten, ensuring a complete roll-back history for critical operational datasets including the central Community Intake Ops sheet and chapter CRMs [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].

## Design System Conformance Sweep
Estate presentation files are audited and conformed via `restyle_design_system.py` against rules in `ooxml_style.py` aligned with [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. The sweep distinguishes between template assets and active organizer event decks:
- **Scope Restriction**: The sweep audits only registered template filenames and chapter `<City> CRM.xlsx` workbooks, skipping personalized drafts or dated event materials [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **SpreadsheetML Boundary**: Workbooks have only their styling layers (`xl/styles.xml` and theme palettes) updated; data cells in `xl/worksheets/` and `xl/sharedStrings.xml` remain untouched [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Pristine Archival**: Prior to applying writes, un-styled files are archived to timestamped directories (`backups/restyle-<UTC>/`), maintaining the earliest pristine copy against successive runs [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# Security and Boundary Controls
Operational execution adheres to strict isolation and containment policies [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]:
- **Tooling Constraints**: All Google Drive interactions are restricted to the authenticated `gws` CLI driven by Python, interacting directly with native Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Headless desktop office suites (such as LibreOffice, `soffice`, or `unoconv`) are strictly prohibited to prevent local font substitution and OOXML degradation [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].
- **Untrusted Input Handling**: Intake form entries and spreadsheet cells are treated as untrusted text. Embedded instructions or prompt injection attempts within intake answers are structurally prevented from altering membership status, chapter assignments, or authorization privileges [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
- **Human Approval Gate**: Decisions regarding chapter admission, access grants, and external communications (such as event announcements conforming to the [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md)) mandate explicit human review under a [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation suite and grading harness benchmarking skill triggering, prompt comprehension, and operational guardrails for community event agent skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical benchmarking harness within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) repository designed to test tool selection, invocation fidelity, and parameter safety across community management agent skills [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad][^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04]. The suite verifies that agent runners correctly bind natural language user requests to underlying skills—such as [community event operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)—without requiring rigid technical phrasing [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].

# Architecture and Grading Methodology
The harness evaluates agent behavior across operational tasks ranging from environment configuration checks to complex data migrations and event lifecycle administration [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad][^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

## Tool Invocation and Trigger Evaluation
Evaluations use targeted test cases and automated assertion graders to verify proper activation of skills formatted according to the [Agent Skills standard](../standards/agent-skills.md) [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad]. For instance, setup verification grading (`evals/check-setup/graders/skill_fires.md`) benchmarks whether the agent accurately triggers `aaif-check-setup` when presented with natural, colloquial queries such as "is it all working" [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad]:
- **Input Matching**: Evaluates structured agent output against regular expressions detecting target skill invocations (e.g., matching `"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?aaif-check-setup"`) [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].
- **Non-Technical Trigger Robustness**: Enforces that the skill triggers reliably on non-expert phrasing without requiring explicit keywords such as "setup" or "check" [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].

## Operational Safety and Protocol Conformance
Beyond skill triggering, the evaluation framework assesses adherence to critical operational boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04]:
- **Proposal Separation**: Verifies that agents do not trigger mutative write operations during diagnostic or scanning prompts [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].
- **Environment Verification**: Benchmarks proper detection of required system dependencies, including authenticated `gws` Google Workspace CLI access and Python runtimes before execution [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad][^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

# Lifecycle History
Developed within the `aaif/community-events` repository, the evaluation suite serves as an automated regression test gate within Foundation CI workflows, standardizing skill routing quality across compatible agent harnesses like [Goose](../resources/goose.md) [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad][^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Portability standards for packaging multi-client agent plugins, managing credential fallback hierarchies, and enforcing headless script execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent plugin portability guidelines define standard manifest layouts, credential resolution flows, and runtime constraints required to execute agent plugins interchangeably across coding agents such as Claude Code, Goose, Codex, and Cursor [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]. By decoupling procedural instructions from environment-specific wrappers, agent plugins maintain consistent execution behavior across headless and desktop interactive harnesses.

Portable plugins adhere to standardized directory layouts that separate the shared procedural spine from runtime wrappers, and they govern secret access without prompting the user in interactive subshells [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Client Manifest Structure
To support multiple agent environments within a single repository, plugins deploy parallel manifest declarations [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:
- **Shared Manifest**: A root `plugin.json` serves as the primary manifest for Codex, Cursor, and generic agent environments.
- **Claude Code Compatibility**: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` are colocated to support discovery in Claude marketplaces.
- **Skill Tree**: Modular capabilities reside under `skills/<skill-name>/` at the repository root, adhering to the standard file layout governed by [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md).

## Non-Interactive Credential Resolution
Agent execution shells typically lack interactive terminal access (TTY) to answer shell prompts [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]. Secret resolution follows a deterministic, non-interactive priority order:
1. Process environment variables (`os.environ`).
2. Local repository configuration files (`.env`).
3. Operating system credential stores (such as macOS Keychain Access via `aaif_events.credentials`).

Keychain lookups are cached per process execution to avoid repeated permission dialogs. Operational diagnostics must guide operators through graphic management tools (e.g., Keychain Access) rather than CLI commands that trigger hanging stdin prompts [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

## Tooling and Document Manipulation Constraints
Portable skills operate strictly via scripted CLIs and native runtime libraries, forbidding tools that alter underlying document structures or require graphical display servers [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]:
- **CLI and Python Integration**: Cloud-backed operations use dedicated CLIs (such as `gws` for Google Workspace) invoked through Python subroutines.
- **Office and Document Formats**: Agents must interact directly with native cloud APIs or perform low-level OOXML surgery on `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` zip structures.
- **Prohibition of Desktop Converters**: Tools such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are prohibited due to font substitution artifacts and loss of unsupported OOXML features [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].
- **Read-Only Verification**: System readiness is verified through isolated, read-only diagnostic checks (e.g., `check_setup.py`) that evaluate tool availability without mutating state [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

# Lifecycle History
The portability rules were formalized in the AAIF Community Events toolkit (`aaif-events`) during unification across Goose and Claude Desktop runtimes [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skills Specification
proposed_concept.description: Open file-based packaging format and progressive disclosure standard for extending AI agents with procedural skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Skills specification defines a file-based packaging format and progressive disclosure architecture for extending autonomous agents with structured, reusable procedural skills [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]. It ensures that agents retrieve concise operational instructions without overwhelming context windows or diluting procedural attention.

Skills are organized into modular directories containing a primary instruction file (`SKILL.md`), optional supplementary references, and automated evaluation harnesses [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

# Architecture / Specification

## Directory Layout
A skill conforms to the standard folder structure [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:
```
skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md            # Primary procedural spine
├── WORKFLOW.md         # Extended multi-phase procedure (optional)
├── scripts/            # Executable helper scripts and unit tests
└── references/         # Deep contextual documentation loaded on demand
```

## Frontmatter Metadata
Each `SKILL.md` must begin with YAML frontmatter declaring identity, runtime prerequisites, and trigger descriptions [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:
- `name`: Unique identifier matching the skill folder name.
- `description`: Single-line statement detailing both capability and trigger conditions ("Use when asked to...") to facilitate autonomous tool selection.
- `compatibility`: Explicit declaration of required CLI binaries, language runtimes, network access, or credentials.
- `metadata`: Client-specific invocation hints, such as argument placeholders.

## Structural and Sizing Rules
To maintain agent attention during task execution, `SKILL.md` documents adhere to strict constraints [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:
1. **Size Ceilings**: The primary `SKILL.md` must remain under 500 lines and approximately 5,000 tokens. Extended procedures must be relocated to `references/` or `WORKFLOW.md`.
2. **Explicit Progressive Disclosure**: Reference documents in `references/` must begin with an explicit trigger phrase ("Load this when..."), paired with a routing table at the end of `SKILL.md`. Vague directives like "see references for details" are prohibited.
3. **Checklist Formatting**: Multi-phase actions must be formatted as markdown checklists (`- [ ] **Step** — command, then rationale`) rather than dense prose.
4. **Focused Gotchas**: Troubleshooting guidance must be limited to non-obvious failure modes ("gotchas") that agents commonly misunderstand, avoiding explanations of standard programming idioms.

# Lifecycle History
The 500-line and 5,000-token threshold was adopted as an enforceable ceiling within the AAIF community events repository following token-bloat remediation where oversized procedural documents degraded agent routing accuracy [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skills
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skills managing AAIF chapter and online series lifecycles, intake triage, presentation drafting, and public-copy privacy controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite (`aaif-events`) automates administrative, operational, and marketing workflows for Agentic AI Foundation chapters and online series [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]. The toolkit operates across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop harnesses to support non-technical chapter leads in intake synchronization, Google Workspace provisioning, and collateral generation [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

The skills strictly enforce data privacy through the public-copy rule, preventing private attendee contact information from leaking into marketing copy or agent interaction transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

# Architecture / Specification

## Modular Skill Capabilities
The operational toolkit contains specialized skills conforming to [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:
- **Setup Diagnostics (`aaif-check-setup`)**: A read-only verification utility evaluating Python dependencies, `gws` Google Workspace CLI authentication, Google Sheets permissions, Slack tokens, Luma API keys, and Chrome PDF engines without altering system state [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Online Series Provisioning (`aaif-create-online-series`)**: Clones the `TemplateSeries` Google Drive directory into the top-level `Online/` workspace, rebranding document templates, attendee CRMs, and slide assets for recurring virtual groups (reading groups, paper clubs) while configuring no-venue runbooks [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].
- **Announcement Generation (`aaif-announcement-post`)**: Extracts event metadata from tracking documents to generate scannable, builder-focused LinkedIn announcement copy adhering to brand tone, hashtag limits, and mandatory Linux Foundation Code of Conduct links [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Slide Deck Assembly (`aaif-dayof-slides`)**: Translates event tracker entries into concise speaker and agenda slides for the standard AAIF "Day of Event" presentation template, preserving fixed brand lockups and partner credit placement [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

## The Public-Copy Privacy Rule
To protect community member data, operational skills enforce a zero-leakage public-copy policy across all generated drafts and agent reasoning traces [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]:
- **PII Withholding**: Intake contact information (email addresses, phone numbers, door access codes, private attendee identities) is withheld during data extraction and must never appear in generated text.
- **Transcript Protection**: Agents are prohibited from echoing omitted values in conversation transcripts (e.g., agents must state "I left out the speaker's email" rather than citing the actual email address), preventing unintended transcript exposure during sharing.
- **Descriptive Substitution**: Where logistical details cannot be published directly, skills substitute functional descriptions (e.g., "venue sends door access to RSVPs") [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

## Operating Constraints
Document operations are conducted exclusively through `gws` and native Python libraries. Headless conversions via desktop suites like LibreOffice are prohibited to prevent template degradation [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]. Credentials fall back from environment variables to `.env` files and the macOS keychain to maintain unattended CLI execution [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

# Lifecycle History
The toolkit was refactored into a single multi-client agent plugin (`aaif-events`) compliant with Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code standards, moving procedural procedures under 500-line ceilings [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].
