proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skills
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skills and deterministic CLI tooling automating AAIF chapter event scheduling, Luma publishing, LinkedIn carousels, and Slack workspace audits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skills provide an automated, agent-executable operational toolkit for managing Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chapters, online series, attendee data, and community communications [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. Implemented as portable [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md), the toolkit couples LLM-driven drafting and validation with deterministic Python and Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) execution [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].

The operations suite standardizes workflows across event scheduling, collateral generation, Luma publishing, and community Slack workspace auditing, enforcing strict data boundaries and PII sanitization to prevent accidental exposure in public repositories [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Architecture / Specification
The toolkit is structured around several modular skills and shared operational constraints:

### Event Scheduling and Publication (`aaif-create-event`)
The `aaif-create-event` skill orchestrates event additions to chapter or series trackers [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]:
- **Tracker Synchronization**: Clones the example event section within `Event Tracker.docx` stored on Google Drive via the `gws` CLI, computing all phase task deadlines backward from the scheduled event date [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].
- **Template Differentiation**: Enforces distinct schemas for in-person chapters (`VENUE`, `LOCATION / CITY`) versus online series (`PLATFORM`, `STREAM / JOIN LINK`), aborting execution if conflicting flags are supplied [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].
- **Live Publishing Gate**: Interacts with the Luma Calendar API using per-calendar credentials; requires an explicit [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) before publishing a live event page [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].

### Content and Copy Generation (`aaif-carousel-copy`)
The `aaif-carousel-copy` skill generates six-slide LinkedIn carousel copy adhering to AAIF brand standards [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]:
- **Copy Structure**: Constrains slide headlines to a maximum of seven words with one short supporting line; slide 1 serves as the hook and slide 6 provides the call to action [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Editorial Voice**: Enforces practitioner-focused messaging ("share the practice, never sell the product") [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Public-Copy PII Rule**: Enforces an explicit policy prohibiting private organizer and attendee data (emails, phone numbers, door access codes, non-public intake names) in generated copy and agent conversation transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Document Rendering Pipeline**: Converts `.pptx` templates via Google Slides API to PDF/PNG for high-fidelity export, explicitly prohibiting desktop office suites (such as LibreOffice / `soffice`) to prevent font corruption and dropped OOXML components [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].

### Slack Workspace Auditing (`aaif-audit-slack`)
Serving as Phase 8 of the estate synchronization pipeline, `aaif-audit-slack` conducts read-only operational checks across the community Slack workspace [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]:
- **Tri-Engine Reporting**: Deploys three distinct audit engines covering organizers (`audit_organizers.py`), topical discussion channels (`audit_topics.py`), and member visibility (`audit_members.py`), backed by an underlying activity measurement engine (`audit_activity.py`) [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Unified Summary Deliverable**: Assembles findings into a single HTML report (`summarize_audits.py`) synthesizing chapter channel coverage, organizer roster alignment, quiet topics, and prioritized recommendations [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].
- **Cache Isolation and Security**: Caches raw API pulls with workspace metadata tags, restricting permissions to `0600` inside `0700` directories and aborting runs if cache or output paths risk accidental staging under `git add -A` [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].
- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Explicitly classifies Slack user profiles, channel descriptions, and intake spreadsheet cells as untrusted data that cannot execute status modifications, administrative grants, or automated recommendations [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Lifecycle History
The Community Event Operations toolkit evolved as part of the `aaif/community-events` repository to standardize operations across global AAIF chapters and online series, moving administrative actions into deterministic, auditable scripts while leveraging agent skills for triage and authoring [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Engineering guidelines for packaging portable multi-client agent plugins across Goose, Claude, and Codex with secure credential fallbacks and decoupled data persistence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines establish architectural standards and runtime conventions for packaging multi-client agent plugins and [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) across diverse agent harnesses, including [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

To enable cross-platform operation without harness lock-in, plugins decouple skill authoring from execution hosts, ensuring consistent relative resolution, multi-tier credential discovery, and data isolation [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Manifest and Packaging Hierarchy
Portable plugins separate cross-client discovery from host-specific manifests [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]:
- **Root Manifest**: Defines the cross-client plugin specification in `plugin.json` at the root of the repository [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Host-Specific Overlays**: Encapsulates client-specific compatibility manifests under dedicated configuration directories (e.g., `.claude-plugin/`) without altering standard skill execution layouts [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

### Relative Pathing and the `<skill-root>` Anchor
Because installed plugins vary between git checkouts (such as in Goose) and isolated directory installations without repository metadata (such as in Claude Desktop), scripts must never assume execution from the repository root [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]:
- **Dynamic Anchoring**: All skill instruction files (`SKILL.md`) reference auxiliary scripts and assets using the `<skill-root>` placeholder resolved at runtime [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Linting and Enforcement**: Static portability checkers validate that paths do not hardcode relative traversal (such as `skills/<name>/...`), ensuring skills execute identically when loaded in standalone installations [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

### Multi-Tier Credential Fallback Hierarchy
Headless assistant applications and sandboxed agent plugins often lack inherited shell environment variables [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Tooling must implement a deterministic, non-interactive credential fallback sequence [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]:
1. **Process Environment**: Checks `os.environ` for direct environment variables (e.g., CI/CD or terminal shells).
2. **Local Dotenv**: Inspects `.env` located at the root of the local development checkout.
3. **OS Keychain / Secret Store**: Queries native system secret storage (such as macOS Keychain via `security find-generic-password` under a dedicated account identifier) [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
4. **Out-of-Band Setup Verification**: Diagnostic skills (such as `aaif-check-setup`) verify authentication status and instruct users on configuring keychains out-of-band, preventing sensitive credentials from leaking into agent conversational transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

### Data Persistence and Update Isolation
Agent plugin installations create distinct ephemeral directories per release version, which risk stranding state or backups during updates [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]:
- **Host Data Directories**: Persistent state, audit caches, and backups must target persistent system data locations (`~/Library/Application Support/AAIF` on macOS or `$XDG_DATA_HOME` on Linux) rather than the transient plugin install folder or the user's working directory [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Environment Overrides**: Runtime configuration allows an explicit absolute override via environment variables (such as `AAIF_DATA_DIR`), ignoring unsafe relative paths [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Repository Cleanliness and PII Isolation**: Tooling verifies that audit outputs and scratch directories are immune to accidental commits (`git add -A`) and enforces filesystem permissions (`0600`/`0700`) on sensitive cached artifacts [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Lifecycle History
Formulated through the deployment of the AAIF Community Events operations toolkit ([`skills/community-event-operations`](../skills/community-event-operations.md)), these portability standards were codified to support multi-client operations across Goose and Claude environments [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skills
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skills and deterministic CLI tooling automating AAIF chapter provisioning, event lifecycle reminders, community recaps, and local state backups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill suite provides automated and deterministic workflows for managing Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) regional chapters, event logistics, and community synchronization across Google Drive, Slack, Luma, and local agent runtimes [^evt-community-events-pr-60]. Packaged as portable agent skills under the [Agent Skills standard](../standards/agent-skills.md), these tools enable non-technical operators to execute operational tasks from environments such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or Claude Desktop without requiring direct command-line access or shell configurations [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

The suite automates repetitive chapter administration while establishing strict security boundaries against prompt injection, data leakage, and document corruption through hardened execution rules [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708], [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapter Provisioning (`aaif-create-chapter`)
Chapter provisioning automates the creation of regional community assets by cloning a canonical `TemplateCity` Google Drive directory and executing in-place token replacement across Office and Google Workspace files [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]:
- **Document Rebranding**: Case-matched replacement of city identifiers, abbreviations, and Luma calendar slugs across tracking spreadsheets, presentation decks, and event templates [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Map Geocoding**: Automatically determines geospatial coordinates via Nominatim to dynamically position the visual chapter marker pin on network presentation slides [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Tooling Constraints**: Mandates Drive manipulation through the `gws` CLI and Python APIs; explicitly prohibits desktop conversion suites such as LibreOffice or `soffice` to prevent font substitution and OOXML degradation [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

## Event Logistics & Reminders (`aaif-attendee-reminder`)
The attendee reminder workflow generates logistical notices for registered event attendees ~1 week out and the morning of each scheduled event [^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e]:
- **Tracker Extraction**: Queries chapter event trackers via `fetch_tracker.py` using title substrings or temporal offsets (`next`/`latest`) [^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].
- **Governance Anchors**: Automatically appends the required Linux Foundation Code of Conduct ([policies/code-of-conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md)) and Privacy Policy links to attendee communications [^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].

## Multi-Audience Recaps (`aaif-community-pulse`)
The biweekly recap engine aggregates recent community activity from Slack, Google Sheets, and Luma into three distinct targeted drafts stored in a local `.pulse-cache/` workspace [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a], [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51]:
1. **Organizer Updates**: Action-oriented summaries delivered to internal `#local-champs` channels [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
2. **Member Recaps**: Broad milestone overviews for `#general` community channels [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
3. **Public Social Copy**: External highlights formatted for LinkedIn and X syndication [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

Drafts are written exclusively to local disk files, leaving external posting actions to explicit human execution [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

## State Snapshots & Backups (`aaif-backup`)
Provides versioned, immutable snapshots of operational spreadsheets and templates prior to destructive modifications [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]:
- Files are stored chronologically at `backups/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>` within the persistent application support path [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].
- Preserves sheet formulas and conditional styling by copying values back manually upon restoration rather than overwriting core files [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

## Security & Isolation Controls
- **Public Copy Rule**: Forbids embedding non-public contact details (such as personal emails, phone numbers, and physical access codes) in model generations or conversational transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a], [^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].
- **Untrusted Input Boundary**: Enforces defensive boundaries treating Slack messages, sheet cells, and web text strictly as untrusted data rather than runtime instructions [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a], [^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
- **Runtime Portability**: Conforms to [guidelines/agent-plugin-portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md) by referencing scripts relative to `<skill-root>` and writing volatile state outside the working directory [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

mutations.rationale: Update plugin portability guidelines to document runtime isolation, persistent datadir discovery, hierarchical secret resolution, and relative path conventions established in PR#60.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Engineering standards for packaging multi-client agent plugins and skills across repository checkouts, Goose CLI, and Claude Desktop runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent plugin portability guidelines define runtime architectures, directory isolation policies, and credential lookup protocols required to run agent skills across multiple client environments [^evt-community-events-pr-60]. While early agent skill toolkits assumed execution within a local git repository checkout possessing a configured shell and ambient environment variables, modern production plugins must execute interchangeably within headful desktop applications (such as Claude Desktop), CLI runtimes like [Goose](../resources/goose.md), and git-less cache directories [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

These guidelines establish uniform design principles for managing script path resolution, persistent application data, credential cascades, and self-diagnostic readiness checks [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification

## 1. Relative Script & Asset Resolution
Portable skills must never rely on process working directories (`cwd`), global `PYTHONPATH` modifications, or repository-root relative paths (`python3 skills/...`) [^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
- Skill instructions and manifests must define paths relative to `<skill-root>`, dynamically resolving the parent directory of the active skill definition (`SKILL.md`) [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708], [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- Automated linter checks (such as `check_skill_portability.py`) must validate skill instruction files to prevent hardcoded repository paths [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## 2. Dynamic Data Directory Resolution (`datadir`)
Agent plugins must decouple internal transient files, output artifacts, and cache directories from the host workspace [^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
- In developer git checkouts, outputs may default to the repository root [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- In installed plugin environments (such as `.git`-less copies in application plugin caches), outputs and caches must resolve to standard OS application support paths (e.g., `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF/` on macOS) rather than the active workspace directory [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7], [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- Relative user overrides for data directories must be rejected or normalized to protect host filesystem integrity [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## 3. Hierarchical Credential Cascades
Installed agent tools often run without user shell profiles or pre-loaded environment variables. Credential resolution must implement a defined fallback cascade [^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
1. **Environment Variables**: Explicit process environment variables.
2. **Local Repository Config**: `.env` files located at the repository root (bypassed if running from an external plugin install).
3. **OS Credential Stores**: Platform keychains (such as macOS Keychain via `security`), cached per execution session to minimize repeated auth prompts.

Failure modes must produce actionable error diagnostics pointing directly to setup remediation tools rather than printing generic authentication tracebacks [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## 4. Git-Independent Execution
Plugins must operate seamlessly in environments where the `.git` directory has been stripped by plugin managers (e.g., Claude Desktop plugin caches) [^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
- Synchronization and deployment utilities must not call out to `git` binaries or assume branch tracking state [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- Gitignore safety guards must dynamically evaluate whether the active directory resides inside a valid git worktree prior to issuing VCS queries [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## 5. Self-Diagnostic Readiness Checks
Plugins must supply a dedicated setup verification command (such as `aaif-check-setup`) [^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
- Evaluates API token presence, OS credential availability, CLI dependencies (`gws`), and network reachability without altering system state [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- Outputs plain-language diagnostics detailing specific missing permissions and the exact scoped sign-in command required for resolution [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

Related implementations are demonstrated in [skills/community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) and governed under the [Agent Skills standard](../standards/agent-skills.md).

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining the Sandbox, Active, and Concluded stages, annual renewal terms, voting rules, and reporting cadences for AAIF Working Groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Lifecycle Policy governs how Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Working Groups are proposed, chartered, operated, renewed, and concluded[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Designed to sustain an active portfolio with minimal administrative overhead, the policy draws governance mechanisms from CNCF Technical Advisory Groups, OpenSSF and Kubernetes working groups, W3C time-bound charters, and the Apache Attic[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. It operates alongside a mandatory monthly asynchronous progress reporting mechanism that provides health signals to the Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8].

Working group governance is administered under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and complements project intake managed through the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

# Architecture / Specification

## Lifecycle Stages
Working Groups navigate three formal lifecycle stages following proposal approval[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]:

1. **Sandbox**: Upon initial approval by the TC, a working group enters Sandbox for six weeks (extendable once by up to six weeks)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. The group meets and drafts its operational charter. Groups that fail to produce a viable charter transition directly to Concluded[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
2. **Active**: Chartered groups delivering against active objectives operate under 12-month charter periods and undergo annual renewal reviews by the TC[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
3. **Concluded**: Groups that achieve their deliverables or cease active operations move to an open-ended archive state preserving their public records, deliverables, and meeting history[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. A concluded group may be revived back into Sandbox through a formal revival proposal[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Participation and Leadership Entitlements
Working group responsibilities are structured according to member tiers[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]:
- **Participation**: Open to anyone across the broader community without membership restrictions[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Proposals and Revivals**: May be submitted by representatives from any AAIF member organization (Platinum, Gold, Silver, or Associate)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Non-members may partner with member sponsors[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Leadership**: Working group chairs and co-chairs must represent Platinum, Gold, or Silver member organizations, with leadership distributed across at least two distinct organizations[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Contested Elections**: Voting in contested chair elections is restricted to participants affiliated with Platinum, Gold, or Silver member organizations[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Technical Committee Decisions and Voting
TC oversight decisions are made primarily by asynchronous lazy consensus on GitHub issues or pull requests over a 7-day objection window[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Any objection forces a formal roll-call vote decided by simple majority[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Three actions strictly require recorded votes[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]:
- Approving a new Working Group (subject to subsequent Governing Board confirmation)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- Retiring a Working Group to Concluded status without the consent of its chairs[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- Removing a chair, requiring a two-thirds supermajority of all TC members[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Monthly Progress Reporting
Working Groups submit a monthly report formatted as `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` via pull request to their respective repositories by the last business day of each month[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8]. Pull requests carry the `monthly-report` label and PR title `[Report] <YYYY-MM>`[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8]. The TC reviews asynchronously within a 7-calendar-day window[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8]. Missing two consecutive monthly reports triggers a mandatory live escalation check-in during the next TC sync[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-01**: Working Group Monthly Reporting framework entered into effect[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8].
- **2026-10-02**: Working Group Lifecycle Policy Revision 2 adopted as final by the Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Intake criteria, required proposal sections, cross-organization sponsor rules, and review workflows for proposing new AAIF Working Groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the structural criteria, documentation standards, and evaluation path required to propose a new Working Group (WG) to the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Proposing a WG requires demonstrating that the scope represents a durable, long-lived domain rather than a temporary or tightly bounded task that could operate as a workstream within an existing group[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

Working group intake is administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in accordance with the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Workstream Evaluation
Before submitting a new working group proposal, initiators must verify whether the targeted technical objectives fit within existing groups[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. AAIF reserves new working groups for broad, persistent domains; specialized tools, single specifications, or time-boxed deliverables should instead be structured as workstreams hosted within an active WG[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Proposal Prerequisites
Proposals are formally submitted through the issue template in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Every proposal must supply five mandatory components[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]:
1. **Problem Statement**: Explicitly articulates the agentic AI gap and demonstrates why neither existing AAIF working groups nor external bodies address the problem[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
2. **Scope and First Deliverables**: Boundaries specifying what the working group will and will not cover, along with concrete deliverables targeted for its initial 12-month charter[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
3. **Overlap and External Coordination**: Mapping of adjacent AAIF efforts and external standards bodies (e.g., W3C, IETF, OpenSSF, CNCF, or OWASP) detailing proactive coordination strategies to prevent duplication[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
4. **Leadership**: Nominated chair and co-chair affiliated with two distinct member organizations (Platinum, Gold, or Silver)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
5. **Demonstrated Demand**: Explicit commitments from named contributors spanning at least three independent organizations[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Review and Admission Workflow
The intake workflow progresses through four procedural checkpoints[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]:
- **Completeness Verification**: AAIF staff screen submissions against formatting and eligibility criteria prior to technical evaluation[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Technical Committee Review**: The TC conducts an asynchronous review on the issue, targeting a decision within eight weeks of a complete filing[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Determinations**: The TC may approve (moving the WG to Sandbox), request revisions, decline with written rationale, or redirect the scope into an existing working group[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Governing Board Confirmation**: Approval by the TC is subject to formal confirmation by the AAIF Governing Board prior to Sandbox entry[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

# References
- Working Group Lifecycle Policy: [../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)
- Technical Committee: [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the AAIF managing project intake, working group lifecycles, cross-group consensus, and technical oversight.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. The committee provides technical stewardship across Foundation initiatives, evaluating project admissions, chartering and supervising working groups, harmonizing cross-boundary architectures, and resolving technical disputes[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

The TC operates in coordination with the AAIF Governing Board and enforces governance standards established in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

# Architecture / Specification

## Decision-Making and Voting Procedures
The TC conducts business primarily through asynchronous communication on public GitHub pull requests and issue trackers[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704][^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8]:
- **Lazy Consensus**: Routine decisions pass under lazy consensus if no TC member objects within seven calendar days of posting[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Contested Decisions**: An objection during lazy consensus triggers a formal vote, decided by a simple majority of all TC members[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
- **Mandatory Roll-Call Votes**: Three specific actions cannot pass via lazy consensus and require formal recorded votes[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]:
  1. Approving a new Working Group (subject to final Governing Board approval)[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
  2. Forcibly moving a Working Group to Concluded status when not requested by its chairs[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].
  3. Removing a Working Group chair, which requires a two-thirds supermajority vote across all TC members[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Working Group Oversight
The TC evaluates proposed working groups according to the [Working Group Submission Guidelines](../guidelines/working-group-submission-guidelines.md), targeting an eight-week evaluation cycle[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Approved groups undergo a Sandbox stage (six weeks, extendable once by up to six weeks) before active charter approval[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704]. Active charters run on 12-month renewal cycles[^evt-technical-committee-file-6f2428968391-033df704].

## Monthly Progress Review
Working Groups submit monthly progress reports via pull requests following the `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` specification[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8]. The TC evaluates submissions within a 7-day review window[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8]. While reviews are asynchronous by default, the TC schedules live synchronization meetings for substantive blockers, cross-WG dependencies, or when a group misses two consecutive monthly reporting cycles[^evt-technical-committee-file-86b96cfaa5c4-64c967b8].

# References

- Working Group Submission Guidelines: [../guidelines/working-group-submission-guidelines.md](../guidelines/working-group-submission-guidelines.md)
- Project Lifecycle Policy: [../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)
